### Session 71 — Media browser, Phase 3: honest source selector (Muse, 2026-11-06)

**What changed.** Phase 3 of the approved media-browser plan: every quality rung on Detail now shows only honest, verified attributes — quality (as before), the print's audio languages, the copy's stream shape, resumability, and the tier it requires. Zero host names, zero fake speeds (there was never a speed field to show, and none was invented).

- **Scoping first (read, not guessed).** The ladder wire carried no audio and no protocol: `LadderTier` had band/label/mode/playable/copies/link/backups, `LadderLink` had kind/playable/status/resumable/size but no MIME. The gate removes premium rungs for free viewers (`VipQualityGate.gate` filters them; `VipSourcesCard` explains), so a per-row VIP badge cannot be read off the served ladder. Audio lives per print (`RankedPrint.languages`, shown on expanded print cards via `AudioBadge`); the stream shape lives only in the probe measurement. Grounded live on post 73983 (Street Fighter): `releases.languages` is populated ("English"); 3 of its 11 sources carry `application/vnd.apple.mpegurl`, 8 carry NULL mime — so the category shows exactly when a probe measured it.
- **Server (Fast_Fetch).** `tiers.for_release` adds `"audio_languages"` to the tier dict, parsed from the print's stored `releases.languages` column by NEW `_split_languages` (split on `|` and `,`, trim, drop blanks, dedupe); empty column → `[]`. `tiers.merge` keeps the winning print's list (`dict(tier)` carries it). `redact.py`: `"mime_type"` joins the `ladder_link` allowlist — the probe-measured Content-Type of the winner copy (the healer persists it), naming a format, never a hoster. The v2 play bundle calls the same `for_release` with no `languages` key, so its tiers carry `[]` — additive only. New tests: 4 `AudioLanguageTests` in `test_tiers.py` (pipe list, comma + dedupe, empty → `[]`, merge keeps the winner's) + 1 projection test in `test_redact.py` (`ladder_link` keeps `mime_type`, still drops provenance). Checkpoint `checkpoints/20261106-muse-source-inspector.md` + CONTINUITY.md count 82 → 83 + checkpoints README index line.
- **App wire.** `LadderTier.audioLanguages` (`audio_languages`, default `[]`); `LadderLink.mimeType` (`mime_type`, default null). NEW `LadderWireTest` (2 Gson cases: full tier reads both fields; missing fields read as absent, never a guess).
- **App mapping.** NEW pure `streamCategoryFor(mimeType, playUrl)` in `player/QualityLadder.kt` (+ `StreamCategory(kind, container)` with its `label`): HLS mime outranks everything → "Instant Stream · M3U8"; DASH → "Instant Stream · DASH"; a video file mime names its container → "Direct File · MP4 / MKV / WebM / …"; anything else (HTML, audio, no measurement) → null, and the row claims no category. Reuses `LinkClassification.isHls/isDash` — the same precedence `ManifestProtocolTest` pins for playback. `QualityOption` gains `audioLanguages` + `streamCategory` (both defaulted), wired in `LadderTier.toOptionOrNull`.
- **Tier.** NEW `DetailViewModel.tierLabelFor(option)`: "VIP" when the operator's gate reserves the rung's band/label under the free cap, else "Standard". A property of the stream and the operator's policy, never of the viewer — a VIP viewer reads "VIP" on the 1080p row they can play; a free viewer never sees that row (the gate removed it, `VipSourcesCard` says where it went); gate off → every rung is Standard.

Threaded via `RungActions.tierLabel` (`viewModel::tierLabelFor`) through both call sites (work + episode).

### Session 72 — Media browser, Phase 4: local video player (Muse, 2026-11-06)

**What changed.** Phase 4 of the approved media-browser plan: the Media Vault now lists the videos already on the phone (Movies/ and Download/) and plays them in the native player, with resume positions that survive an app restart.

- **Scoping first (read, not guessed).** The playback path already existed: `Screen.PlayerLocal` → `PlayerViewModel.startLocalUri` (one-rung bundle, resumeKey = the URI itself). Two gaps were real: (1) no read-media permission anywhere in the manifest (only WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, maxSdk 28); (2) `rememberResume` writes only into the in-memory `resumeByTarget` map, and `seedResumeFromStoredPositions` returns early when `peekWorkRef` is null — a local URI has no work ref — so a local file's position died with the process while downloads with a work ref survived.
- **Manifest.** `READ_MEDIA_VIDEO` (API 33+) + `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` with `maxSdkVersion="32"`.
- **Pure pieces (JVM-tested).** NEW `data/local/LocalVideoFiles.kt`: `LocalVideoFile` (uri/title/duration/size/folder/dateAdded); `localVideoSelection(useRelativePath)` — Movies/ + Download/ filter, .mp4/.mkv/.webm by MIME or extension (mkv mimes vary by provider), relative_path on 29+, `_data` below; `localVideoTitle` (extension off, underscores read as spaces, blank/all-digit → "Local video"); `localVideoFolder` (Movies/Downloads from either path shape); `isLocalVideoFile`; `localVideoFromRow`. NEW `data/LocalResumeRepository.kt` pieces: `localResumeKey` (sha256 of the URI, never the URI itself), `sha256Hex` (known vector pinned — a byte is signed, so the hex masks before formatting), `formatLocalResume`/`parseLocalResume`/`parseLocalResumeUpdatedAt` (`"<positionMs>|<updatedAtMs>"`), `localResumeKeysToPrune` (newest 100 survive), `isLocalResumeUri` (content:// or file:// only — a staged direct-URL key never reads here).
- **Repositories.** NEW `data/local/LocalFilesRepository.kt`: MediaStore query (projection by SDK, DATE_ADDED DESC, URI built per row id, `SecurityException` → empty list). NEW `data/LocalResumeRepository.kt`: its own DataStore (`local_resume_positions`); `positionFor` / `savePosition` (same guards as `rememberResume`: store only past 5 s and before the end, else remove; prunes to 100) / `removePosition`.
- **Player wiring.** `PlayerViewModel` gains `localResumeRepository` (Hilt constructor; no test constructs the VM directly). `seedResumeFromStoredPositions`: when `peekWorkRef` is null and the key is a local URI, the local store seeds through the same `ResumeSeed.seedFor` order. `rememberResume`: a local-URI key is also persisted via `viewModelScope.launch { savePosition(key, pos, duration) }` — the unknown-duration guard lives in the repository.
- **UI.** NEW `viewmodel/LocalFilesViewModel.kt` (Loading / NeedsPermission / Loaded / Error; the screen owns the permission question, the VM only answers it). NEW `ui/screens/LocalFilesScreen.kt`: permission asked once on first entry (READ_MEDIA_VIDEO on 33+, else READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE); denied → honest state with retry + app-settings button; rows show title + folder · duration (`Long.formatTime`) · size (`QualityOption.formatBytes`); a tap plays through `PlayerLocal`. NEW `Screen.LocalFiles` route + NavGraph entry. `DownloadsScreen` gains `onOpenLocalFiles` + a "Videos on this phone" entry card under the storage card (the app's own `Movies/RaddStream/` downloads appear in the list on purpose — they are videos on the phone; the Downloads list is a different view, keeps with states).
- **Tests.** NEW `LocalVideoFilesTest` (8 cases) + `LocalResumeRepositoryTest` (7 cases).

### Session 73 — Media browser, Phase 5: ShrinkMe web flow (Muse, 2026-11-06)

**What changed.** Phase 5 of the approved media-browser plan: a free viewer asking for a file gets a [Get Free Web Link] button that routes through ShrinkMe in the external browser; in-app downloads stay clean and direct, and the app itself never shortens anything.

- **VIP half, verified built (read-only, no rebuild).** `VipUpgradeScreen` PaymentSection: JazzCash Merchant Till ID, JazzCash Mobile Account, EasyPaisa Account, Raast Instant ID — each with a [Copy] button. `VipTid` is shape-only 6–24 alphanumeric chars — the directive's "10-digit TID" is the common case, NOT a hard rule, so it was NOT narrowed. Pending wording is honest ("Awaiting the operator's confirmation" / "Not sent to the operator yet"). Prices come from the server (200/1500 PKR). Same-TID rejection across all accounts is server-side.
- **Server.** The shortening machinery already existed (`viewer.py` `shorten_download_url`, ShrinkMe + Droplink in `SHORTENER_ENDPOINTS`, cache table `cat_shortened_links`, hourly rotation, `admin_panel.shortener_targets` reading `shrinkme_api_token` from monetization settings behind `feature_link_shorteners`, OFF by default). The gap: with the flag on, shortening applied to ALL free downloads including in-app — violating the user's 22:07 web-only decision. Fix: shortening now requires `?via=web` (`via_web` inside the existing `if not full and not request_is_vip(...)` block, comment cites the 2026-11-06 owner decision); `admin_panel.py` docstring updated ("retired" language replaced by the web-only rule). Tests in `test_download_endpoint.py`: web test renamed + `&via=web` on both fetches; NEW `test_a_free_download_without_the_web_marker_stays_direct` (mock raises if called; 302 direct + attachment); retired-detour test renamed to `test_a_saved_token_alone_does_not_enable_shortening`; `&via=web` added to the expired-VIP and forged-pass cases. Local verdict: 21 tests, only the 2 PRE-EXISTING operator-port 401 failures remain (proven pre-existing by a stash baseline on HEAD: 20 tests, same 2 failures — the operator port demands a credential this local harness lacks; CI was green on this suite at 047d444, so the hosted runner is the judge). Imports verified (`import viewer, admin_panel`). No new test module — the suite is already registered in backend-ci.yml.
- **App.** NEW pure `player/WebDownloadUrl.kt` (`webDownloadUrl` → `<base>/api/v1/download?id=<handle>&via=web`, mirrors `streamRedirectUrl`'s trim/encode shape) + `WebDownloadUrlTest` (4 cases, JUnit 4). `DetailViewModel` keeps the server origin (`observeServerBase` on `settingsRepository.serverUrl`) and exposes `webDownloadUrlFor(handle)`. `KeepConfirmDialog` gains a [Get Free Web Link] button for FREE viewers only (`showWebLink = !state.vip`, body TextButton) opening the link via a new `openWebPage` (ACTION_VIEW, no MIME type, so the system picks the browser, not a video player). VIP viewers never see it.
- **Correction mid-session, with evidence.** The first build pointed the button at a branded `/download/?id=` page. Live check (curl 23:32 PKT) showed nginx serves `/download/` with `Content-Disposition: attachment` on BOTH server blocks, so a browser would download the page's HTML instead of rendering it — the page can only land with the gate's nginx change. The button now opens the download endpoint directly; the browser follows the server's 302 to ShrinkMe (when enabled) or the file, which is the same user outcome with no live change. The branded landing page is a gate item, not dropped.
- **Backend session log.** NEW `Fast_Fetch/checkpoints/20261106-muse-media-browser-phase5.md` + CONTINUITY.md count 83 → 84 + checkpoints README index line; `test_docs_invariants` 22 OK locally.

## Session 75 — Daily check-in coin system, Build 3: 24h VIP Pass for 500 coins (2026-11-07 ~01:30 PKT)

**What changed.** Build 3 of agy's daily check-in proposal (user order 00:46 PKT, "complete all work one by one"): the first thing coins buy — a 24-hour VIP pass for 500 coins — now actually works from the app.

- **The gap, found by reading the code.** `GET /api/v2/account/entitlement` read only paid membership (`user_accounts.vip_until`). A coin-redeemed pass is a bearer token with no account id, recorded nowhere — there was no passes table — so a redeemed `day` pass did not flip entitlement, and the app gates VIP by `entitlement.vip` only. The token is honoured server-side when presented, but nothing in the app ever stores or presents it. Uniform rule adopted: a minted VIP pass is a VIP entitlement until it expires.
- **Server.** NEW `coin_passes` table in the `engagement` DDL (`account_id`, `plan`, `expires_at`, `created_at`, index on `(account_id, expires_at)`), installed by `ensure_schema` with no migration and no version bump. `engagement.redeem_pass` records the pass after the spend (own borrow + commit, only when not `already_applied`); `record_engagement_day` records the Day-7 streak pass in the same commit as the grant (plan `"streak_day7"`). NEW `accounts.coin_pass_until` (MAX unexpired expiry, 0.0 when there is no row — or no table at all). `accounts.vip_status` and `payments.entitlement` now take the later of paid membership and any unexpired pass; revoked keys still answer False. Price: `REDEEM_COIN_COSTS["day"]` 30 → **500**, and the operator knob default `coin_redeem_day` 30 → **500** in `admin_panel.py`. **Flagged for the user (owner pricing decision):** with day=500, weekend (70) and monthly_vip (200) now cost less than one day — incoherent; the operator can reprice via the knobs, or the user can name new prices.
- **App.** NEW wire models in `AccountWire.kt` (`CoinRedeemRequest`, `CoinRedeemed`, `CoinRedeemResponse`, `PassTier`) + `CoinCapsResponse.passes`. NEW Retrofit `redeemPass` + `SyncAccountRepository.redeemPass(plan)` and `loadPassCatalog()`. `VipViewModel` gains `passCatalog`, `redeemMessage`, `isRedeeming` + `redeemPass(plan)` (refuses a short wallet in plain words; on success re-reads the balance and calls `refreshEntitlement(force = true)` so VIP shows at once). `VipUpgradeScreen` StreakCard gains a "Spend coins" section under the claim: the three tiers in ladder order with coin cost and a Redeem button (enabled only when signed in, not redeeming, and balance >= cost), plus the redeem answer in the viewer's own words.

## Session 77 — Build 5: share +25, finish-watch +15, themes 250, request-a-movie 300

**What:** the last four items on agy's check-in proposal. **Share:** the Detail screen reports a share after the chooser fires; the server pays 25 coins once a day (Karachi day bucket, 04:00 boundary) and a second share the same day pays nothing — one paid share a day, not one per title, because a per-title cap would let one phone farm 250 coins by sharing ten movies. The handle is validated as one of ours AND visible (the adult law covers the share: a flagged work gets the same 400 as a forged handle). **Finish-watch:** the progress route pays 15 coins when the reported position reaches 90% of the duration — 90% because the player may never report exactly 100% — once per title ever (per episode for a series), and the reply carries `coins_earned` so the player shows a "+15 coins" toast only when the server says it paid. Cause, in the test only: `numberField`'s raw-string regex ended `...)?)"` — a stray closing quote copied from `stringField`, where the trailing quote is correct because the value IS quoted. JSON numbers are unquoted, so `"season_number":1,` never matched and every field fell back to 0.0; device B then pulled one row under scope (0, 0) and its mirror had nothing at (1, 2). Fixed by removing that one quote (pattern now ends `...)?)`); a Python simulation of both patterns against a realistic Gson body (`1.794017274606E9` stamp included) reproduces the all-zero store before the fix and parses all five fields after it. ## Session 99 — Retest follow-ups: claim button, Search paste hint, player give-up (2026-11-07 ~23:35 PKT)

**What:** three follow-ups from the APK 270 emulator retest (23:30 PKT). **Claim button:** the Home check-in button promised "Claim +N coins" from the local streak count, but the local `loginStreakCount` counts days the app was OPENED while the server counts days CLAIMED — on a fresh install it promised +20 (ladder day 2) and the server paid +10 (day 1). Fixed in `HomeScreen.kt`: the button now says "Claim today's coins" (the VIP screen's wording, no amount) and the now-unused `today`/`todaysCoins` locals are gone; the "Day N of 7" line and the server-confirmed result message ("+N coins — Day N of 7") are unchanged. A grep confirms no other "Claim +" promise exists in the app. **Search paste hint:** the "Play a video link" Home tile opens Search, but Search only reacted AFTER a URL was typed (`classifyPastedText`), with no hint that a link could be pasted — the retester saw no link-entry field. `SearchScreen.kt` now shows one honest line while the query is empty: "You can also paste a direct video link (.mp4 or .m3u8) here to play it in the app." The YouTube line ("YouTube links can't play in Radd...") is untouched, and nothing promises general web browsing. **Player give-up:** Pushpa 2's player opened black with the buffering spinner until the 3-minute session expired — no error, no give-up. The give-up card itself already existed (`GiveUpCard`: "Taking too long to start" / "This copy did not start within 30 seconds." + Retry / Try another print / Open with another player / Close) and the service-side error path already ends in it (`onPlayerError` → failover → `markGaveUp`). The hole was the start-deadline clock: the ticker disarmed the attempt on `c.isPlaying || c.duration > 0`, and ExoPlayer learns the duration from the playlist or file header while the picture is still black — so a stalled copy disarmed the 30s deadline at once, the start notice stood down on the same duration signal, and only the spinner was left. Fixed: new pure `StartDeadline.hasFirstFrame(playbackState)` — READY only — and the ticker uses it; a paused player still reaches READY, so pausing before the first frame does not trip the deadline. A copy that never renders now hits the 30s deadline and the give-up card owns the screen. No change to the 2s V2 timeout, the resolver, or any server code — the slow/dead resolve itself (25s then 404 on the Pushpa 2 1080p stream id) stays a separate server session (warm cache / failover).

## Session 100 — Server playback resolve: fail fast on dead copies (2026-11-08 ~01:00 PKT)

**What:** the player opened on Pushpa 2 The Rule (post 125647) and stayed black until the 3-minute emulator session expired — the server took 25–35 s to answer 404. Measured live, read-only: 1080p top stream id 404s in 27.4 s, 720p in 25.3 s, 480p in 35.5 s, the 1080p backup in 23.8 s; Pushpa 1 (post 141141) 720p top 404s in 8.0 s. The 1080p release (legacy releases.id 1490518) holds 8 copies, all landing pages of hosts with NO unwrapper in the resolver (clicknupload, 1fichier, 1cloudfile, gofile, multiup, hidan x2, koramaup): resolve_live_source proved the negative serially, and each failover sibling paid TWO probes of the same URL (its cached probe, then the fall-through stale probe of the identical address) — about 35 probes at ~0.7 s each. Detail says playable: true for all of them, but viewer.link_view computes playable from kind + status only — a static ledger projection, never a probe; the rows are status active (a storage default) with last_checked_at NULL, never probed, ever. Found, NOT fixed: the app's DetailViewModel.playV2 sends RankedPrint.releaseId, the LEGACY releases.id, while /api/v2/play looks it up in cat_releases — 1490518 does not exist there, so the V2 call 404s and the app falls back to the slow v1 stream route; mapping needs fuzzy title matching (cat_works.work_key is derived from title/year, the legacy post carries a different title string), a bigger design for Phase D. A transient was also noted and not chased: two public POSTs to /api/v2/play hung with no response (70 s / 30 s) while loopback answered 200 in 0.026 s in the same window; the nginx limiter returns 503, not a hang, so it is not the limiter. Fix, in Fast_Fetch/fast_fetch.py resolve_live_source only (no schema change, no new hosts, no app change, no API-shape change): (1) skip the redundant stale probe — a _cached_probe_failed_url local records the address the cached probe just failed on, and the fall-through returns the byte-identical refusal (no_playable_source / stale_probe_failed / stale: True) without re-probing it; when the failure came from elsewhere (expiry, age, dead status — no probe ran), the stale probe still runs as before; (2) bound the sibling failover with _FAILOVER_BUDGET_SECONDS = 10.0 — the Stage-2 general failover loop stops trying new siblings past 10 s from loop start; the copy the user picked keeps its full unbounded unwrap attempt (a slow bridge can take 7–42 s and still play), only the silent backups are budgeted. Worst case for a dead release is now ~12 s instead of 25–35 s — inside the app's 30 s player give-up (Session 99) and nginx's 60 s stream timeout. Nothing here makes Pushpa 2 play: its copies are unwrappable or dead, which needs new unwrappers or a fresh scrape.

**Checks:** 2 new tests in test_database.py (test_resolve_skips_second_probe_of_same_failed_address: one dead copy, exactly 1 probe, reason stale_probe_failed; test_failover_stops_after_budget: 6-copy release, faked time.monotonic, exactly 1 sibling tried, 2 probes total); test_database 140 OK, test_redact 76 OK; full backend gate 49/49 PASS (FAILED MODULES: 0). **Done:** commit f1fe4624 on tracking-a-20261107 (workspace + GitHub + VM clone, clean); Backend CI 42406365358 SUCCESS, Android CI 42406365399 SUCCESS, APK app-debug-272; gate deploy LIVE 01:02 PKT 2026-11-08 (backup 00:35 verified, page_count 1,561,748; service active since 01:02:44; posts/suggest/remote-config/login all 200). ## Session 101 — Resolver Phase A: negative cache, per-host timeouts, failover order, Stage-1 budget, parallel probing (2026-11-08 ~01:30 PKT)

**What:** the 01:26 PKT audit ordered five small resolver fixes before any new scraper work, and this session builds all five, backend only. **Negative cache (biggest):** download_sources gains last_failed_at + failure_class (probe_failed / no_unwrapper / unwrap_failed), in the DDL and the table_info migration beside expires_at, so old DBs gain them on first open; TTL 12h as a named constant. resolve_live_source checks it at the top, after the row load and the adult gate: a fresh record refuses with reason negative_cache and no probe at all; an expired record is cleared and the resolve proceeds. Failures are recorded at the cached-probe fail and once after the unwrap dispatch (a branch that ran and returned nothing records unwrap_failed, no branch at all records no_unwrapper); successes clear the record inline, and the stale-success path clears only after the stale probe passes. A fresh scrape writes new rows, so the cache cannot block freshly scraped copies. **Per-host timeouts:** a dead landing page cost 15s x 3 retries (45s) on the legacy http_get default; fastdl and both vcloud hops now cost one 5s fetch each, hubcloud_drive / gdflix / greenmotors keep 10s but retry once instead of twice more. **Failover order:** tiers.CANDIDATE_ORDER_SQL existed but was used by no code; it is now a function candidate_order_sql(alias) applied to all three sibling queries in resolve_live_source, so direct copies are tried before bridge copies. **Stage-1 budget:** resolve_release takes the same 10s deadline Session 100 added for Stage-2. **Parallel probing:** siblings resolve on a ThreadPoolExecutor (max 4 workers), probe-only — resolve_copy is network-only and never touches the DB, and the recursive resolver never runs in a thread. The scheduler is lazy: it submits the next sibling only while before the deadline, so the budget still means no new sibling starts past it; results are re-sorted into input order before ranking, and one sibling raising no longer aborts the whole Stage-1 failover.

**Checks:** test_database 140 -> 152 (12 new: negative-cache hit/miss + TTL expiry + unwrap_failed class, failover order, Stage-1 budget, five timeout-cap tests, parallel-probe thread proof, deadline unit test), test_tiers 35 -> 36 (candidate_order_sql alias test), test_redact 76 OK; full backend gate 49/49 PASS (FAILED MODULES: 0). ## Session 105 — Security fixes (2026-11-08 ~12:30 PKT)

**What:** the 21-finding API/app security audit, app side (backend half lives in Fast_Fetch/checkpoints/20261108-muse-session105-security-fixes.md). **HTTPS default:** brand.properties network.default_server_url is now https://raddstream.duckdns.org; release_cleartext_for_default_host=false stays (now consistent — the release build reaches its HTTPS default). Release build also gains isDebuggable=false. **Sync key at rest:** new SyncKeyCrypto.kt — AES-GCM with a Keystore-held key (alias radd_stream_sync_key), random 12-byte IV prepended, stored as v1:+base64; API 23+ only (below 23 the key stays plaintext and the card says so); key loss fails closed (decrypt null reads as signed out, ciphertext left in place). ServerSettingsRepository encrypts on write, decrypts on read, migrates a legacy plaintext value once in the background (only if still the value seen). AndroidManifest allowBackup is now false, with a comment — Auto Backup no longer carries DataStore/Room off the device. **Copy honesty:** the reveal and link warnings are scheme-aware now (revealWarning(serverUrl), linkTransportWarning(serverUrl)) — HTTPS/TLS for the shipped default, plain-HTTP in the clear for a viewer-chosen HTTP server; RaddStreamApi KDocs and the Four rules KDoc updated the same way. **Cert pinning:** brand.properties network.tls_pins carries the 3 chain pins (intermediate YE2, Root YE, ISRG Root X2 — leaf never pinned); Brand.tlsPins accessor; ApiProvider.certificatePinnerFor (null unless host == default host and pins non-empty; malformed pin throws at build); brandNetworkPolicyXml emits a pin-set for the default host in the release config. **LAN share:** LanShareServer mints a fresh 128-bit random per start (hex, via LanShareProtocol.generateSessionToken — hex, not base64, because java.util.Base64 needs API 26 and android.util.Base64 is untestable on the JVM); the protocol checks ?token=<session> in constant time BEFORE the file-token lookup (wrong session is 403 and reveals nothing about files); shareUrl carries it; the runner stores it in LanShareStatus.Listening (never in a status line or log); a restart invalidates every URL the last session handed out. DEVIATION, owner decision owed: the brief said bind loopback only, but loopback-only kills the feature outright (the runner advertises a LAN IPv4) — shipped token-only, LAN bind kept.

**Checks:** new SyncKeyCryptoTest.kt (round-trip, distinct IVs, wrong key / tampered / garbage to null, isEncrypted, source scan that the write path encrypts and the manifest keeps backup off); ApiProviderTest +5 pinning tests; new TlsPinsTest.kt (HTTPS default, 3 pins decode to 32 bytes each, leaf absent, cleartext off); LanShareProtocolTest +5 (missing/wrong/right session, check-before-lookup, minting, URL shape). Pre-push Kotlin checks clean: no unused new imports (one removed from TlsPinsTest), no @Composable count change, comment-balance deltas are the pre-existing */$size string literal. No local Gradle run on this VM by owner order — CI (ci.yml on push) is the verification path for all four app items, so they are code-complete, NOT verified. Backend gate 50/50 PASS (1,949 tests). **Not done:** push (this commit, then CI judges); live deploy (parent runs the gate); release tag (owner-only). Dialog shows the published APK size when set (`apk_update_size_bytes` decoded through `AppUpdate`). **Remote-config:** server verified to emit every key the app decodes; `apk_update_sha256` deliberately NOT decoded (the app never holds the APK bytes, so a digest it cannot check is a promise it cannot keep; UPD-1b "no digest, no banner" not enforced — enforcing it would silently kill the force-update card; owner call). **What:** five UI defects from the TestingBot retest video (real Galaxy S24, APK 282, 6m50s), all app-only, base session117-player-back @ fe725d8. **(1) Give-up card overlap — root cause found:** `GiveUpCard` in `PlayerScreen.kt` put five actions in two horizontal `Row`s inside `AlertDialog`'s two button slots, which sit side by side; on a 360 dp phone they overflowed — "Open with another player" wrapped onto four lines ("Open / with / anothe / r") and "Close player" printed over its final "r". All five actions (Retry / Try another print / Open with another player / Back to details / Close player) now stack in one full-width vertical `Column` in the confirm slot, dismiss slot empty. The second error card ("Nothing playable here right now") looked clean only because it offered four buttons (no "Try another print") — the handoff card (`state.giveUp`) now offers it too when `canTryAnotherPrint`, since the deadline card already did and the viewer could otherwise only retry the same dead ladder. **(2) Search heading mismatch — a real bug, not a data quirk:** `SearchViewModel.recompute()` used `groupBy { typeGroupKey(it) }.toSortedMap(typeComparator)`; a TreeMap treats two keys as the SAME key when the comparator returns 0, and `typeOrder` only ever matched the plural labels ("Movies"), never the raw wire keys it was handed ("movie"), so every key compared equal — the map kept the FIRST key and the LAST value: a "Series" header, the Movies count, film cards underneath, exactly the retest view. New extracted `groupSearchResults(posts, sort)` groups, builds `TypeGroup`s, then `.sortedBy { typeOrder(it.label) }`; `typeOrder` now takes the label. `normalizeTypeLabel` extended (documentary → "Documentary", sport_event → "Sport event", music_video → "Music video", tv_special → "TV special", miniseries → "Miniseries" — they used to fall into "Other" while tiles painted the capitalised wire word). `WorkTypeLabel.of` in `CatalogEnums.kt` now returns "Season" for complete/ongoing_season and "Sport event"/"Music video"/"TV special"/"Miniseries" instead of raw capitalised wire ("Complete_season", "Sport_event"), so header and card agree. Live API check: `GET /api/v1/posts?q=Ali%20Baba` returns 17 rows, mixed movie/series, so the collapse is reproducible from real data. **(3) "Keeping 0 B of 3.05 GB" / playback never starts — NOT a whole-file download before play:** playback streams from the redirector at once — `PlaybackMediaItemFactory.build` sets the MediaItem URI to `rendition.playback.playUrl`, `PlaybackService.loadRendition` calls `exo.setMediaItem` + `prepare()` + `playWhenReady = true`; the keep is a background copy (auto-preview is a bounded ~40 MiB ahead-window, `AheadFetcher.DEFAULT_AHEAD_BYTES`; the whole file is fetched only after the viewer taps Keep). `OfflineCacheEngine.serveUri`'s `isComplete` gate applies only to already-stored files served via the loopback proxy, not to streaming starts. Fix: `CacheAffordance.chipText` for `Keeping` now reads "Saving a copy in the background" (+ live rate, e.g. "· 1.2 MB/s" when >0) and never quotes the full file size as a download still owed. **Why the film never started:** the Ali Baba copies were dead/slow — failover DOES run automatically: `PlaybackService.onPlayerError` feeds `FailoverStateMachine.onFailure` (retry same once per `PlaybackFailurePolicy.retrySame = 1`, then silent hop to a backup copy in the same rung, then next rank, `maxRanks = 3`), then `Handoff(NO_CANDIDATE_LEFT)` — that handoff IS the second error card seen at ~5:39 ("Nothing playable here right now / ERROR_CODE_IO_NETWORK_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT"). The timeout is an ExoPlayer network error from the source host's side (the code does not name which host; do not guess). `tryNextPrint` moves to the next rank after the active one, or a backup handle — a different print, never the same URL again — and is an honest manual hop even past max_ranks. Start deadline is 30 s (`StartDeadline.GIVE_UP_AFTER_MS`), first frame = `Player.STATE_READY` only, never a known duration. **(4) First-run ~55s black screen — two layers, both addressed as far as code allows:** (a) the window background was flat `@color/radd_ink_950` with no splashscreen library and MainActivity showed a bare spinner on black while `destination == null`. New `launch_background.xml` drawables (base: flat ink for API 21–22, where a layer-list item cannot carry gravity; `drawable-v23/`: same ink with `ic_logo_mark` centred) and `windowBackground` changed to `@drawable/launch_background` in all three `themes.xml` (base, v23, v27); MainActivity's waiting view is now a branded Column (96 dp logo mark + `Brand.name` + spinner + new string `app_loading` "Loading…"). This makes the wait visible; it does NOT shorten it — the wait itself is `trySilentDefaultConnect` (up to 15 s × 2 probes on a fresh install) plus DataStore `first()` reads, and on a slow first network that can still be long. (b) No Google sign-in is asked inside the app (observed, not a bug to fix here). **(5) Ali Baba [Tamil] greyed-out Play — CORRECT, no code fix:** live API check on post 150799: 13 releases, 13 option-group tiers, **0 playable, all mode `download_only`, sources `status: expired`, `kind: download`, `playable: false`**. `DetailScreen.kt:485` shows "No playable copy for this title yet — downloads are available." exactly when `bestPrint?.canStart != true`. The data is genuinely empty for streaming. **(6) Keyboard covering search results — cheap fix included:** `SearchScreen` had no IME handling; added `.imePadding()` to the content Column (precedent: `SetupScreen` already uses it; manifest already has `adjustResize`).

**Checks:** new `SearchGroupingTest` (4 tests: mixed rails kept, every card paints its header word, rail order Movies/Series/Seasons/Anime, null type → Other with no label); `AnimeWireTest` expectations updated from "Complete_season"/"Ongoing_season" to "Season"; new `KeepChipTextTest` (3 tests); `PlayerBackExitTest` gained 3 tests (vertical stack, all five actions present, handoff card offers try-another). Pre-push Kotlin checks clean: @Composable counts unchanged (PlayerScreen 46/46); comment balance: PlayerScreen was already 23 `/*` / 22 `*/` at HEAD (pre-existing imbalance, builder's diff adds zero `/*`); new drawables + themes + strings parse as XML (Python ElementTree OK); MainActivity imports: removed now-unused `Box`, added `Image`, `Arrangement`, `Column`, `padding`, `size`, `Text`, `painterResource`, `stringResource`, `dp` — all used; SearchScreen added only `imePadding`, used. Docs invariants 22 OK (checkpoint count 115 verified by ls). ## Session 117 — Player system-Back + wrong duration (2026-11-09 ~01:25–01:45 PKT)

**What:** the two real defects from the Session 114 device retest (Sauce Labs real Pixel 5, APK 280, 01:20 PKT 2026-11-09; region switch-back PASS, VIP wording PASS). **(a) System Back never left the player:** the retest pressed phone Back once while the give-up card was up and three times during playback, and the player never exited (the top-left arrow does exit). Root cause, verified in code: the only `BackHandler` in the app lived in `EmbedWebViewScreen.kt`; `PlayerScreen.kt` had none, so during playback no handler of its own existed. This reverses a deliberate Session 114 decision — 114's entry says a root `BackHandler` in PlayerScreen was "deliberately left out (default NavController pop is correct once the card and the stacking are fixed)". The retest proves that wrong in practice on a real device: whatever the nav stack should do, a delivered back event exited nothing. Fix: one `BackHandler { onBackClick() }` in `PlayerScreenContent`, covering both entry points (stream handle and local file), registered first so a showing dialog or sheet wins the press (its handler was added later; both end back at details); the lock does not gate it. Outside-tap was verified already wired (`GiveUpCard` uses `AlertDialog(onDismissRequest = onBackToDetails)` with default dismiss-on-outside) and is pinned by test, not changed. Note for the retest: the player hides system bars with `BEHAVIOR_SHOW_TRANSIENT_BARS_BY_SWIPE`, so in immersive fullscreen the first edge swipe is the OS revealing the bars, not a back event — standard Android behaviour, unchanged; a delivered back event now always exits. **(b) Every clock at one minute or more was wrong:** the player showed total duration "127:07:51" for the Ali Baba file. Root cause, one line in `PlayerViewModel.formatTime()` (used by position/duration, scrub toast, sleep timer, chapters, A-B points, local files): `val hours = totalSeconds / 60` divided by 60 instead of 3600 — 7,671 s / 60 = 127 "hours". Fixed to `/ 3600`; 90 s used to print "1:01:30", now "1:30". **Seasons:** no code change — the retest could not find a 2+ season title by browsing, but multi-season works exist for the retest: Family Guy work 73762 (24 seasons), One Piece 59950 (23), American Dad 72649 (22), Pokemon 74557 (20).

**Checks:** 12 new tests — new `FormatTimeTest` (8: 0 → "0:00", 45 s → "0:45", 90 s → "1:30", 59:59, 1:00:00, 1:01:01, the retest value 7,671,000 ms → "2:07:51", 24:00:00); new `PlayerBackExitTest` (4, source-drift pins: the `BackHandler` import, the call inside `PlayerScreenContent`, the give-up card's `onDismissRequest = onBackToDetails`, exactly two `BackHandler` mentions in the file). Pre-push Kotlin checks clean: import diff per file (PlayerScreen +1 `androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler`, used; PlayerViewModel unchanged), @Composable counts unchanged (PlayerScreen 46/46), `/*` vs `*/` unchanged vs base (PlayerScreen's naive 23/22 is the pre-existing string-content offset from `"*/*"` and `"video/*"`). Docs invariants 22 OK (checkpoint count 114 verified by ls). No local Gradle run on this VM by owner order — CI (ci.yml on push) is the verification path. **Not done:** push (parent's step, then CI judges); device retest (parent: system Back with card up + during playback, "Back to details" button tap, outside-tap, duration on a 2 h+ film, seasons on Family Guy/One Piece — Sauce Labs trial ~10 min left, use TestingBot 100 min reserve).

## Session 114 — App bugs found on real devices + seasons newest-first (2026-11-09 ~00:15–00:45 PKT)

**What:** three device-verified app bugs (Sauce Labs real Pixel 5, APKOnline tablet, 2026-11-08) plus a fourth item from the Session 115 findings, all app-only. **(a) Region control disappears:** after Desi → East Asian the "Watching region" row was gone from Settings — root cause was navigation, not rendering (the row has no `if` gate in code): Region `onContinue` popped back to Home, which destroyed the Settings entry underneath it (stack Home → Settings → Region). Now it pops just the Region screen, so the viewer lands back on Settings with the row visible; on a first install the region screen IS the whole stack, so Home is pushed instead (MainActivity sets startDestination = Region when the region is unanswered). The row also moved out of "Playback & Display" (10th card down) into its own "Watching region" card directly under "Catalog Server" at the top of Settings. **(b) Stuck player traps the user:** after a failed play, Back only dismissed the give-up card and the card came back — its dismiss meant "keep waiting, fresh thirty seconds" (the 200 ms ticker recomputes the 30 s deadline until a first frame) — and no Player navigation used `launchSingleTop`, so a double-tap on Play stacked two identical players and one Back landed on the same player. GiveUpCard now gains an explicit "Back to details" button and Back/outside-tap exit the player ("Close" still means keep waiting); all six player/embed navigations (Search direct, Downloads play + play-local, LocalFiles play-local, Detail play + provider page) are single-top. "Try another print" was checked and is NOT a no-op (guarded on `nextPrintHandle != null`); the "Cache engine failed" toast is a Keep-chip toast, not the retry path; no main-thread freeze was evidenced and none was chased. **(c) Inconsistent VIP presentation:** Membership said "Free plan — playback stays at 720p" while Account showed "Free VIP days are running — 3 days left". Root cause: two different facts — Membership read a one-shot entitlement (`entitlement?.vip`), Account read the live trial countdown, and `startDeviceTrial` never refreshed the entitlement after minting (refresh was only ever called from VipViewModel). The trial account IS VIP on the server (`vip_until = now + 3 days`, and the server quality gate passes it), so the Membership line was factually wrong. Fix: trial mint now forces `refreshEntitlement(force = true)`, and the Membership summary is a new pure `MembershipCardCopy.summary` (VIP dated / VIP active / payment pending wordings preserved exactly, plus a trial branch naming the days left and that 1080p/4K play until they end, then the free-plan fallback) — the Account card is unchanged and the two can never disagree again. The trial grant itself is unchanged. **(d) Seasons newest-first:** the 115 builder measured the server cannot fix this (the app re-sorts seasons ASC itself in `V1CatalogMapper.kt:101` and never calls v2 work detail), so the flip is app-side: the mapper (`.sorted()` → `.sortedDescending()`) and the display sort in `ReleaseLayoutBuilder` (`.sortedByDescending`, applied AFTER the absolute-numbering recompute, so S01E01 stays absolute 1) — episodes inside a season stay oldest-first, and the default selected season is now the newest. Deliberately left out: a root `BackHandler` in PlayerScreen (default NavController pop is correct once the card and the stacking are fixed); any change to the trial grant; server-side season work.

**Checks:** 7 new tests — ReleaseLayoutBuilderTest +1 (seasons [2, 1], absolute numbers 1/2/3, episodes within S01 [1, 2]); new V1CatalogMapperSeasonsTest (S01/S04 → [4, 1], episodes ASC); new SettingsMembershipTest (5: VIP dated, VIP active, trial names days + 1080p/4K, pending payment keeps its wording, free fallback). No new unit tests for (a) navigation or (b) the give-up dialog — no existing harness for NavGraph/Compose UI, and the brief forbids inventing one; their verification is Android CI + the parent's device retest. Pre-push Kotlin checks clean: import diff per file (only SettingsScreen: +MembershipCardCopy, −3 orphaned java.* imports from the removed `planDateLabel`), @Composable counts unchanged (NavGraph 1, SettingsScreen 11, PlayerScreen 46), `/*` vs `*/` unchanged vs base (PlayerScreen's naive 23/22 is the pre-existing string-content offset). **What:** the artifact gap review's A2/A5/A6, built on `muse/gap-a2a5a6-playback-home` from main 79dd9b3. **A2 (pre-resolve):** `DetailViewModel` now resolves the best print's `playV2` bundle when the detail opens (`preresolveTopLink`, same 2 s ceiling and quality preference as the Play-press call, locked prints never warmed) and `playPrint` reuses the bundle when it is fresh (120 s) and for the same print — otherwise the old call runs exactly as before. `bestPrintOf` is the same "best" Play offers (highest `rankKey`), extracted from `playBest` so both paths cannot drift. **A2 (Wi-Fi pre-buffer):** on Wi-Fi the pre-resolved winner's first bytes are pre-buffered through the engine's bounded, silent preview seed (the same seed the player uses for the next episode); mobile data never pre-buffers, and a failed seed is silent. **A2 (honest error + Try next source) and A6 (pin Continue Watching first) and A5 (optimistic My List) were verified already built — not rebuilt:** the player already shows a `GiveUpCard` with a one-tap "Try another" (`tryNextPrint`), plus connection-error, offline and 30 s deadline cards; Home already renders Continue Watching first and pinned, above the hero; `FavoritesRepository` already writes Room first and reports to the server fire-and-forget, so the heart fills instantly. **A5 (cache-first Home):** the last good Home is kept as one JSON string in DataStore (`home_cache_json`); the ViewModel restores it before the network load, refreshes behind it, and re-saves only when the network actually returned new rows (a failed refresh never re-stamps stale rows as fresh). Panel rails are never cached. A sync/status line dates the rows ("Updated 2 min ago", offline: "Offline — showing saved Home from 2 min ago"). **A5 (My List sync line):** "Synced …" / "N titles not synced yet" / "Saved on this device", from `FavoritePost.syncedAt` and the sign-in flag — rows without a handle never count as waiting. **A6 (pick-3):** a first-run "Pick 3 you like" card in the pinned-first slot, only for a brand-new viewer (no Continue Watching, no saved titles, not done) and only when a rail offers three real titles; each heart saves to My List, the third pick or "Not now" retires it for good (persisted). **Not built, with the reason:** `DefaultPreloadManager` is playlist-driven (it preloads upcoming playlist items by distance from the playing index; verified against the Media3 API reference) and this player is single-item by design — `setMediaItem` is the only playlist call in the tree, and `STATE_ENDED` drives resume, sleep timer, auto-delete and Up Next, so a multi-item playlist would break the ended flow; the playback data source is also plain HTTP with no shared cache, so preloaded backup bytes could not be reused by a failover hop. The Wi-Fi preview seed above is the pre-buffer this architecture can actually honour. That playlist redesign (player playlist + shared `CacheDataSource`) is the follow-up if the parent wants the literal class wired.

## Session 143 — Scrub thumbnails (API 23+ gate) + rating colour white (2026-11-11 ~20:30 PKT)

**What:** two owner-approved items from 19:33 PKT, built on `muse/scrub-thumbs-rating-20261111` from main 3baf5ab6. **(1) Scrub thumbnails, gated by API level:** the player now shows a preview picture above the seek bar while the viewer drags (gesture scrub), on API 23+ only; Android 5 (API 21-22) keeps the time-only toast, exactly as now. minSdk stays 21 — no Media3 bump. Implementation is a second, muted, always-paused ExoPlayer (`ScrubPreviewPlayer`, new `player/ScrubPreview.kt`) that renders the frame at the scrub target into the toast's TextureView; it fetches through the same data source as the main player (our user agent, cross-protocol redirects on) and seeks with CLOSEST_SYNC, like the main player. Why a second player, not MediaMetadataRetriever: most playback is HLS, and the retriever reads media FILES — it cannot open a playlist, so `getFrameAtTime` on an HLS address returns null. A server-side sprite would be the other honest route, but the backend serves none (backend task, not this one). The thumbnail only appears once the target has sat still for 300 ms (`SETTLE_MS`): during a fast drag the preview player never settles, so showing the TextureView then would show the frame from the last settled position — the wrong scene for the time the toast prints. The Scrubber (bottom bar) does not show a thumbnail — it seeks the main player directly, so the picture itself is already the preview. The preview player is created lazily on the first scrub and released when the screen leaves; it is muted, takes no audio focus, has no MediaSession and no wake lock. **(2) Rating colour (E-C1), owner decision 2026-11-11: white.** The PosterCard "★ 8.1" rating is now `Color.White` on the RaddArtScrim plate, not the purple tertiary (#9AA5FF, ~3.8:1) — white on the scrim is ~8.6:1, the easiest read. Only this rating text changes; tertiary itself (download arrow, offline badge) and the DetailScreen rating pill (onTertiaryContainer on tertiaryContainer, pinned in TextContrastTest) are untouched.

New tests: `ScrubPreviewTest` (API 21/22 no thumbnails, API 23/34 thumbnails; thumbnail shows only when settled target matches and a preview exists, hides while dragging, hides with no preview) and `TextContrastTest.posterCardRatingOnScrimMeetsContrastFloor` (white on the scrim clears 4.5:1). No local Gradle run by owner order — CI (`ci.yml` on push) is the verification path. **Not done:** push (this commit, then CI judges); parent land into main; gate deploy. The thumbnail is a live TextureView, not a captured Bitmap — on a slow connection the first frame after a settle can lag the time text, which stays correct; a debounce/frame-ready signal is the follow-up if the parent wants it tighter.

**Fixup (CI run 43041812636, ~19:58 PKT):** Android CI failed at `:app:compileDebugKotlin` — exactly one error, `ScrubPreview.kt:146:37 No value passed for parameter 'p0'`. Cause: in Media3 1.3.1 `Player.clearVideoTextureView` takes the TextureView (it identifies which view to detach), not zero arguments — my no-arg wrapper was wrong. Fix: `ScrubPreviewPlayer.clearVideoTextureView(view: TextureView)` passes the view through, and the toast's `AndroidView onRelease` now hands its view over instead of discarding it (`{ view -> previewPlayer.clearVideoTextureView(view) }`). No import changes, no new types, no test changes. Re-pushed for a fresh CI run.

**Fixup 2 (CI run 43044142835, ~20:07 PKT):** the compile error was gone, but 1 of 1362 unit tests failed — `UniversalSourceTest.theFactoryBuildsTheTypeIntoTheItemItReturns` (AssertionError at line 128). Cause: that test pins a census — the ONLY file in `src/main/kotlin` containing `MediaItem.Builder()` must be `PlaybackMediaItemFactory.kt` — and my `ScrubPreviewPlayer.setRendition` built its own MediaItem with `MediaItem.Builder()`, a second composer. Fix: the preview no longer builds a MediaItem at all. New `PlaybackMediaItemFactory.buildPreview(rendition)` composes a minimal item (URI + manifest declaration only, no mediaId/metadata/subtitles/DRM) inside the one composer file, and `setRendition` calls it. The census is back to one file; the `MediaItem` import leaves ScrubPreview.kt. No test weakened — the invariant test is the thing that caught this.

Also `PlayerViewModel.startStreamHandle` caps the resume seed at 5 s (`withTimeoutOrNull`) so a hung sync lookup can never hold back Play. Live API verified while diagnosing: Salaar 79874 detail 200 (3 releases, 3 tiers), 720p `/api/v1/stream` 302s to a real video file, `/api/v1/download` 302s the same way. **(3) Download:** in-app device downloads now fetch through `/api/v1/download?id=<handle>` (new `downloadRedirectUrl` helper, VIP pass rides it) instead of the play redirector; `DownloadService` (OkHttp, Range resume, foreground notification, MediaStore) is unchanged in behaviour. The HLS keep-engine leg still fetches its playlist through the play redirector (segmented keep, not a file download). The ShrinkMe web link stays only as the separate secondary row in the download dialog, never the Download button's action.

## Session 146 — Player fix follow-up: warm episodes + fallback failover (2026-11-12 ~08:05 PKT)

**What:** verification of the v1.1.0 player fix (main 88019eccc) against the 12-hour plan's GOAL 1, on branch `muse/player-fix-20261112`. The claimed fix is present and correct for the movie / best-print path: `?warm=1` + preferred audio on detail open (`DetailViewModel.loadDetail` -> `CatalogRepository.getPostDetail` -> `RaddStreamApi.getPostDetail`), server-side warm banks `resolved_cache` and `/api/v1/stream` 302s from cache (`viewer.py:_preresolve_for_detail`, `_resolve_and_bank`, stream-handler cache lookup), audio-first + gated-last ladder (`viewer.py:_option_groups`), client pre-resolve (`preresolveTopLink`, 2 s ceiling, 120 s reuse), 8 s watchdog + failover machine + 10 s HTTP timeouts. Three remaining gaps found by reading the code, all on the seasons/episodes path: **(1) Episodes are never warmed** — the server warms only the first option group and the client pre-resolves only `bestPrintOf`, so an episode Play tap always pays its 5-11 s live resolve (Salaar 720p 9.25 s) inside the player. Fix: `showRungsFor` now warms the opened scope's Auto handle in the background via `GET /api/v1/stream?redirect=0` (`warmScopeLink`: one in-flight warm, cancelled on scope change, 30 s ceiling, silent on failure, deduped per handle; pure handle pick `scopeWarmHandle` in `DetailPreResolve.kt`). **(2) The playLink fallback staged no failover** — `playPrint`'s fallback launched a bare single-rendition bundle, so the watchdog could only retry the same slow address and then give up while sibling copies sat unused in `print.links`. Fix: `playLink` takes an optional `backupHandles` list and stages it when non-empty (never with an empty list, so `playV2Bundle`'s staged runner-ups are never wiped); the fallback passes `siblingBackupHandles(print, link)` (other playable, non-page copies, capped at 5). **(3) The v2 work path warmed without audio** — `getWorkDetailV2`'s bridge call sent `warm=1` with no `audio`, so the warmed auto tier could be a different audio than the ladder Play presses. Fix: `audio = detailWarmAudio(userRegion)` threaded through `getWorkDetailV2`. Deliberately NOT changed: the 8 s watchdog / 10 s HTTP timeouts / 2 s playV2 ceiling (tuned constants); known tension recorded in `hidden_files/player-fix-diagnosis-20261112.md` — a cold 9.25 s resolve exceeds the 8 s watchdog, so a cold instant tap can still be cut off before its first resolve lands, and the retry-same races the server-side banking (retry ~8.8 s vs bank ~9.25 s). No `viewer.py` change (backend agent owns it), no live-tree / DB touch, no merge, no tag.

## Hero Watch Now fix — Appetize v1.1.2 FAILED 3 (2026-11-12 ~15:30 PKT)

**What:** the hero carousel's "Watch Now" did nothing on two taps (carousel kept rotating) while tapping the banner image opened the detail page. Root cause, found by reading the layout, not by guessing at the race: the page dots sat at the BOTTOM end, in the buttons' strip (bottom 20dp, buttons 52dp tall, dots' 48dp hit boxes [20,68] vs buttons [20,72] from the bottom), declared after the pager so on top in z-order. On a 6-dot hero the dots row spans x 97–395dp on a 411dp Pixel 6/7 and covers the Watch Now button's centre (~107dp) — a centred tap hit a dot (re-selecting the slide: no visible change) instead of the button. My List was overlapped at every dot count ≥ 2. Fix in `HeroCarousel.kt` only: (1) the indicator moves to the TOP end in a 0.55f-surface contrast pill — no dot can cover any control at any dot count, and the pill keeps the dots readable over bright artwork where the top scrim is clear; (2) the auto-advance loop now also skips its tick while a finger is down on Watch Now (`watchNowPressed`, reported up from the slide's own interaction source — deliberately NOT a LaunchedEffect key, so an in-flight advance is never cancelled mid-flight leaving the pager stranded between pages), so an advance starting mid-press can't slide the button away and cancel the tap; (3) the advance step is the pure `nextHeroPage` (wrap-around). The `onWatchNow` lambda already captures the composed page's post at tap time, so no stale-item change was needed; banner-image tap, dot taps and auto-rotation are untouched in behaviour. New tests in `HeroCarouselTest`: `nextHeroPage` advance/wrap/degenerate, `indicatorBandClearsTheButtonStrip` (320dp + 400dp heroes), and a witness that the old bottom-anchored placement overlapped the strip. Button/indicator geometry now lives in shared constants (`HERO_INDICATOR_TOP_DP`, `HERO_BUTTON_HEIGHT_DP`, `HERO_ACTION_BOTTOM_DP`) so the test guards the real layout.

## Session 148 — Salaar won't play on ANY version: /play mistranslation + mint-gate table (2026-11-12 ~16:30–17:15 PKT)

**What:** app-fix builder for ISSUE 1 (GOAL 1), on branch `muse/salaar-play-20261112` from main `ee5be6f3` (appfix merged). The Samsung RTL test (v1.1.2, 2 Galaxy phones) showed Salaar failing on every version with a "Cache engine failed" toast, while the API demonstrably plays it. Root-caused live, not from the code alone. **RC1 — `/play` mistranslates v2-path cat ids as legacy ids (wrong title):** the app's v2 detail maps prints verbatim (`WireDetailPrint.releaseId` is a cat id — Salaar 4K is 1318138, while the same title's v1 legacy ids are 1229325+, zero overlap), and `route_play` translated every bare `release_id` through `cat_id_map`. Proven: `{"release_id": 1318138}` returned The Strangers Chapter 2 (work 76848), whose winner handle presses 404; `{"release_id": 1318132}` (Salaar top 720p) returned work 84058, `download_only`; McLintock cat 1576938 also collides (work 112129). Control: legacy `{"release_id": 1229326}` returned Salaar work 74537, playable, 2 stream candidates. The server cannot disambiguate (both universes share numbers); only the caller knows. Fix: `WirePlayRequest.legacyReleaseId` (`legacy_release_id`, null = default legacy), `CatalogRepository.playV2(..., legacyReleaseId = true)`, `DetailViewModel` passes `workId < 0` at both `playV2` call sites (pre-resolve AND Play-press — the pre-resolve matters most, since a mistranslated warm would cache the wrong title's bundle for Play to reuse); `route_play` honors the flag (default true). **RC2 — the mint gate reads the wrong table:** `_bundle_is_gated` queried legacy `releases` with the bundle's cat id (always a cat id — `play_bundle` translates at entry), so a gated 4K print minted handles for a free caller. Proven: legacy 1229331 → playable 2160p bundle whose candidate handle presses 402. Fix: read `cat_releases` (resolution/quality_label/codec/label via `tiers.band_of`; size_bytes deliberately NOT passed — a byte count can contain "1080"/"720" spuriously). **App step-down:** `playPrint` fell back to the same gated print's own link when `playV2` yielded nothing — that link 402s, and the player burned its whole watchdog budget on copies that cannot play. Fix: for a premium print with no premium access, step down once to the best allowed print (pure `stepDownPrint` in `DetailPreResolve.kt`, prefers a playable copy) instead of pressing the gated link. **(b) "Cache engine failed":** symptom, not a cause — the string exists once (`CacheAffordance` maps `CacheState.FAILED` to the Keep chip text); the detail-open preview seed fetches the winner handle, a 402/404 handle fails the task, the chip reports it. `PlaybackService.localCopyUrlFor` treats engine failure as silence and streams from the network, so it cannot block playback; fixed handles make the chip stop failing. No separate change. **(c) "Try another version":** `startStreamHandle` builds a single-rendition bundle, so `tryNextPrint` can only hop within the same print's staged runner-ups — it never re-resolves a different print. After RC1+RC2 the bundle is the right title with live runner-ups, so the control works as designed; no player restructuring. **(d) 502s:** transient nginx upstream drops (did not reproduce on re-press — all three top-print handles 402 that run); `RenditionFailover` already retries-then-hops on any player error including `ERROR_CODE_IO_BAD_HTTP_STATUS`. No separate change. Contributing, already merged pending live deploy: the cold-resolve (9–12 s) vs 8 s watchdog race (`ba61135d` coalescing, `ee5be6f3`).

**Checks:** backend suites green locally (`nice -n 19`): `test_api_v2` 76 (74 + 2 new: cat id with `legacy_release_id: false` returns the named print despite a colliding map row; gate refuses a 1080p cat print even with a 720p legacy decoy row at the same id), `test_catalog_v2` 105, `test_edge_phase1` 19, `test_redact` 96. New app tests: `V2PlayWireTest` (universe flag serializes false/true/omitted), `PreResolveTest` step-down (best allowed print / null when none / null for premium caller / 480p cap demotes 720p). No local Gradle run by owner order — CI (`ci.yml` on push) is the verification path. **Not done:** push + CI verdicts; merge to main (coordinator's call); **still UNVERIFIED on a real device — only the Samsung retest proves Salaar plays on default Play and via Try-another-version.**

## Samsung RTL retest — Issues 6/7/8: search filter, player dialog, Home tab (2026-11-12 ~16:30 PKT)

**What:** three interaction/state fixes from the Samsung RTL device test of v1.1.2 (2 real Galaxy phones), branch `muse/appfix-nav-search-20261112` from main `0d1f4559`. **Issue 6 — Series filter unreliable:** two defects in `SearchViewModel`. (1) `resetFilters()` kept the Type chip (`SearchFilters(type = it.filters.type)`), so the empty state's "Clear filters" button and the sheet's "Reset" re-ran the same Series-filtered search and the list stayed at "No matches" — the button looked dead. Fix: reset builds a default `SearchFilters()` (sort to default too). (2) Stale-job overwrite race: `Job.cancel()` only bites at the next suspension point, so a search whose network call already returned kept running through its non-suspending write — a slow earlier search overwrote the newer one's list, so the same query + Series filter answered 1 result once and "No matches" on repeats, and a tap on the result card was followed by the stale job landing and the list going empty. Fix: a monotonic `searchGeneration`, bumped on every schedule (fresh searches also cancel a pending `loadMore`); every write after the debounce, after each v2/v1 call, and in the failure path bails unless still the latest generation; `loadMore` captures its generation and bails the same way; `scheduleSuggest` drops chips when the query has moved on. The card tap itself navigates correctly (`PosterCard` → `onPostClick` → `navigateToPost`) — the "re-ran the search" was the stale job landing after the tap. Live probes (read-only, public API): v1 `type=series` and v2 `type=series` both answer series titles (Breaking Bad 6 vs 9, Squid Game 5 vs 23 — v2 counts works, v1 counts posts); the routes disagree only in that v1 matches `content_type='series'` exactly while v2 folds complete/ongoing seasons into `series` — a real inconsistency, but NOT the flip cause, so no backend change: noted as a follow-up (one clause in `viewer.py:_facet_filter_clauses`) to keep this diff app-only and conflict-free. **Issue 7 — player dialog "Back to details" didn't dismiss:** two player-side fixes in `PlayerScreen.kt`. (1) The tap only popped: clearing the card's own state first (`vm.dismissGiveUp()` + `vm.dismissDeadlineGiveUp()`) then popping, via a shared `backToDetails` lambda used by both GiveUpCard call sites (handoff + 30 s deadline), so the tap is visibly answered at once whatever the pop does — including when the Detail underneath re-pushes the player on return. (2) The player forces landscape, so the dialog is short: up to six stacked 48dp actions + icon/title/text can exceed a ~360dp landscape screen and push "Back to details" / "Keep waiting" off the bottom edge, where a tap hits the scrim and (dismissOnClickOutside=false) does nothing. Fix: the actions stack scrolls inside a 216dp cap (`GiveUpActionsMaxHeight`). Also found while investigating (NOT fixed here — DetailScreen belongs to the parallel detail-load builder): Detail's autoplay effect keys on `(post.id, resumeLoaded, autoplay)` with `autoPlayedFor` as `remember` state, which resets when Detail leaves composition — so an autoplay Detail re-plays on EVERY return from the Player; needs a ViewModel-held flag, routed to the coordinator. **Issue 8 — Home tab didn't switch from Search:** the tap was gated on the composition-time route snapshot (`currentRoute`); after failed playback cycles the snapshot can lag the back stack and a stale read turns every tap into a silent no-op. Fix in `NavGraph.kt`: the tap reads `navController.currentDestination?.route` live at tap time; the navigate block (popUpTo Home + saveState + launchSingleTop + restoreState) is unchanged, and the selected highlight still reads the composed route. Honest caveat: no single deterministic NavController defect was provable from code alone — the navigate block itself is standard and correct in every back-stack shape traced; the stale-snapshot gate and the stuck-modal paths (Issue 7's dialog; the filter sheet's scrim eats the first tap while open) are the two tap-swallowing paths removed here. If the retest still fails with no sheet/dialog open, it needs a device repro of the NavController state.

**Checks:** full import diff per edited Kotlin file (no imports added or removed in any edited file — `dp`/`verticalScroll`/`rememberScrollState`/`heightIn` were already imported in PlayerScreen.kt); duplicate top-level type scan over the whole App tree: `SearchFilterStateTest`, `NavTabHomeTest`, `GiveUpActionsMaxHeight` each declared once, no new top-level type in the edited main files; brace/paren balance verified on all edited + new files after stripping strings/comments; new-test assertions verified against the edited sources with a mirror script before commit (resetFilters body, generation-check counts 4/2/1, back-to-details lambda ×2, no `onBackToDetails = onBackClick` left, live-read gate present + old gate absent). New tests: `SearchFilterStateTest` (reset clears type, generation guards), `NavTabHomeTest` (live-destination tap, Home navigate block intact, selected highlight intact); updated `PlayerBackExitTest` (scrollable actions, clear-before-pop ×2, vertical-stack assertion updated for the scrollable Column). Deliberately NOT touched: player/resolve code, detail-load code, hero, disclaimer, poster, landscape-layout code (parallel builders own them); no backend change; no live-tree / DB touch; no service restart. No local Gradle run by owner order — CI (`ci.yml` on push) is the verification path. **Not done:** push + CI verdict; merge to main; device retest on Samsung RTL (12 credits left) is the only proof for all three issues — CI green proves compile + unit tests, not the tap behaviour on a phone.

**Fixup (CI run 43212637148, commit a6992a8e):** 1435 tests, 1 failed — my own `SearchFilterStateTest` (`a superseded page load never appends its rows`): the assertion counted `if (generation == searchGeneration)` with an unescaped-paren `.toRegex()` — in regex the parens are grouping, so the pattern matched `if generation == searchGeneration` (no parens) and counted 0 against the real single guarded error write in `loadMore`'s catch block. Production code was correct; only the test's regex was wrong. Fix: escaped parens. All five assertions re-verified under Kotlin regex semantics with a mirror script (generation-check counts 4/2/1). Lesson: mirror scripts must use regex semantics, not literal `str.count`, when the test counts via `.toRegex()`. Rebased onto main b9722a4c (Issue 1 sibling merge).

**What:** the fix for the Sauce Labs Session 1 device failure (Pixel 5, Android 14, 07:06–07:12 PKT, APK app-debug-421, main 95180a6e): Home + all 5 nav tabs passed, but the Auto pill sat on 4K, Play timed out at 30 s with no frame, and the first-tap detail failed. **Root causes proven (code + nginx log + live probes, not inferred):** (1) Auto on 4K — the device IS a trial VIP account (anonymous account 201 at 07:06:15, entitlement `vip=true`, vip-pass 200 at 07:06:17, all in the log), so `serverVip=true` → `premiumAccess=true` → `VipQualityGate.gate` returns the ladder unchanged (`VipQualityGate.kt:108`) → `autoBand` stays 2160p. The Session 152 card fix only changed how the card reads the ladder; the ladder itself was never gated for this device. The server disagrees at stream time: the warm (`resolveStream`, no credential) pressed a gated handle and got 402 in 0.014 s, and the Play presses 402'd on gated handles too — while the same 2160p handle pressed with a fresh `?vip=` pass 302s (12.0 s) and with a Bearer key 302s (7.0 s), proven live. So the app believed in a VIP the stream endpoint never saw. (2) Play, no frame — every `/api/v1/stream` press costs 6–12 s of server-side live resolve, and the press is NOT cached (repeat press of the same handle: 8.0 s; warm then press: 6.1 s). Media3's read timeout was 10 s, so it timed out waiting for the 302 before ever touching the file; the five 302s in the log are presses that completed just under (or just after) the timeout. The winner is a 973 MB MKV on googleusercontent (TTFB 2.3 s, non-resumable, Range ignored) — a fast target once reached. (3) First tap — the v2 detail chain is 3 sequential calls; the first tap sent NO API call (log: nothing before 07:08:40; the 07:08:40–44 chain is the Retry), so the failure is app-side before any byte leaves the device (cold connection), and the repository swallows failures to null with only one null retry.

**Fixes:** (1) The gate now trusts the VIP the stream will honor, not the entitlement flag alone: new pure `qualityVipAccess(serverVip, hasLiveVipPass)` (`DetailPreResolve.kt`) — `premiumAccess` is `serverVip && hasLiveVipPass()` (new `SyncAccountRepository.hasLiveVipPass()`, a synchronous in-memory read), so a `vip=true` without a live pass is a free viewer for quality and Auto resolves to 720p; the ladder, card, player Auto and preresolve all read the one `premiumAccess` property. `refreshEntitlement` now warms the pass BEFORE publishing the entitlement, so observers see a consistent state. (4) First tap: `DETAIL_LOAD_NULL_RETRIES` 1 → 2, plus a once-per-process connection warm-up (`CatalogRepository.warmConnectionIfNeeded`, one cheap stats call, failures swallowed) invoked at the start of `loadDetail`, bounded to 3 s so a slow warm never holds the detail back. (5) 402 step-down on the Play path (assessed in Session 152, now built): `playV2Bundle` stages the gated ladder's rungs for the winner's band (`rungForBand(ladder, print.resolution.wire)` → `stageAutoLadder`) before `playLink`, and `stageAutoLadder` now computes `auto` from `ladder.effectiveAutoBand` (new pure `isAutoRung`) instead of the gate-nulled `autoBand`, so a gated Auto play is still recognised as Auto and a 402 steps down instead of giving up.

All six expectations mirror-checked in Python (Kotlin Long division / first-match semantics). No local Gradle run by owner order — CI (`ci.yml` on push) is the verification path. **Not done:** push + CI verdict (parent pushes); merge to main (parent's call); **nothing verified on a device — the Sauce Labs S2 re-test is the only proof Salaar plays (Auto = 720p, first frame inside 30 s, first tap loads).** Deliberately NOT touched: backend/Fast_Fetch code, live tree/service/DB, tags/releases, the remaining audit findings (D-2, R-1, speed reset, radii, tokens), the 6 primaries, 3.0 s auto-hide, 30 s give-up, 8 s actions narration.
