## Session — Batch C regression diagnosis + watchdog start-failover fix (2026-11-14)

**Diagnosis (this session, from code + server + the Robo Batch C report):** APK 499 (main c8b61fec) regressed vs APK 490 (bcacd5ea): McLintock! video black at 0:02, 30 s timeout give-up; Live TV stuck on "Finding your video…". The only player-path changes between the two builds are 78cd48a7 (429-as-pause) and 2420730f (warm-on-tap for Live TV/Downloads; the detail warm is unchanged). Neither can cause a stall: the 429 branch only adds a handoff, and the warm only adds a metadata ask. Proof the 429 fix never fired: the observed card was the 30 s deadline card ("Taking too long to start"), which renders only when `state.giveUp` is null — i.e. the failover machine never handed off RATE_LIMITED, so no 429 ever surfaced as a player error before the deadline. The stall was in the loading path, not the error path.

**Root mechanism, proven server-side:** every `/api/v1/stream` hit — warm (`redirect=0`), player press (`redirect=1`), and every cache-engine preview request through the redirector URL — charges the same 30/min/IP "play" bucket (`viewer.py` `_bucket_for` → `"play"`; the gate runs on path only). One title play therefore spends warm + player + preview presses, multiplied by Media3 internal retries and every failover hop, and Robo burned the bucket ~12 s in. Live TV warm wiring itself is sound (server-side bank, no client key to mismatch); Live TV failed because the movie session had already emptied the shared bucket and Robo's fast taps cancel earlier warms (`warmJob?.cancel()`).

**Fix (this commit):** the stall watchdog called `machine.onFailure(...)` without `beforeFirstFrame`, so its first failover was RetrySame — re-pressing the same stalled/429'd address (and re-seeding a preview press-pair) while the 30 s clock ran out — contradicting `onFailure`'s own S2 rule ("a start failure must never retry the SAME rendition") and the watchdog's own comment ("failed over exactly as a player error would be"). Now passes `beforeFirstFrame = true`: a 20 s stall hops to a backup / the next rank instead. The S5 kept-copy exception is preserved (`isLocalCopyAttempt` still buys one live-link retry). Effect: a stalled play under an exhausted bucket now reaches the honest RATE_LIMITED handoff ("The server asked us to slow down", user-gated retry) instead of the misleading timeout card. Winner-link/moov-at-tail for the 499 prints stays unproven (490's winner was never recorded) — owed probe: ranged moov check on the two 499 winners (gd-mirror, nexus).

**Tests:** no new test needed — the `beforeFirstFrame = true` machine behavior is already pinned by `RenditionFailoverStartTest`; the change is one flag in the service call site.

**Checks:** duplicate top-level type scan — no new top-level types. Full import diff — no import changes (comment + one named argument only). No local Gradle run by owner order — CI (`ci.yml` on push) is the verification path. **Not done:** CI verdict on this commit; merge to main (parent's call); Robo re-run for device proof (do not re-run until this fix candidate exists — it now does; the re-run itself is the supervisor's call, one of 10 virtual/day).

## Session — Robo re-test fix (app half): follow once, fetch preview chunks direct (2026-11-14)

**Diagnosis (this session, from code + the Robo re-test report):** matrix-2o5vajv1g1wia (APK 501, server 71c34004 with the bucket split live) still played nothing: McLintock! buffered 35 s with zero bytes, Live TV failed 6x with `UnrecognizedInputFormatException` in ~35 s. Nginx for the Robo device shows 36 `/api/v1/stream` presses in one minute (12:20) and 9x 429 on stream presses — the play bucket still tripped after the server split. Press accounting, proven from code: `AheadFetcher` fetches one 1 MiB chunk per OkHttp GET against `task.currentUrl`, which is the redirector URL (`CacheRepository.enqueue` sets it from `seed.redirectUrl`), so one 40 MiB preview pass costs up to 40 redirector presses (a first seed 8). The app's own preview/metadata calls already default to `redirect=0` (`RaddStreamApi.kt`), but the cache engine's byte fetches go through the redirector with `redirect=1`. The HLS path already does it right: `HlsAheadBuffer` records the post-redirect `finalUrl` and resolves segments against it, so segments never re-press the redirector.

**Fix (this commit):** the progressive fetcher now does the same. `RangeByteFetcher.fetch` reports the URL that actually served the bytes (`RangeFetchResult.Success.finalUrl`, from `response.request.url` — the pattern `HlsAheadBuffer` and the 402-gate check already use). `AheadFetcher.run` adopts it for the rest of the pass, so one pass costs exactly one redirector press; the learned address lives only in that pass and is never persisted — every `persist*`/`finalize` call still passes the row's `currentUrl`, so the row keeps our redirector address, re-resolve (`RedirectorSourceResolver.reResolve`, keyed off `task.resourceId`) and identity keep working, and a rotted target still falls back to `NEEDS_RERESOLVE`. One guard: `fetch` takes a `gateUrl` (default = the fetched URL; `AheadFetcher` passes the row's redirector URL), so a 402 from the file host is never mistaken for our own quality gate's 402 — the Salaar distinction stays exact. The player's own play path is untouched (it still plays via the redirector) and the failover machine is untouched.

**The seed cap/debounce half was already satisfied — nothing built for it:** the engine dedupes seeds by sourceKey (`CacheRepository.enqueue` returns `AlreadyKept` for a live row; `launchTask` no-ops when the job is active), the detail seed is linger-gated + Wi-Fi-only + first-seed capped, and binge prefetch is probe-first (`redirect=0`) + planner-bounded. Re-seeding the same handle cannot add a press; the multiplier was entirely per-chunk presses, fixed above.

**Tests:** three new Robolectric cases in `AheadFetcherFinalizeTest` behind a client that plays redirector (302 to a file host) + file host (Range slices): a 40 MiB preview pass makes exactly 1 redirector press with the row still naming the redirector; a file host that 403s from chunk two yields `NEEDS_RERESOLVE` with the row still on the redirector; a full download through the redirector commits with correct bytes and the row still on the redirector. A fourth case pins the `gateUrl` guard: a 402 from the file host is a retryable `RETRY_LATER`, never our gate refusing the rung.

**CI failure + test fix (same session):** branch CI run 43575181977 FAILED — all 3 new tests failed at their first outcome assertion (1634 tests, 3 failed, all mine; production code untouched by the failure). Root cause in the TESTS, not the fix: the client returned a real 302 from a network interceptor, which OkHttp never follows — the fetcher saw the 302 itself (`HttpError(302)`) instead of the file host's 206. The codebase's own pattern (`HlsAheadBufferTest`) is to simulate the post-redirect state with an application interceptor that answers the redirector's request with the file host's bytes and the response carrying the post-redirect request URL — that is exactly how OkHttp presents a followed 302, and the redirect itself is OkHttp's job, proven in production. Rewrote the client to that pattern (counts now read 1 redirector + 39 direct for the 40-chunk pass, since chunk one's bytes arrive via the 302) and added the 402 case above. **Not done:** CI verdict on this commit; merge to main (parent's call); device proof on the next Robo run; the server half (art bucket + first-tick warm cap) is a separate branch.

## Session — Live TV "Nothing playable": declare HLS on the channel path (2026-11-14)

**Diagnosis (this session, from the Robo #4 report + logcat + nginx + code):** APK 504 (main b18f0dc5) still played no Live TV: Aaseervatham TV stuck on "Finding your video", Aastha Gujarati failed with "Nothing playable here right now". Logcat shows exactly 3 player errors, all `ERROR_CODE_PARSING_CONTAINER_UNSUPPORTED` / `UnrecognizedInputFormatException` via `ProgressiveMediaPeriod$ExtractingLoadable` — the player treated the streams as progressive files. Nginx for the Robo device (70.32.142.212, 14:11–14:20 PKT): 12 stream presses, 7x 302 + 5x 200 warm, ZERO 429/404 — the server served every press. Direct probe of both channels' 302 targets: real HLS master playlists (206, `application/vnd.apple.mpegurl` / `application/x-mpegURL`, `#EXTM3U` multivariant). The server's links are good; the failure is the reader choice. Chain: Live TV tap -> `player/{streamId}/{title}` -> `PlayerViewModel.startStreamHandle` -> `PlaybackBundle.forStreamHandle` with `mimeType=null`, so `LinkClassification.classify` sees only the extensionless redirector URL, `isHls()` is false, protocol defaults to PROGRESSIVE, `manifestMimeType` returns null, and `DefaultMediaSourceFactory` infers progressive — the exact failure its own comment describes. The movie path is unaffected (the v2 bundle carries protocol per rendition); only the bare-handle path builds blind. All 759 channels are HLS (registry check: every `stream_url` ends `.m3u8`).

**Fix (this commit):** the Live TV tap stages the manifest MIME (`PlayerSessionStore.stageManifestMime`, same in-memory-only discipline as `stageFailover`) and `startStreamHandle` hands it to `forStreamHandle`'s existing `mimeType` parameter — so `classify` sees HLS, protocol becomes `hls`, and `manifestMimeType` returns `APPLICATION_M3U8`. The route is untouched (a protocol hint is launch metadata, not an address, and the store is where this codebase stages exactly that). A bare handle with no staged entry — a movie, a deep link — passes null and builds exactly as before. Failover machine, play path, server, seed/cache engine untouched.

**Tests:** 7 new cases in `LiveTvHlsDeclareTest`: a Live TV bundle declares HLS (`isHls`, protocol `hls`, `manifestMimeType` M3U8) for the constant and the vendor alias spelling; a bare handle stays progressive with no declaration; store stage/peek round-trip, peek-does-not-consume, blank-guard, unknown-handle-null.

Two Robolectric tests in HomeCheckInNudgeTest pin it (gate on → strip shown, gate off → strip absent even with a ladder). Goldens unaffected (the Paparazzi fake state's default is true). Still owed in Phase 5: coins + VIP buttons on Dashboard/Profile, SponsorCard + VipSourcesCard on Detail, VIP-screen entry points, and a foreground `refreshNow()` so panel changes land live.

**Free launch 3 (branch free-launch-20261115, 2026-11-15):** the ultimate plan's Phase 5, slice 3 — the last paywall surfaces plus the live refresh. **Search speed (branch search-fts-count-20261115, 2026-11-15):** the ultimate plan's Phase 1, first API item — measured before touching code (in-process, read-only live catalog): "love" 8.67s, "the" ~4.4s, "salaar" 0.03s. The split: the second COUNT(*) cost ~half (love 8.67s with it, 4.38s without), the rest was the per-token LIKEs + haystack UDF. Surprise: "love" is a mood word, so it never ran a text search — it answers as a romance/drama genre browse, and the genre browse itself was 7.9s (the radd_list_has Python UDF). Backend (`catalog_api.py`): (1) when `cat_works_fts` exists it IS the text match — the LIKEs are dropped for execution (same normalised fields in the index; only substring-inside-a-word recall is lost, "glove" for "love"); cursors keep working because the fingerprint is still computed from the LIKE shape; the LIKE scan stays as the no-FTS fallback and the FTS-error degrade path is unchanged. (2) Totals cap at 1000 with `total_capped=True` for any search OR faceted browse (threaded `total_cap` param so tests can set it small); only a plain unfiltered browse keeps the exact count. (3) Genre/language facet predicates go from the Python UDF to C-level `instr()` (measured 0.26s vs 4.62s for "romance", over-match 8 in 23,852); `json_each` was rejected because the genres column is mixed JSON-array and comma-separated plain text. (4) Language browse: the 133s cold was a cold-cache first touch of cat_releases; warm it is 4–6s and the correlated EXISTS stays — an IN-subquery measured 119.8s and a bare releases scan 34.6s — with the cap keeping a cold load under the 15s edge. The manifest's pagination "carries" list names `total_capped`, and test_api_v2 pins both that and the field on the wire (83 tests OK). App: `WireBrowseResponse`/`V2BrowsePage` carry `totalCapped`; `resultsSummary` prints "Showing N of 1000+ results" when capped; the v1 fallback and fresh-search resets clear the flag (v1 totals are exact). Tests: backend 138 in test_catalog_api (2 new: capped total incl. faceted browse, FTS pinned queries, facet equivalence vs `_list_has`) + fts_search 9, redact 104, search_forgiving 11, viewer_search_forgiving 20, catalog_v2 106, api_v2 83 — all green locally; full backend gate (101 suites) runs in CI. App tests: capped wording + wire deserialisation. Measured after: love 0.65s, the 0.24s (capped), salaar 0.01s, cafe 0.04s, romance browse 0.60s, plain browse 0.53s, Hindi browse 4–6s warm.

**Robo crash fix (branch crash-filter-sheet-20261115, 2026-11-15):** Robo #6 (APK 571) FAILED with one fatal exception — `IllegalStateException: Vertically scrollable component was measured with an infinity maximum height constraints` — on the Search screen in the final minute, twice (PIDs 8770 @ 08:11:57, 10123 @ 08:11:01 PKT). Full stack trace from the Firebase console has no app frames; the first frames are `CheckScrollableContainerConstraints.kt:35` ← `ScrollingLayoutNode.measure (Scroll.kt:385)`, i.e. a `Modifier.verticalScroll` node measured with infinite max height. Pinpoint (VM clone @ f5af45ab, read-only): the only verticalScroll on the Search screen that can receive unbounded height is the filter sheet's scrolling middle — `FilterSheetBody`'s `weight(1f, fill = false)` Column inside a wrap-content outer Column in a ModalBottomSheet. The discovery column is bounded by the root Column, Settings/Home/Dashboard scrolled columns are Scaffold-bounded, and the consent sheet has no verticalScroll (Robo passed onboarding). The crash is latent, not a regression: the F10 sheet rebuild (Batch B) introduced the weight, and Robo #6 is the first run whose taps opened the sheet. Fix: one modifier — `.heightIn(max = 1200.dp)` before the weight — the cap sits above any phone screen, so it only binds on the unbounded path; the bounded path (and the goldens) are untouched. Regression test `SearchFilterSheetTest.survivesUnboundedParentHeight` renders the sheet body under a scrolling (unbounded-height) parent and asserts the sections + footer exist instead of throwing during measure. Screenshot re-read (45–50.png) confirmed no sheet was visible in the sampled frames — Robo recovered between the crash and the next screenshot — and confirmed the "Trending searches / Trending now" labels are real (they live at SearchScreen.kt:618/646; an earlier grep missed them because the VM clone's working tree holds a staged revert that deletes them — read HEAD, never that worktree, for crash analysis).

**Robo crash fix, fixup (same branch, 2026-11-15):** CI 580 (43675000368) FAILED at `:app:compileDebugUnitTestKotlin` — one error: `SearchFilterSheetTest.kt:10:33 Unresolved reference 'assertExists'`. The import `androidx.compose.ui.test.assertExists` does not resolve in this Compose version; in this codebase assertExists is a member of the node interaction, never an import (see CatalogImageLoadingTest.kt:68). Fix: delete the import line; the test's `.assertExists()` calls resolve as members, matching every other test in the tree. A NOTE comment in the test pins the rule so it is not re-added. Nothing else changed; the fix itself (heightIn cap) is untouched.

SectionHeader (every rail header in the app) goes from `RaddEmphasized.titleLarge` (22sp bold) to `RaddEmphasized.titleMedium` (16sp bold) — the Android research agent's biggest single win: 22sp is the app-bar/page-title slot, and a rail head at 22sp shouts over the posters below it. M3 Expressive has no density scale factor; density comes from picking the smaller token. One call site (CommonUi.kt), comment rewritten to record the decision. Two research corrections found while scoping this slice, recorded so nobody re-chases them: (1) the "6× 15sp literals" claim is wrong — there are ZERO `.sp` literals anywhere in the App tree (verified by grep); every size goes through typography tokens, so there is nothing to snap. (2) "Row titles 16→14sp" is not a blanket change — PosterCard's title is already titleSmall (14sp), and the remaining titleMedium (16sp) sites are mostly card/screen headings; the two checked (DetailErrorHeader's title beside the poster, My List's "Most versions") are one-off headings, not repeated rows, so they stay 16sp. Expected golden impact: every Paparazzi shot rendering a SectionHeader (homeLoaded and others) will shift — CI's verifyPaparazziDebug will say; re-record and accept by eye. No test pins the header style (TextContrastTest checks its colour, not its size).

**CI: lint runs as its own parallel job (branch ci-lint-split-20261115, 2026-11-15):** `lintDebug` moves out of the build job's single Gradle invocation into a `lint` job that runs in parallel with it (same setup steps: checkout, JDK 17, Gradle cache restore, SDK, google-services.json). Lint is 1–2 min of a 4–7 min run; the wall-clock saving is ~0.5–1.5 min per run. The workflow verdict is unchanged — GitHub fails the run if either job fails — and the lint report is uploaded from the lint job (`ci-lint-<run_number>`), so a lint failure is still one click away in the same run. The build job keeps its single invocation (assemble + tests) and the Paparazzi verify step. Correction recorded so nobody re-chases it: the Android-density-CI report's #1 (`gradle/actions/setup-gradle` with caching, est. 1–2.5 min/run) assumed the Gradle User Home is wiped every run — WRONG for this repo. ci.yml has restored `~/.gradle/caches` + `~/.gradle/wrapper` via `actions/cache` (keyed on wrapper properties + versions + build scripts) since commit 34219adc. `setup-gradle` would add only the build-cache + kotlin-dsl script caches on top — a marginal duplicate, NOT built.

Shape is a true pill now (24dp radius on a 48dp pill, was 20dp). No selected-state inversion: every chip navigates away, none filters in place. **Cards vary now (M11) (branch home-varied-cards-m11-20261115, 2026-11-15):** a rail read as identical grey rectangles because every tile was one image + text with nothing of its own. Two of the three fixes are real now, one is scoped out honestly. (1) Artwork accent: PosterCard passes the loaded bitmap to `rememberArtworkAccent` — the 81-pixel sampler DetailScreen's poster border already uses — and paints a 1dp rim in the poster's own colour (0.55 alpha, Detail's value) plus a 6dp tinted glow (`Modifier.shadow`, ambient 0.18 / spot 0.30). Nothing paints until the bitmap loads: the fallback accent would rim every unloaded tile in brand jade, the uniform look this removes. On pre-S devices the tinted shadow colours are ignored and the card is exactly as before. (2) NEW pill: a jade pill on the free TopEnd corner (rank owns TopStart, rating BottomStart) when the year is plausible and within the last two calendar years — `isNewReleaseYear`, upper bound stricter than `displayYearLabel` (NEW means released, so next year's film never earns it; CI run 43689489607 caught the first version letting 2027 through, fixed the same hour). Paint-only; the tile's one spoken sentence says "new release". (3) Quality badge: NOT built — the list wire carries no quality field (it lives on Detail's RankedPrint) and inventing one would break the honesty rule; it waits on a server `best_quality` field. Tests: `IsNewReleaseYearTest` (pure, 4 cases) + `PosterCardNewBadgeTest` (Robolectric, sentence pins the wiring; the year comes off the clock so the test stays current in 2027+). Golden impact: none expected — no Paparazzi fixture year is 2025+ and no bitmap loads under Paparazzi, so the rim/glow/pill never render there.

**Live duration/seek bar (branch live-duration-hide-20261115, 2026-11-15):** Discover Pakistan showed a 2:00:12 duration with a seek bar on a live channel. The UI already gated everything on `isLive` (seek bar, time row, buffered %, LIVE mark), but `isLive` came only from Media3's `isCurrentMediaItemLive`, which reads false when the channel's HLS playlist carries an end tag — the 2-hour DVR window then poses as a VOD. The Live TV tap already stages per-handle state in PlayerSessionStore (the manifest MIME, Robo #4), so it now stages a live flag next to it (`stageLiveChannel`/`isLiveChannel`, same in-memory-only discipline, same 24-entry cap); PlayerViewModel captures it once per bundle in `beginBundle` and the ticker ORs it with the Media3 value, and a live bundle never adopts the DVR window as `durationMs`. A movie opened after a channel in the same session clears the flag. Tests: three new cases in LiveTvHlsDeclareTest (flag reads back, reads without consuming, blank stages nothing); the isLive UI gating was already covered (PlayerStatusWordTest + the isLive Paparazzi shot).

Nothing is removed — swipe, dots and Watch Now all work, the pure advance helpers (`nextHeroPage`, `shouldAdvanceHero`) are untouched, and the operator can still publish `hero_autoplay: true` from the panel, with the viewer's own autoplay-previews switch still gating it (`theme.heroAutoplay && autoplayPreviews` in NavGraph). The 8 s interval is unchanged. Test: the "no theme decodes to the dark brand defaults" case moves with the default (`assertFalse`). Golden impact: none — the Paparazzi home shots already pass `heroAutoplay = false` because the carousel timer never settles in a snapshot.

The app now says the same thing everywhere the viewer sees it: the Home rail title (`initialHomeSections`), the My List empty-state rail, and the Search sort label (`SearchSort.MOST_SOURCES`). **First open is the catalog, not a wall (B5 + M9) (branch home-first-open-b5-m9-20261115, 2026-11-15):** a first-time viewer hit three chores before any title — Disclaimer, then the analytics question, then Pick 3 — with no "watch now" in under 30 seconds. Two of the three move. (1) The analytics sheet gains a visible "Skip for now" (full-width, 48dp) — one tap reaches the catalog, the question asks again on the next launch; a swipe-down dismiss is the same skip, and skipping records and counts nothing. MainActivity hides the sheet for the launch only (`consentSkippedThisLaunch` — without it a skip would re-show on the next recomposition, since null is still "never asked"). The Disclaimer is untouched — wording, "I understand" / Decline, and the no-dismiss rule are the owner's legal text. (2) Pick 3 waits for the first browse or play: a new persisted flag `firstBrowseDone` (ServerSettingsRepository, same shape as `pickThreeDone`) gates `showPickThree`, and it is set from the two choke points that cover every path — DetailViewModel init (any detail open, from Home, Search, Similar or a deep link) and PlayerViewModel `beginBundle` (any playback start, including Live TV) — never from Home alone, so a first browse from Search counts too. The write is fire-and-forget and idempotent, like the other one-time flags. (3) M9: "Not now" is a real button now — an OutlinedButton with a 48dp minimum height (the floor the file's other dismissals already use), not a ~40dp TextButton link; the heart IconButtons were already 48dp. Tests: PickThreeTest's "brand new viewer sees the card" case moves with the gate (a viewer who has browsed once sees it) and a new case pins the deferral (candidates ready, card hidden until the first browse). Golden impact: none expected — no Paparazzi fake renders the card (loadedHome has Continue Watching + a favorite; loading/empty have no candidates), and the consent sheet is not snapshotted.

**Skeletons mirror the real layout (branch home-skeletons-20261115, 2026-11-15):** every loading placeholder measured against the composable it stands in for, dimension by dimension — a skeleton that is not the size of its content is a page that jumps when the data lands. The shared `PosterCellTextSkeleton` now draws the card's own text column: a 40dp title slot (titleSmall's 20dp line, twice), a 16dp details line, the always-24dp badge slot, and the card's 10dp bottom padding. (2) Detail: the old skeleton was a poster + 3 lines + a 44dp bar — the whole lower screen reflowed. It now mirrors `DetailContent` block for block (hero, Play, secondary row, rung card, synopsis, cast, print summary, similar titles), 16dp apart like the LazyColumn. Play is 48dp (was 44dp — the 4dp jump, pinned by `SkeletonParityTest` against `PrimaryActions`' `heightIn(min = 48.dp)`); the secondary row (Save/Download/Share, 48dp each) is new; the rung card is "Quality" + subtitle + three 76dp rows; the header mirrors `PosterHeader` (176dp backdrop band + 92dp spacer, 120dp poster, two 36dp title lines, 16dp meta/included lines, 20dp rating badge, 22dp chips row). The skeleton also dropped its own double padding — the caller already applies `detailPadding`, so the old one sat 32dp in from the edge and 8dp low. **Hero pin + branded fallback frame + prefetch (branch home-hero-pin-20261115, 2026-11-15):** the hero rode the first visible section, and the panel's sections come first — so when the panel's curated hero list went stale (McLintock! 1963, Tarzan's Revenge, The Stranger 1946) the first screen showed old films while the newest feed walked 2027s. (a) Stale-hero fallback: `selectHeroSection` (pure, in HomeViewModel.kt) — a panel-managed first rail whose newest plausible year is older than last year loses the slot to "Recently added"; fresh panel curation (a 2026 or 2027 title) is used as-is, and a built-in first rail is never stale-checked (newest by construction). Plausibility reuses `displayYearLabel` (1900..currentYear+1), so a mis-parsed 20215 or an all-null-year list is stale. When the panel hero is stale and Recent is still loading the function returns null and the hero skeleton holds — never flash the old hero for one frame; when Recent failed or came back empty the stale hero still shows (stale beats nothing). (b) Branded fallback frame: new vector `res/drawable/hero_fallback.xml` (dark surface + jade mark, ~3.6 KB, no raster art, no fake posters) painted by `HeroFallbackFrame` as CatalogImage's loading slot on the hero slide — the bare shimmer is what read as a black void on first paint. The frame carries no title text on purpose: the slide's headline already prints the title in big type through the whole load, and printing it on the frame too duplicates it (M1, Appetize-proven); the no-URL branch still carries the title on its fallback card, where the headline is dropped. The error path is unchanged (Hero-tone fallback card). (c) Prefetch: HomeContent warms the hero items' art (`prefetchHeroArt`, hero items only, HERO_LIMIT = 6) the moment the hero items are known, built exactly like the slide's own request — same TMDB sizing rewrite, same host allowlist, same metered gate — and Coil dedupes the slide already loading; it never throws. Tests: HeroSelectionTest (12 pure cases incl. the 2027-fresh / 2025-fresh / 2024-stale / all-null / 20215 / skeleton-hold / failed-Recent / panel-owned-Recent edges), HeroArtPrefetchTest (backdrop-first, poster fallback, blanks, dedupe, order), HeroFallbackFrameTest (Robolectric, the frame renders). A Paparazzi heroLoadingFrame shot (the slide with a real TMDB URL, so the loading slot and its frame show) was tried and dropped: any real art URL reaches CatalogImage, whose Hilt entry-point lookup throws under Layoutlib ("Could not find an Application in the given context") — the same reason every Paparazzi fake carries a null art URL; the record run failed on it in both verify and record mode (CI 43712367734, record 43712838753). Expected golden impact: none — homeLoaded/homeLoading unchanged (the fixture's first rail is built-in, not panel-managed; the skeleton holds the same slot), no new golden.

**Pick 3 stays up (branch home-pick3-stay-20261115, 2026-11-15):** two Firebase Robo runs on b944e0e2 (123 + 100 actions) never showed the "Pick 3 you like" card even though every other gate was met, and the second run killed the favourite-first theory (My List stayed empty the whole run). Root cause, found in code: PickThreeCard fired onShown from a LaunchedEffect on first composition, markPickThreeShown set the persisted pick_three_shown flag, and showPickThree required that flag false — so the card retired itself the frame it appeared and lived ~0-1 frames. Fix: the once is now a whole Home visit — HomeUiState gains a session-only pickThreeShownThisVisit latch with pure onPickThreeShown()/onPickThreeVisitEnded() transitions, showPickThree stays true while the latch holds (the empty-favourites gate is an entry condition, not a live one — one or two picks do not hide the card mid-visit; the third pick retires it via pickThreeDone), and a DisposableEffect at the call site clears the latch when the card leaves composition (Home left, or the card scrolled out of the feed), after which the persisted flag keeps it away. markPickThreeShown() now applies the state transition + persists; new endPickThreeVisit() clears only the latch. Tests: PickThreeTest gains lifecycle cases (display latches the visit, leaving Home ends it, one pick does not hide it, third pick retires it) and a new PickThreeVisitTest drives the real HomeContent gate (the card survives the shown callback + recomposition; leaving Home and coming back shows nothing). Expected golden impact: none — the homeLoaded fixture has a saved title, so the card never renders there.

**Search filter rail reveals its selection (branch search-chip-scroll-20261115, 2026-11-15):** Robo #7 noted the last Search filter chip ("Complete series") cut off at the right edge ("Comp…") — and shot 34 showed it STILL cut off while selected ("Filtered: Complete series" in the top bar). Checking the code: the rail already scrolls (LazyRow) with end content padding (Session 121 P-29), so the last chip was always reachable by hand — what it never did was reveal its own selection. Fix, in FilterRail only: a LazyListState + LaunchedEffect on the selected type scrolls just enough to bring that chip fully into view (minimal delta from layoutInfo offsets; nothing when it is already visible, so tapping a visible chip never moves the row; far off-screen falls back to scroll-to-item). The effect waits one frame first (withFrameNanos) because layoutInfo is empty until the row's first layout pass. Chip labels, order, and tap behaviour are unchanged; the suggestions/recents/trending rows already carry the same end padding and have no selection state, so they are untouched. Tests: new SearchFilterRailTest (last chip + Filters button reveal by scrolling; selected "Complete series" scrolls fully into view on a 360dp viewport; selecting a visible "Movies" chip does not move the row). Expected golden impact: none — the searchFilterRail golden selects "Movies", already fully visible, so the effect is a no-op there.
**Home tab does not switch after failed playback (branch home-tab-playback-20261115, 2026-11-15):** owed Phase 2 check, root cause found in DetailScreen, not in the player service or the tab handler. The tab tap already reads `navController.currentDestination` live at tap time (Issue 8 fix, pinned by NavTabHomeTest; in Navigation 2.7.7 that getter reads a synchronously-updated StateFlow) and `PlaybackService.onPlayerError` never touches navigation — so the wedge was upstream: DetailScreen's autoplay once-per-title latch `autoPlayedFor` was a plain `remember`, which Navigation Compose discards when Detail leaves the composition for the Player. Coming back from a failed playback, the latch was null again — and the post was already loaded and the resume lookup already landed in the surviving ViewModel — so the autoplay effect re-fired at once and `playBest()` re-opened the failed player within a frame. Every exit from the player was undone before the viewer could reach a tab, which reads exactly as "tapping Home does nothing" (PlayerScreen's own "Back to details" comment already documents the mechanism: the Detail underneath "re-pushes the player on return (its autoplay effect re-fires on a fresh composition)"). Fix: `autoPlayedFor` is now `rememberSaveable`, kept in the back-stack entry's saved state, so a return never re-plays; a different title is a different entry, so its own autoplay is untouched. Second half, same journey: the player card's way home (NAV-4) and the dead-link screen's way home (NAV-5) both navigated to Home with `launchSingleTop` only and no `popUpTo`, stacking a second Home over the dead Player — Back from it dropped the viewer back into the failed player. Both now use the tab-tap block (popUpTo Home with saveState + restoreState). Tests: new DetailAutoplayLatchTest (latch is rememberSaveable; effect still guards and sets it) and PlayerHomeNavigationTest (both way-home blocks pop up to Home). Expected golden impact: none — no Home layout changed. CI note: run 43725641191 on 3cc59907 failed compileDebugKotlin — `rememberSaveable` was imported from `androidx.compose.runtime`, which does not exist; it lives in `androidx.compose.runtime.saveable` (as LocalFilesScreen already imports it). The drift test asserted the wrong import too; both fixed in the follow-up commit.

**Detail screen redesign (branch detail-redesign-20261115, 2026-11-15):** the comparison spec (~/workspace/detail-screen-comparison-20261115.md) rebuilt Detail in Netflix/Disney+ order. (1) The synopsis sits directly under the Play actions, the quality ladder below it, with one consolidated "Audio & Subtitles" line between them (pure `audioSubtitleLine`, from the prints' own languages/subtitle langs — null when neither exists). (2) SponsorCard and VipSourcesCard are deleted; the lock is the rung's own VIP tier pill, never a second card — and Report moves from the top bar into a More overflow ("More options" → "Report broken stream"). (3) The version list and PrintSummary are gone: the ladder already folds one best copy per band, so PrintCards render only when the server sent no ladder at all (max 3 + "Show all N files" / "Show fewer files"); "versions" becomes "files" everywhere the viewer sees it, copy numbers stay spoken-only on the fallback cards, and the cam warning survives as one user-words line ("Some copies here are cam recordings — low quality.") when any print is cam. (4) The painted title strips its suffixes: the server's `display_title` is now read on Post/PostDetail (`displayTitleWire`), preferred when present, else the clean title stripped by pure `UserWords.detailTitle`/`stripTitleSuffixes` (trailing "(YYYY)" matching the post's year, a trailing language word from the post's own languages, a trailing Movie/Series word — tail only, so "The English Patient" and "1917" keep theirs); hero, backdrop fallback and error header all paint it. (5) Tier 2, only where the data exists: a series with more than five seasons gets a SeasonDropdown (M3 DropdownMenu) instead of a chip strip; the season header gains a Download-season button (scrimmed 48dp circle, BottomEnd) that plans one best keepable copy per episode (`seasonKeepPlan`, pure — VIP-locked episodes counted, never downloaded; packed-only episodes skipped) and asks first via SeasonKeepConfirmDialog (count + total size, "Size unknown" when none named), confirming through the same per-handle keep routing as a single download (engine for HLS, device file otherwise, Wi-Fi gate re-checked at confirm); episode rows show a jade "Downloaded" check when a READY download on this device covers one of their prints (`DeviceDownload` gains `handle`, carried from the entity that already stored it; the ViewModel collects READY handles into `downloadedHandles`); a dead end gets its reason in plain words (`deadEndReasonFor`, pure — no sources / only VIP copies / no copies / no working sources, with or without a download on the table) plus a "Browse similar titles" button that scrolls the rail into view; the similar rail is renamed "More Like This". Verified during the build, not assumed: a free viewer can never download a VIP rung (`keepRung` refuses locked options and the gate removes premium bands outright); the pre-resolve warm already skips titles with no playable copy; with the gate OFF every rung is Standard and no premium shows; and T1-5 (episode duration/synopsis) plus T2-3 (director, cast photos, actor page), T2-4 (trailer row), T2-5 (vote count, Rate action) are OWED for missing server data — the wire carries no director, cast artwork, trailer URL, vote count or Top-10 rank, and EpisodeGroup carries no runtime or synopsis, so none of it was faked. One real compile bug caught in review: `seasonKeepPlan` called a 3-arg `VipQualityGate.allowsResolution` that did not exist — the cap-aware overload now exists, mirroring `allowsBand`. Tests: UserWordsTest gains 6 title cases; DetailPaywallTest rewritten (no "Go VIP" / "4K and 1080p are part of VIP" ever, rung VIP pill still shows, free launch shows no "VIP" at all); new DetailRedesignTest (synopsis above the Quality header, "More Like This", dropdown past five seasons, dead-end reason + Browse similar); new DetailDeadEndReasonTest, DetailSeasonKeepPlanTest, DetailAudioLineTest. Paparazzi fixtures updated (removed params, honest included lines — "720p included — 1080p and 4K need VIP" for the locked movie, "Included with free — up to 720p" for the series); expected golden impact: detailMovie, detailMovieError, detailSeries, detailSeriesEpisodes — record run + eye-check owed after CI.

**Robo #10 nested-scroll crash fixed (branch crash-nested-scroll-20261116, 2026-11-16):** Robo #10 (APK 757) failed on `IllegalStateException: Vertically scrollable component was measured with an infinity maximum height constraints`; the Test Lab stack named no screen (only androidx.compose frames) and the VIP screen was ruled out as the prime suspect (71.png was captured after the crash, not before it). A full static sweep found no nest — 31 scroll sites, 4 bottom sheets, 7 dialogs, every lazy layout with a finite parent, no `wrapContentSize(unbounded = true)`, no custom layout — so the hunt went empirical: new `NestedScrollCrashTest` renders every screen's content with rich state (non-empty lists, so the lazy branches compose) plus every sheet body inside its real bottom sheet, one test per composition. First CI run 43758154976: 7 failures, of which exactly one was the crash — `playerSheetLandscapeWithScrollableContent` threw the verbatim Robo #10 exception. Root cause, PlayerSheet's landscape branch: the side panel wrapped the sheet in its own verticalScroll column while four sheets (SubtitleSettings, Tracks, More, PrintLog) scroll themselves, and the player forces landscape on entry (PlayerScreen sets SCREEN_ORIENTATION_LANDSCAPE), so opening any of those sheets after playback started threw. Fix, one scroller owns the column: the landscape panel is now a plain fillMaxSize Column and each sheet scrolls its own content; the four plain sheets (Speed, Quality, Sleep, SubtitleOffset) gained their own verticalScroll root so a long quality list still scrolls sideways. Portrait is untouched (ModalBottomSheet path). The other six first-run failures were test bugs, fixed in the same branch: the samplePosts helper wrote a leading space into titles with an empty prefix, below-fold assertions now scroll into view first, the filter sheet's Apply asserts existence (sheet opens partially expanded), Home asserts "Most copies" (Audit #18 dedupes the hero rail's titles out of the rail below, so its header never paints), and Languages uses the "Audio language: Hindi" content description. CI 43759607063 SUCCESS on cd043146, both jobs, 1948 tests with 0 failures (NestedScrollCrashTest 29/29). Not merged — parent merges.

**480p default start (branch muse/player-480p-default-20261116, 2026-11-16):** owner order 07:01 PKT 16 Nov — playback always starts at 480p unless the viewer set their own default quality. The decision point is the pure `resolveStartBand` in PlayerDefaults.kt (single call site: `PlayerViewModel.armQualityChoices`); the new precedence is explicit tap > saved fixed default > staged Auto band > 480p start (only when no default was ever picked and the ladder has a 480p rung) > first rung. The 480p start turns Auto off for the title, like a fixed default — the viewer can still switch up, or pick Auto, from the quality sheet. The subtlety the slice exists to honour: the repo's `defaultQuality` flow returns "auto" for BOTH "never picked" and "picked Auto", so a new `defaultQualitySet` flow (`preferences.contains(player_default_quality)`) tells them apart — a viewer who picked Auto keeps Auto, only the never-picked get 480p. No Settings UI change (the chips still show Auto selected when unset); no quality-gate interaction (rungs are gate-filtered before `resolveStartBand` runs, and 480p sits below the 720p free cap); Data Saver's mobile-data 480p cap still applies after, unchanged. Tests: PlayerDefaultsTest gains 4 cases (no saved default → 480p incl. blank band; no 480p rung → first rung; explicit tap still wins; saved 720p still wins) and the old `no default means Auto keeps its pick` test is renamed `an explicit Auto default keeps Auto's pick` — same assertions, the old name would now mislead. No golden changes (no UI touched). CI owed at push time; parent merges.

**Playback telemetry beacon + host ranking storage (branch muse/telemetry-beacon-20261116, 2026-11-16):** owner decision 20:25 PKT 16 Nov — YES, aggregates-only (per-host × network-type counters, no per-user/per-device history, no identity beyond what the API already sees, follows the existing analytics consent). App: one finished session per beacon — sid (random UUID), opaque stream handle, band, nominal rung bitrate, bytes + load wall time, first-load time (the closest Media3 1.3.1 exposes to TTFB), stalls + rebuffer ms after the first frame, outcome (played/failed/abandoned) + closed error class (only network/timeout blame the host), coarse network (wifi/mobile/none). Measured from the player's own load samples (autoQualityListener.feedSample) and state callbacks; a pure PlaybackBeaconRecorder (injectable clock + sid) decides the outcome at finish. Queued in SharedPreferences (cap 20, oldest shed, synchronous commit, Gson — never the framework org.json, which is a stub on the JVM), gated on Telemetry.consentAccepted, and ridden onto POST /api/v2/account/progress as a `playback_beacon` block beside the existing `usage` block — no new endpoint (the in-code law in `_note_client_usage` forbids a new public route for client-reported totals), acknowledged only on SyncAck.WRITTEN. Local-copy loads and handle-less loads start no session; the previous session finalises on every hop/rung change/end/destroy. No separate 5-minute heartbeat: the 15s progress cadence + forced pause/teardown writes already bound delivery to ≤15s after session end; persistence covers completed-but-unsent beacons, an in-flight session is lost on kill (same as the usage counters' pre-report window). Server: `record_playback_beacon` in usage_stats.py resolves each handle to `download_sources.service` via redact.parse_token(signed_only=True) and upserts one row per beacon into the new `usage_host_quality` table (day, host, net; 30-day window, 0.9/day decay, n ≥ 20 raw-plays floor; TTFB buckets, mean mtp derived from byte/load sums); forged, expired, bare-id and unresolvable handles are dropped and counted; the handle is never stored. `summary()` gains `playback_by_host`. Two bugs found and fixed in the build: the sid shape check reused the 32-char `_VALUE_RE` while a UUID is 36 chars (every valid beacon was dropped), and the aggregate divided decayed numerators by raw plays (now tracks decayed `plays_weighted` for all rates, raw plays only for the floor). Tests: Fast_Fetch/test_playback_beacon.py (27, all OK) + test_usage_stats schema pin (100 OK) + test_accounts_api (46 OK); PlaybackBeaconTest + PlaybackBeaconRecorderTest + beacon wire cases in ProgressUsageWireTest. CI green on the rebased tip 790e0474 (Android 43900995481, backend 43900995493), merged to main, both Oracle VM clones ff'd. Spec errors found: no `AnalyticsCollector` exists anywhere in App/ (the report's claim is wrong — measurement sources are the autoQualityListener samples + Player.Listener callbacks only); the app already fetches video bytes on Detail open (8 MiB first seed), so prefetching was not new — warm prepare is. Ranking use comes later; this slice is collection + storage only. NOT deployed live — the gate deploy waits for the post-autocrawl window (~21:30 PKT).
**Blogspot deadman-switch wiring (branch muse/blogspot-discovery-wire-20261116, 2026-11-16):** the app already had DynamicServerDiscovery (meta-tag parser, probe, persist) with zero call sites, and the gateway serves JSON, not meta tags — `{"status":"ok","primary":"http://92.4.95.252","backups":["https://backup1.yourdomain.com","https://backup2.yourdomain.com"],"v":"1.0.0"}` (stale: old http IP primary, placeholder backups). (1) Parser: hand-rolled JSON first (no org.json, plain-JVM-testable like Brand), meta tags kept as fallback; placeholders (yourdomain/example) dropped before probing; the gateway host itself is never a candidate. (2) Call site: RemoteConfigWatcher.refreshOnce()'s catch branch — the failure path of the poll the app already makes, on the background scope, never on launch, never a new poller; a 30-minute in-memory cooldown inside the switch keeps a long outage quiet. (3) Persistence rule: only an HTTPS candidate overwrites the saved primary (saveServerUrl); a plain-HTTP working candidate becomes a session-only in-memory override in ApiProvider (keyed to the saved value it was decided from, so a mid-session server change invalidates it; cleared on process death and by clearSessionServerUrl, which also drops the cached client). (4) Scope guard: recovery only runs when the configured server is one of ours (shipped default host or the new brand key network.fallback_server_url=http://92.4.95.252) — a viewer on their own catalog is never moved. (5) Probe kept: a candidate must answer /api/v1/posts?limit=1 with 200–399 before it is used or saved. Tests: DynamicServerDiscoveryTest gains JSON/meta/shape-selection/placeholder/persistable/our-server/cooldown cases (live payload included verbatim); new ApiProviderSessionFallbackTest (4 Robolectric cases) and RemoteConfigWatcherDiscoveryTest (failure attempts + saved unchanged, healthy never invokes, foreign never attempts — recording discovery pointed at unroutable 127.0.0.1:9, no real gateway). NOT unlocked by this slice: the http fallback cannot work in a RELEASE build as shipped — the release network policy permits cleartext for loopback hosts only (App/AGENTS.md §11); the owner decision to allow 92.4.95.252 is still owed; the security config was not touched. The blog itself was not changed (owner's action): it should carry primary https://raddstream.duckdns.org, backups ["http://92.4.95.252"] (raddstream.cc.cd joins only once that domain exists and points at the VM). No UI touched, no golden changes. CI owed at push time; parent merges.

**Field-test harness verification fixes (coordinator, same branch, 2026-11-16):** the builder's commit was verified in-diff against the server before push and 4 bugs were fixed here, not in the builder's commit. (1) `encodeFilename` returned "/plain.mp4" for a slash-less URL — `substringBeforeLast('/', "")` returns "" and the `head == url` guard never matched; now `lastIndexOf('/')` with an early return, matching the server's rpartition/`if not sep` exactly. (2) `percentEncode` used `Char.isLetterOrDigit()`, which accepts non-ASCII letters — byte 0xC3 leaked out as a raw 'Ã' instead of %C3; now ASCII letters/digits only, matching urllib quote's always-safe set. (3) The plus test asserted '+' stays '+', but the server's `quote(safe=".-_~")` encodes '+' as %2B — the "plus stays a plus" rule is on the decode side (unquote never turns '+' into a space); the test now expects %2B. (4) `HttpChainEngine.resolve` ran blocking OkHttp `execute()` calls on the ViewModel's Main thread — two 15 s POSTs + a probe per attempt would ANR the test phone, and no unit test would catch it (fake transport); the chain now runs inside `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`. All three encode cases were re-traced by hand against the server's `quote(unquote(tail), safe=".-_~")`.
**G-10 press/download test — harness extension (branch muse/field-test-harness-20261116, 2026-11-16):** second screen of the debug-only field-test harness, for the other phone (never opted in, never resolved, home Wi-Fi) after the parent banks the minted links. New package files in `com.raddstream.app.resolve`: PressModels.kt (PressRunHeader with `phase: "press"` + run kind, PressResult with press/mint epoch timestamps + post_id/link_id per row so the parent can check the server log on the VM), PressStats.kt (Wilson 95% interval, T-1/T-2/T-3 scorer, 15–17/20 repeat eligibility), PressPlaybackStats.kt (the ~50-line event→counter mapping: custom AnalyticsListener for first frame/rebuffers/dropped frames/bytes + PlaybackStatsListener for its own play-time/rebuffer totals), PressTestViewModel.kt (sequential 40-link run, one repeat run per eligible group), PressTestScreen.kt (second-phone note, control exclusion, repeat buttons), PressTestExport.kt (own JSON + summary with per-group/overall pass counts and Wilson intervals). Wiring only: `Screen.PressTest`, DEBUG-gated NavGraph entry, second button in the DEBUG Settings card, "Open press test" button on the Resolve Test screen, 29 new `press_test_*` strings. REAL PATHS REUSED (read first, no mint re-implemented): Play = Detail's `playBest`/`playPrint`/`playLadder` → `PlayStream(streamId, title)` → `PlayerViewModel.startStreamHandle` — the harness looks the handle up from `CatalogRepository.getPostDetail(postId, warm = false)` (warm OFF, or the lookup would pre-resolve the link), builds the URL with the same `streamRedirectUrl` + `withVipPass` helpers, and plays it on its own minimal ExoPlayer (released after every press and when the screen leaves); `CatalogRepository.playV2` is NOT on this path — it picks the server's winner for a print, while this test presses one sampled link by its own handle. Download = Detail's confirmKeep → `DeviceDownloadsRepository.enqueue(handle, title, quality)`, polled through the repository's downloads flow for the first byte, then `requestRemove` right after — never a full file. MEASUREMENT POINT (documented in the ViewModel KDoc and here): the app has NO in-app suspend call at press time that returns the 302 — `startStreamHandle` builds the redirector URL locally and the 302 happens inside the player — so mint-to-302 IS the duration of a no-follow GET to the exact play URL the player is about to load, issued once per press just before the player starts. Limits: it is a second stream hit per press (the log shows two banked stream hits per press: probe + player), and it measures the redirector's 302, not the player's internal redirect-follow; the 302 Location is recorded as the banked `minted_url`. Bars: T-1 mint-to-302 ≤ 100 ms, T-2 press-to-first-frame ≤ 2000 ms (via `onRenderedFirstFrame`, 30 s timeout, 5 s observation window after the frame), T-3 tap-to-first-byte ≤ 2000 ms. T-3 LIMIT: the first byte is observed through the repository's ~1 s-pace progress flush, so a sub-second first byte can read up to ~1 s late — an upper bound, never an understatement. The "no resolve log line" bar is NOT claimed on the phone (it cannot see the server log); the export records press/mint epoch timestamps for the parent's VM check, and the summary says so. Control links excluded (no banked direct link — 40 links, not 50). Tests (plain JVM + one Robolectric file for string resources): PressStatsTest (Wilson known values incl. 0/20 and 20/20, collector counter mapping, scorer + repeat boundaries 14/18 vs 15–17) and PressTestExportTest (JSON shape incl. phase/run-kind/minted URL/timestamps, summary pass counts + Wilson intervals). No Paparazzi goldens (debug-only screen). No local Gradle on this VM — CI (`ci.yml`: assembleDebug + testDebugUnitTest + lintDebug) is the gate; parent pushes and reviews the run. Do NOT run the field test from here — the owner runs it on the second phone on home Wi-Fi.

**Field-test harness fix after run 1 (branch muse/harness-fix-run1-20261116, 2026-11-16):** run 1 (owner's TECNO KF6p, Android 11, home Wi-Fi, 22:00–22:13 PKT; log in `results/field-test-run1-20261116.json`) minted 0/50 — the CONTROL set (filemoon + rpmplay, hosts that should mint) went 0/10, proving the harness, not the hosts, is broken. Fault 1: filepress 20/20 `downlaod: http:301` — `HttpChainEngine.apiCall` treated any non-200 as terminal and never followed redirects; it now follows 301/302/303/307/308 by re-POSTing the same JSON body to the resolved `Location` (5-hop cap, Referer re-based per hop; the FileBee mirrors rotate, so the 301 is the mirror moving, not a failure) and the labels now read `download:`/`download2:` (the wire spelling `indexDownlaod`/`/api/file/downlaod/` is unchanged, deliberately diverging from the server's `host_resolvers.py` vocabulary). Fault 2: WebView minted 0/30 — the detector only recognised media-extension URLs while these players stream extensionless playlists and .ts segments; it now records every subresource URL, reads `currentSrc` (not just `src` — hls.js/MediaSource leaves `src` empty) and the `performance` resource list, ranks candidates (DownloadListener URL → media extensions → extensionless media-marker URLs → other non-static) and Range-probes them inside the 30 s cap (4/round, 24 max); the first ACTIVE probe mints at once, and .ts/.m4s segments, the bridge URL, blocklisted hosts and static assets are never candidates. Fault 3: rpmplay 5/5 `other_host` — the guard aborted cross-host same-tab navigation, which is rpmplay's normal bridge flow; it now follows it and only refuses non-http(s) schemes. Secondary: the download-click JS now also matches French "télécharger" (1fichier) and anchors. Emulator verification (owner order 22:19 PKT): a "Run control only" button runs just the 10 control samples (~1–5 min, short enough for a Firebase Robo run), logcat reports per-attempt `RESOLVE_ATTEMPT` and end-of-run `RESOLVE_SUMMARY` lines (tag `ResolveTest`), and `App/docs/robo-resolve-test.json` drives the Robo run (Settings → Open resolve test → Run control only → wait for "Mint again" → terminate). Control must mint > 0 on the emulator before the owner re-runs; this branch claims no filepress/1fichier crack — the re-run will tell. Tests: 4 new redirect tests in `HttpChainEngineTest` (301 followed, relative Location, no-Location, redirect loop) plus new `WebViewDetectorTest` (ranking, navigation, extraction, and a local fixture page — JDK `HttpServer` serving a video page + mp4 + m3u8 + segment — whose candidates probe ACTIVE through the real transport while the segment never mints). **Screenshot fixes (branch muse/screenshot-fix-20261116, 2026-11-16):** owner photographed the real app on his TECNO KF6p (Android 11, mobile data, 0.5–25 KB/s) at 22:53–22:59 PKT — 18 screenshots, six real failures + design issues D1–D8. (1) Detail "Couldn't load this title" (Paradise, Kraven): the endpoints are healthy (v1 detail 55–89 KB, 200 in ~0.1 s) — the app opens detail via the v2 path when the row carries workId, and `GET /api/v2/works/8521` is **440,859 B** on the wire, so at the phone's 2.6–25 KB/s it runs 18–170 s against the 15 s OkHttp read timeout and the 4-attempt retry burns out. The real cause was nginx: `gzip_proxied any` and `gzip_types ... application/json` were commented out, so proxied JSON was never compressed. Nginx fix (ENABLED file only, backup /home/ubuntu/radd-stream.screenshot-fix-20261116.before): `gzip on; gzip_proxied any; gzip_comp_level 6; gzip_types application/json; gzip_vary on;` in both API server blocks — works detail now wires at **19,870 B** (was 440,859), live-tv channels at **29,157 B** (was 167,364). App-side: per-request timeout interceptor in ApiProvider (`readTimeoutSecondsForPath` — works 60 s, live-tv 45 s, v1 detail 30 s, everything else 15 s; ApiProviderTimeoutTest pins it). (2) Live TV empty screen: 759 channels serve fine (verified payload, 9 categories, zero dupes/missing fields) — the void was NOT reproducible from code (grid is always rendered when channels are non-empty; most probable runtime cause is the 167 KB fetch vs the 15 s timeout on the slow connection, and the ViewModel had NO retry). Fixes: `fetchChannelsWithRetry` in LiveTvViewModel (one silent retry on IOException, 1 s delay, max 2 attempts), the 45 s live-tv timeout + gzip above, and a real empty state (TV icon + Retry button, D3). New LiveTvRealPayloadTest parses the REAL server payload (test resource live-tv-channels-759.json, 167,364 B) via buildRaddGson: 759 channels, 9 categories in order, first Dunya News id 1, 759 unique ids, visibleChannels passes all 759 through, category filter keeps only news, cache round-trips all 759. (3) 429s on /api/v1/stream: OUR OWN nginx limit_req (zone 10 r/s, burst 30 on stream) — one Play press fires ~13 stream requests in one second plus concurrent art/detail calls sharing the zone; owner's IP had 101 429s, 94 on stream at 22:59, matching his "slow down" dialog. Fix: stream burst 30 → **60** in both API server blocks (rate 10 r/s unchanged — the follow-up lever if he still 429s on repeated presses). Verified: 20 rapid stream presses from the VM → all 400 (dummy id rejected upstream, as expected), **zero 429s**. App-side ladder still treats a 429 as a failed handle and tries the next one with no Retry-After honoring — a retry-storm follow-up, not in this branch. (1+8) FilterRail rebuilt: the Filters button is fixed at the row's left edge (it was the 6th item in the scrolling row, fully off-screen on a 360dp phone, so the sheet was undiscoverable without a swipe) and the five type chips scroll in the remaining space under Home's shared RowEndFade — the local 32dp fade is deleted (it painted, but chip fill → background is ~10 RGB steps on this palette, so it advertised nothing). The selected-chip auto-scroll is untouched. (3) Dead `suggestionsUnavailable` deleted — the flag was set in 7 places, read in 0 (grep), and its ViewModel comment ("the screen says so") contradicted the screen's Audit #34 deliberate silence; the suggest comment now says what the screen does (chips stay empty on failure). (4) Discovery loading state: `SearchUiState.discoveryLoading` (default true) flips false only when BOTH first loads settle (success or failure — a dead route settles, via `markDiscoverySettled` + the pure `discoveryLoading()` rule); while true and all three sections are empty, `SearchDiscoveryContent` shows `SearchDiscoverySkeleton` (hand-built rows — PosterRailSkeleton/PosterGridSkeleton are lazy and this column scrolls, the Robo #6 infinite-height crash) and the hint waits for the settle, so it only ever means the catalog is really empty. (2) NOT cut — no static mechanism exists: the outer Column is top-anchored (default Arrangement.Top), the Scaffold content is top-placed, the NavHost hosts Search directly, SearchField is a fixed 52dp pill, and the only Arrangement.Center in MainActivity is the pre-route loading screen — and the field is FIXED at y139–209 in all 7 frames while the rail moves, which kills any "whole block centered" theory (Gemini's 584px = 50% fit is suggestive, the code contradicts it). Layout Inspector checklist for the Robo 05:05 pass: (a) record title/field/rail/discovery-column top Y + heights, keyboard open vs closed — rail top must equal field bottom + 8dp; a taller-than-static node above the rail is the displacer; (b) record window height + IME inset per keyboard state — if the window shrinks by the keyboard height, adjustResize is resizing despite enableEdgeToEdge; (c) select SearchDiscoveryContent — height 0 or top below the viewport is the rendering defect (the unconditional hint proves it is layout, not data); if height > 0 and the hint node exists but is invisible, check isVisible/alpha/clip on its parents; (d) read the Scaffold's runtime contentPadding — top far above the ~24–31px status-bar inset is a double-apply (Home §3.3 precedent); (e) confirm the parent chain (NavHost → Scaffold content → Column) holds no centering Box/Arrangement — the static read says none exists, so one in the tree IS the mechanism. (7) Left alone: the 15s+15s serial search timeout is a one-line change in `readTimeoutSecondsForPath`, but the review says measure first and the file documents the 15s default saving slow-network attempts (owner's phone 2–25 KB/s) — cutting v2 to 8s without measurement could turn slow-but-working searches into errors. Parked, not built: voice search, inline back/cancel when focused (Gemini points for a later slice); Home's rail still uses ALL-CAPS + jade-fill tokens (this slice unified Search's rail with its own sheet + the nav pill only). Tests: SearchFilterRailTest rewritten (K-Pop scroll reveal, Filters fixed at rest with left edge 0dp, selected-chip scroll, fade tag on the shared RowEndFade), SearchDiscoveryTest +2 (skeleton while loading, sections win over skeleton when data exists; hint test now pins the settled state), new SearchDiscoveryLoadingTest (pure rule + default true). **Detail review fixes — buildable-now items 1–8 (branch muse/detail-fix-20261118, 2026-11-18):** the code-grounded Detail review (DETAIL-REVIEW-20261118.md, no P0) left 8 fixes buildable without device proof; all 8 landed here, item 9 is the Robo R1–R11 checklist (not code) and is NOT built. (1) Truncation honesty: `PostDetail` parses `release_total` / `releases_truncated` (v1) and `toPostDetail` passes `print_total` / `prints_truncated` through (v2) — both nullable, because Gson does not run Kotlin default initialisers for a missing key — with `isTruncated` / `totalReleases` derived helpers; the page shows one honest line above the episode/file list ("Showing the first 1,000 of 8,316 releases", resourced, grouped numbers) and the movie file expander counts the work's true total, not the capped list length. Per-season episode counts cannot be corrected from this signal (releases are not episodes; the v1 payload carries no per-season total) — the line is the disclosure, and plumbing v2's `WireDetailSeason.episode_count` through the layout builder is a recorded follow-up. (2) Genre-chips fade: the invisible local 32dp fade is deleted — `fillMaxHeight()` in a wrap-content Box inside a scrolling column collapses to 0px (Home §3.4), and the detailMovie golden shows the last chip as "E…" hard-clipped with no fade at all — and `GenreChipsRow` shares Home's `RowEndFade` at 22dp (a CapabilityChip Pill: labelSmall 11sp/16sp + 3dp vertical padding ×2); `RowEndFade` gained an optional `height: Dp = 48.dp` parameter, so Home/Search/Live TV keep 48dp. (3) `similarLoading`: the flag was set and never read — now it renders a rail skeleton (real "More Like This" header + `PosterRailSkeleton`, which carries its own 16dp sides) while the rail loads and the list is empty, instead of deleting the flag. (4) Touch-target floor: `heightIn(min = 48.dp)` on all five expanders ("Read more", "and N more", "Show all files" ×2 — the review listed four; the movie files expander is the same class and got the same floor — "Start over") and on both packed-banner buttons (M3 buttons are 40dp by default); the top-bar back/More targets went 40dp → 48dp circles, so there is no 40dp exception to record. (5) Locked downloads: the dead end's Download now targets the best KEEPABLE print for this viewer (`deadEndKeepPrint` — pure, gate allows its resolution with the operator's free cap + a keepable link, max rankKey) and disables when none is keepable, instead of offering the best-ranked print (which on a gated title can be a locked 4K copy or a provider page); `RungRow` disables (veiled, 0.38 alpha) the Download pad on a locked rung, with the signal threaded through `RungActions.isLocked` from the ViewModel's existing `isLocked` check (now internal). Note for the record: the locked-rung case is narrow in practice — the gated layout/ladder already remove premium prints/bands when the gate is on, and `premiumAccess` is true when the gate is off — so the live divergence is mainly the best-ranked print having no keepable link while another print does; the fix is still strictly more honest. (6) Skeleton reorder: `DetailSkeleton` now mirrors the redesigned page (hero, Play, synopsis, utility row, audio line, quality rungs, cast, print summary, similar) — the utility row is four 48dp icon+label skeleton cells, the audio line one 48dp row — and `SkeletonParityTest` pins the section order by the skeleton's own testTags. No series episode placeholder: the screen does not know movie-vs-series until the load lands (recorded follow-up). (7) Season dropdown chevron: `Icons.Default.ArrowDropDown` instead of the "▾" text glyph. (8) Episode row "Downloading" state: `observeDownloads` now also collects QUEUED + DOWNLOADING handles into `downloadingHandles` (PAUSED stays unmarked — it is not moving) and the row says "Downloading" while its keep runs. Tests: ModelsTest +2 (v1 truncation decode + missing-key fallback), V2CatalogWireTest +4 asserts (v2 passthrough), DetailDeadEndReasonTest +4 (best keepable beats best-ranked locked, VIP keeps best-ranked, null when nothing keepable, page is not keepable), QualityRungCardTest +1 (locked rung Download disabled, unlocked stays enabled), DetailRedesignTest +7 (genre fade 22dp, truncation line, true-total file count, similar skeleton, episode Downloading, dead-end targets keepable print, dead-end disables when nothing keepable) + the chevron pin in the dropdown test, SkeletonParityTest +1 (section order), new DetailTouchTargetTest (every TextButton carries the floor; top-bar 48dp circles + both packed-banner buttons). Paparazzi: only the detailMovie golden is expected to change (the genre fade now actually paints); record run (workflow 418582550, numeric id) + CI re-run owed on the pushed tip. **R3 segmented downloads + Media3 HLS keeps (branch muse/segmented-downloads-20261118, 2026-11-18):** from ~/workspace/playback-download-research-20261118.md §R3 (R5/R7 cache design). File downloads: `SegmentedDownload.kt` — `planSegments` (remainder spread, 256 KB minimum segment, hard cap 8), `SegmentJournal` (`total|idx:start-end:done,...`, corrupt/gapped/overlapping → null, ranges must tile [0,total)), `segmentCountFor` (4 segments only on unmetered Wi-Fi with a file worth splitting, else 1), `SegmentedDownloader` (supervisorScope, per-segment retry 3 with exponential backoff honouring Retry-After, per-segment RandomAccessFile handles, journal snapshot in the progress callback), `OkHttpSegmentFetcher` (1-byte probe `Range: bytes=0-0`; 206 → range OK; 200/403 → single-connection fallback; 404/410 → source dead; 429 → Retry-After). `DownloadService.download()` dispatches to `downloadSegmented()` (temp file `cacheDir/segmented/<id>.tmp`, pre-allocated, MediaStore entry created only at merge time) or the old body as `downloadSingle()`; a single-connection resume offset (bytes already in the public file, no journal) stays single so segmenting never throws a head-start away. `DeviceDownloadsRepository` gains `DeviceDownloadState.PARTIAL` (6th state; canResume; PARTIAL → requestResume; `markPartial`; journal prefs `segments:<id>`; `removeEntry`/`resetResume` clear the journal; `toUi` shows the failure reason for PARTIAL too). A partial file is NEVER marked READY — the merge runs the same `completionDefect` gate as the single path, and PARTIAL keeps its bytes + journal so Resume retries only the missing segments. HLS keeps: new `MediaDownloadCache` (one SimpleCache in `filesDir/media_downloads`, NoOpCacheEvictor — a keep must never be LRU-evicted — StandaloneDatabaseProvider, DownloadManager maxParallelDownloads=2), `HlsKeepDownloader` (enqueue/stateFor/isComplete/manifestUrlFor/pause/remove/drive; `drive` re-adds a FAILED download with the same id to resume from cached segments; classifyFailure: 402 + 0 bytes → Gated, 404/410/403 → SourceDead, else Failed; pure `mapHlsKeepState` — stopped → PAUSED, REMOVED → NOT_STARTED), `Media3HlsDownloadService` (foreground notification id 7103, `getScheduler()` = null — coordinator re-drives on its tick), `CacheCoordinator.runHlsPass` routes FULL_DOWNLOAD HLS keeps to Media3 (free-disk gate first; outcomes map to COMPLETED/RETRY_LATER/NEEDS_RERESOLVE/GATED), `cancelTask` also removes the Media3 download, `OfflineCacheEngine.serveUri` serves a completed Media3 keep from its manifest URL (no loopback proxy, no file row) and `hasCommittedFile` ORs with `isComplete`. `PlaybackService` wraps its HTTP factory in `MediaDownloadCache.playbackFactory` (read-only — playback never writes to the download store). Manifest registers the service (foregroundServiceType dataSync); `media3-datasource` added explicitly; Media3 stays 1.3.1 (upgrade NOT authorised). Per-host caps: 4 parallel connections only on unmetered Wi-Fi, never against a host that answered 403, Retry-After honoured. Tests: `SegmentedDownloadTest` (plan/journal/engine with a fake fetcher + the real OkHttp fetcher through an in-memory Range interceptor; resume skips done segments; 206-fallback; 403-fallback; PARTIAL-never-READY via the merge gate) and `HlsKeepDownloadStateTest` (pure state mapping). No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Parent merges.

**MX Player idea #1 — FFmpeg software audio decoder (branch muse/mx-ffmpeg-audio-20261118, 2026-11-18):** the "each movie and all kind of format play" fix — titles with AC-3/E-AC-3/DTS/TrueHD audio that today show the give-up card will play. Player: `PlaybackService`'s `DefaultRenderersFactory` gets `setExtensionRendererMode(EXTENSION_RENDERER_MODE_PREFER)`; the FFmpeg audio renderer only ever claims the five formats it knows, so AAC/MP3 and everything else stays on MediaCodec exactly as before. Failover: new `FailoverDecision.RetryWithSoftwareDecoder` — on `ERROR_CODE_DECODING_FAILED` the machine retries the SAME rendition once with the software decoder (the S2 exception: a decode failure is a decoder problem, not a dead copy) before hopping to another copy; one per rendition, no backoff, and it does not touch the retry_same budget. New `FfmpegSupport` answers availability by reflection (`FfmpegLibrary.isAvailable()`), so the app compiles and runs with or without the AAR. `humanizeErrorSummary` now maps `ERROR_CODE_DECODING_FAILED` to "This device could not play this video." (it previously fell to the generic message — "DECODING_FAILED" holds no "DECODER" substring). Tests: new `FfmpegSoftwareRetryTest` (8 — SW retry before/after first frame, hop when no SW decoder, second failure hops, last-rank retry-then-handoff, non-decode failures do not spend the retry, retry_same budget untouched, humanized message). Native build: the extension is NOT on Maven — `App/scripts/build-ffmpeg-aar.sh` clones Media3 1.3.1 + FFmpeg release/6.0 (GitHub mirror), builds the static libs with the trimmed `App/scripts/build-ffmpeg.sh` (a verbatim trim of upstream's `build_ffmpeg.sh`, arm64-v8a + armeabi-v7a only, x86/x86_64 blocks removed), patches the module to the two ARM ABIs, builds `:lib-decoder-ffmpeg:assembleRelease`, and drops the AAR at `App/app/libs/media3-ffmpeg-1.3.1.aar`; it is idempotent (skips a verified AAR) and FAILS LOUDLY if it cannot produce one, and verifies the AAR holds exactly the two `libffmpegJNI.so` files. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, both jobs): SDK gains `platforms;android-34`, `cmake;3.22.1`, `ndk;26.2.11394342` (r26b); AAR cache keyed on the two scripts; FFmpeg build step before Gradle; build summary reports the AAR size and both `.so` sizes inside the APK; both job timeouts 45 → 60 min (cold-cache native build). Gradle: conditional `files("libs/media3-ffmpeg-1.3.1.aar")` dependency (warns when absent; a build without the AAR still compiles and plays as before). `.gitignore` gains `App/app/libs/`. LGPL: `App/ffmpeg/NOTICE.md` — the five decoders are LGPL only (no GPL components), build scripts in-repo for rebuild/replace; owner may want a legal review before shipping. Corrections to the report's spec, verified against Media3 1.3.1 source: (1) the DTS decoder is `dca`, not `dts` — `--enable-decoder=dts` would fail configure; (2) the JNI wrapper is built by Gradle+CMake, not ndk-build (`build_ffmpeg.sh` only builds the FFmpeg static libs); (3) `FfmpegLibrary.getCodecName` has no `audio/mlp` mapping, so the FFmpeg renderer will not claim standalone MLP tracks even with the `mlp` decoder built (included anyway, tiny). Push + CI verdict owed on this tip — the native FFmpeg build step is the validation (if it is not feasible in CI, report the evidence and the best alternative instead of forcing it); APK size delta vs the ~23 MB main baseline is measured from the CI summary, not estimated. Parent merges. No local Gradle — CI is the gate.

**MX Player idea #1 — CI fixup 1 (same branch, 2026-11-18):** Android CI 44377426180 on c62cd953 failed in 1m57s in BOTH jobs at the new FFmpeg AAR build step — the fail-loud design worked (the app never built without the decoder). Root cause, two parts, both in the scripts: (1) FFmpeg 6.0's configure probes for nasm/yasm even for ARM targets (x86asm is enabled by default) and DIES if neither is installed — the GitHub ubuntu-24.04 runner ships no nasm, and the log shows the first configure dying 1.5 s in with "nasm/yasm not found or too old. Use --disable-x86asm for a crippled build." Verified in FFmpeg 6.0's configure source (the probe at line 11876, inside `elif enabled x86`, gated on `! disabled_any asm mmx x86asm` — disabling x86asm skips it). Fix: `--disable-x86asm` added to COMMON_OPTIONS in the trimmed build-ffmpeg.sh, recorded in its header as the ONE deliberate deviation from upstream — for an ARM-only build it is not a cripple (no x86 assembly exists in an ARM library; ARM/NEON assembly is unaffected). Upstream's script omits it because Media3's environment has nasm. (2) The NDK precedence was wrong: the driver script let ANDROID_NDK_HOME win, and setup-android sets it to the latest preinstalled NDK (27.3.13750724 in the log) instead of the pinned r26b. Fix: the pinned `$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/26.2.11394342` is preferred when installed; ANDROID_NDK_HOME is only a fallback. Pre-push checks passed; push + CI verdict owed on the fixup tip; parent merges. No local Gradle — CI is the gate.

**MX Player idea #1 — CI fixup 2 (same branch, 2026-11-18):** Android CI 44380041485 on 224b7e12 failed again in both jobs at the FFmpeg AAR build with the SAME "nasm/yasm not found" error — even though --disable-x86asm was in the pushed script (and the NDK fix worked: the log shows r26b). Root cause is NOT nasm at all: a truly blank line after a `\` continuation TERMINATES the command in bash (proven with a minimal test: `echo foo \` + blank line + `bar` prints only "foo", then "bar: command not found"). My trimmed build-ffmpeg.sh had blank lines between the \-continued ./configure option lines, so `./configure` ran with NO arguments — configure defaulted to the HOST arch (x86_64), enabled x86, and died on the nasm probe before ever seeing --arch=arm or --disable-x86asm. Proven with a fake-configure harness (bash -x showed `+ ./configure` with zero args, then `--libdir=...: No such file or directory`). Fix: the two ./configure blocks are reflowed with no blank lines (verified with the same harness — the configure now receives --arch=arm, --cpu=armv7-a, --disable-x86asm and all five --enable-decoder flags), and the script header records this as Deviation 2. A scan confirms no `\`-then-blank-line remains in either script. Note: the "verbatim trim" claim in fixup 1's entry is corrected — the upstream rendering showed blank lines, but they cannot be in a working script. Pre-push checks passed; push + CI verdict owed on the fixup tip; parent merges. No local Gradle — CI is the gate.
