**Feel-instant S8 — Catalog preload, done safely (branch muse/feel-instant-s8-20261119, 2026-11-19):** preload the ANSWERS, not the catalog — the client-side twin of the server's 21:00 top-100 pre-warm. (1) `CatalogWarmWorker` (new `work/`, @HiltWorker CoroutineWorker, daily, KEEP): in the overnight window (UNMETERED + charging + idle + battery-not-low + storage-not-low — the spec's five constraints, all kept; the trade-off is documented in code, a phone rarely charging on Wi-Fi overnight simply never warms and the app behaves exactly as before S8) it fetches every warmable Home rail's first page (7 rails: 5 static + 2 regional; panel-managed and related rails excluded — the worker cannot fetch either) through the same v2-first chain Home's loadSection runs (`fetchRailFirstPage`, pure and tested: v2 hit, v2 null/empty/throw → fallback, trending rail tries the dedicated trending route then v1, related rails use their own route, CancellationException rethrown never swallowed). Each fetch warms the OkHttp disk cache (S1) and upserts titles into FTS (S3c) through the repository's own `cachePosts`; the first two posters per rail are prefetched via the S2 helper (14 urls, under the 20 cap, metered gate included). Sequential, not parallel like Home — nobody waits on this run. One dead rail never stops the others; a failure never retries (next day covers it, same rule as CacheSweepWorker). (2) `CatalogIndexSyncWorker` (same shape): the S3c Phase 2 delta sync — pages v2 trending by cursor (popularity order, the FTS ranking) until the 5,000-title cap, a short page, or a page the server cannot serve; v2 null on the first page falls back to v1 page-numbered for the whole run, v2 dying mid-run stops instead of switching (a switch would re-seed from the top and duplicate banked pages), a null cursor with hasMore true stops after its page. The 5k cap is the S3c size math (top 5k ≈ 0.6 MB raw / ~1–1.5 MB indexed, inside the ≤ 2 MB/day budget A11); the 20k tier and the dedicated catalog-index endpoint (§5.2) do not exist yet and are a follow-up — no server endpoint was invented. (3) Connection warm moved earlier: `HomeViewModel.init` now launches `warmConnectionIfNeeded()` at Home first paint, once per process (repository AtomicBoolean guard); Detail keeps its own call as the deep-link backstop. (4) Wiring: `CatalogPreloadCatalog` interface + `ApiCatalogPreloadCatalog` (Hilt @Binds via `CatalogPreloadModule`, mirroring FollowSeriesModule), both workers enqueued in `RaddStreamApplication.onCreate` with `enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(KEEP)` next to CacheSweep/FollowSeries. No new permissions, no manifest change, no WorkManager bump (app pins 2.9.0; research found 2.11.0 latest, noted only), no DB schema change. Tests (Robolectric, mirroring CacheSweepWorkerTest/FollowSeriesWorkerTest): `CatalogPreloadTest` (constraints pin, warmable-sections filter, daily request interval via workSpec), `CatalogWarmWorkerTest` (warm across all 7 rails, dead-rail skip, empty-rail skip, 6 chain tests, Hilt factory pin), `CatalogIndexSyncWorkerTest` (cursor chain, 5,000 cap, mid-run death keeps banked pages, v1 fallback, withheld cursor, Hilt factory pin). The two new Robolectric worker tests join the arch-conditioned exclusion in build.gradle.kts (same TestListenableWorkerBuilder machinery as the excluded CacheSweepWorkerTest; CI is x86_64 and runs them). CI rounds: first check failed on 3 compile errors (player_cast string removed by the cinema slice — now `detail_cast`; a doubled @Composable from the SeasonRow insert; SeasonKeepConfirmDialog's missing wifiOnly) + one test-compile error (`SemanticsConfiguration` has no getOrNull — now `contains`, then `assertIsNotEnabled`); then 3 test failures (CatalogGridRule + CardGeometryTest — the season grid is rows of six in a LazyColumn now, tile shape is `CardGeometry.SEASON_TILE_ASPECT`). No local Gradle — CI is the gate; push + CI verdict owed on the branch tip; parent merges.

**Feel-instant S7 — Startup diet + baseline profile (branch muse/feel-instant-s7-20261119, 2026-11-19):** research first (3 wide searches + Android docs): layered init (critical / background / IdleHandler), baseline profile via `com.android.test` module + `androidx.baselineprofile` plugin, R8 full mode default since AGP 8.0. (1) Deferred startup: new `DeferredStartup` (exactly-once AtomicBoolean guard; a throwing step is logged and the rest still run) owns the half of `Application.onCreate` that may wait — `cacheEngineRunner.start()`, `lanShareRunner.start()`, `syncAccountRepository.startEntitlementWatch()` + `ensureDeviceTrialAtLaunch`, and `deviceDownloadsRepository.autoResumeInterrupted()` (the last is an audit extra the spec did not name: it reads the download ledger from disk on the calling thread). `MainActivity` starts it once via `decorView.doOnPreDraw` + `post` (runs after the first frame's traversal; doOnPreDraw waits for attach, so it cannot miss on cold start). Fallback: a 5 s timer in the Application starts it anyway for a process that never draws a frame (PlaybackService/worker start) — safe either way because every `CacheEngineHolder.engine` reader null-checks it. Stays on the critical path, with reasons in code: `Brand.load` + `CrashReporting`, `Telemetry` (already backgrounded), `keepTtlHolder` + `imageSizingHolder` (the first frame reads what they seed), `remoteConfigWatcher` (maintenance mode must cover the whole app from the first paint), WorkManager enqueues. Tests: new `DeferredStartupTest` (5 — order, exactly-once, throw-does-not-stop-rest, throw-still-counts-as-started, empty list), plain JVM. (2) Baseline profile module: new `:baselineprofile` (`com.android.test`, `targetProjectPath = ":app"`, AGP 8.5.2) with `BaselineProfileGenerator` — `startup` + `homeSearchDetail` (Home → Search tab → type "One Piece" → tap the first result by its announced title → Detail → back), both `includeInStartupProfile = true`. Versions (verified against AndroidX release notes + Google Maven metadata): benchmark 1.4.1 (plugin + macro-junit4, one train; 1.5.0 exists but is a month old), UiAutomator 2.3.0 (pairs with androidx-test 1.6.1), ext-junit 1.2.1, runner 1.6.2. App module applies the plugin + `baselineProfile(project(":baselineprofile"))`. The generator deliberately does NOT tap the disclaimer ("I understand") — it fails telling the operator to accept it once by hand; it does tap "Skip for now" on the analytics sheet (answers nothing). Generation itself (`:app:generateBaselineProfile`) is a device run and is OWED — CI only compiles + packages the module via the new `:baselineprofile:assembleDebug` step in ci.yml (header comment updated: `:app` is no longer the only module). The generated `baseline-prof.txt` is not in this slice (no device); regenerate per release. (3) shrinkResources: ALREADY `true` in the release build type (line ~290) — verified, not re-added; the spec's ask was already met. (4) R8 full mode: EVALUATED, stays OFF — `android.enableR8.fullMode=false` is left as-is. The unit suite runs debug builds (minify off), so green tests would not validate full mode at all, and the app's reflection-heavy paths (Gson models, Media3/FfmpegSupport reflective lookup) are exactly the class full mode breaks; the real gate is a release build + device smoke test, which is owed. (5) Release APK size: NOT measurable from CI — ci.yml builds debug only, and a release build needs the owner's tag (release.yml). **MX idea #3 — one-tap HW/SW decoder switch (branch muse/mx-decoder-switch-20261119, 2026-11-19):** MX parity for the player: a HW/SW chip in the top-right TopBar (after the print-sheet button, same shape as the speed pill) that toggles the video decoder with one tap, and a live rebuild of the player in the other mode that keeps position and play/pause state. Research first (standing order): Media3 has no API to swap a RenderersFactory on a live player — the switch rebuilds the player; MediaSession.setPlayer (same application looper) re-points the session so the MediaController never rebinds; software decode is a custom MediaCodecSelector (setMediaCodecSelector), not an extension mode (OFF=0/ON=1/PREFER=2); no HW+ exists in Media3 — MX's HW+ is its own framework, so only HW/SW are offered, and the code says so. Two modes: HW = MediaCodecSelector.DEFAULT, SW = SoftwareMediaCodecSelector (delegates to DEFAULT, keeps software decoders — API 29+ MediaCodecInfo.softwareOnly, below 29 the OMX.google./c2.android. name heuristic — falls back to the full list when a format has no software decoder, so a title is never unplayable for want of one). The FFmpeg audio extension stays PREFER in both modes (audio-only; #1's automatic retry depends on it) — the switch moves the VIDEO decoder path, documented in DecoderMode.kt. Persistence: player_decoder_mode in DataStore (ServerSettingsRepository.decoderMode/saveDecoderMode, enum-name contract like viewModeChoice); PlayerSessionStore.decoderMode is the in-process truth; ViewModel loads the pref at init, toggles via toggleDecoderMode() (mirrored var, no double-tap race), service builds in store.decoderMode.value at onCreate and collects it for live rebuilds (buildPlayer(mode) factored out of onCreate; rebuildPlayer releases the old player, builds the new one, re-attaches both listeners, setPlayer, reloads the active rendition at the saved position with countAsAttempt=false and restores playWhenReady — a paused viewer stays paused; an ended player restarts from 0; a rebuild before the first load just swaps the idle player). Graceful failure: FailoverDecision.RetryWithOtherDecoderMode — fires on a decode failure after #1's audio retry is spent, or at once when no FFmpeg AAR is present; once per rendition, does not touch retry_same; the service sets the store mode (ephemeral — the persisted preference is NOT overwritten) and announces "Hardware decoding failed — switched to software decoding" (or the reverse) in the settled banner's 5s transient; if the other mode also fails to decode, the machine falls through to the ordinary hop path. #1's automatic retry is byte-for-byte unchanged in behaviour when available (first decode failure still RetryWithSoftwareDecoder); the three #1 tests whose expectations the new middle step changes are updated (second failure is now the mode fallback, third hops/hands off). Tests: new DecoderModeTest (4), SoftwareMediaCodecSelectorTest (7: predicate on both SDK branches, selector filtering, empty-list fallback, mode-to-selector mapping), DecoderModeFallbackTest (7), +1 store banner test, +2 PlayerMockupTest chip tests (shows HW + toggles; shows SW in software mode); PaparazziPreviewTest + PlayerMockupTest TopBar call sites updated for the new onToggleDecoderMode param (the playerTopBar goldens will change — a record run is expected). Known limits: a kept copy playing reloads from the live link after a rebuild (same bytes, different source); in Ghost mode the chip is hidden with the rest of the chrome (leave Ghost to toggle); a decode failure cannot say whether audio or video failed, so an audio-undecodable title spends the mode fallback once before hopping; no DataStore round-trip test for the repository row (no harness exists — same as viewModeChoice). Pre-push checks passed; push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges. No local Gradle — CI is the gate.

**MX idea #5 — subtitle gestures + full ASS styling (branch muse/mx-subtitles-20261119, 2026-11-19):** MX parity for subtitles, built on the existing two-path renderer (native SubtitleView + custom overlay). Research first (standing order): (a) Media3 1.3.1 already parses ASS natively (SsaParser) and `setApplyEmbeddedStyles` is on by default — the app deliberately turns it off (Robo run 4: dark fansub styles render black-on-black); (b) libass has NO viable free prebuilt path — no Maven Central AAR, it is a C library (FreeType + FriBidi + HarfBuzz) needing an NDK build per ABI under LGPL, and the only GitHub ASS renderers (averyzhong/SubtitleForAndroid) are dead (JCenter, target SDK 28). Verdict, honest: no native libass build — ASS styling is delivered two ways instead: a viewer toggle that hands the native view back to Media3's parsed styles, and a pure-Kotlin ASS parser for external files rendered as overlay spans. (1) `AssParser.kt` (pure Kotlin, JVM-tested): Script Info (PlayResX/Y), V4+ Styles (Format-driven columns), Events Dialogue (Format-driven, text kept whole past its 9th comma); override tags `\b \i \u \s \c \1c \fs \an \pos \r` (+ named-style reset); `\N`/`\n`/`\h`; colours `&HAABBGGRR&` converted (inverted alpha, BGR order) with a dark-colour guard (Rec.709 luminance < 0.35 falls back to the viewer's colour — the Robo run-4 rule); malformed lines skipped, never thrown. Deliberately NOT done: karaoke timing, fades/movement/rotation/clipping/drawing, embedded fonts (`\fn` — not installed), `\2c/\3c/\4c` — all documented in the file header. (2) Common overlay model (`OverlayCues.kt`): `OverlaySubtitleFile` implemented by both `SubtitleFile` (SRT/VTT, one plain run) and `AssFile` (styled runs, placement, style weight); `SubtitleLineJump` (next = strictly greater start — no grace window, which would skip a line about to start; prev = restart-the-line past 1s else the line before, gap = the line just shown). (3) Routing: `.ass/.ssa` now go to the overlay (`isCustomRenderable` + `SubtitleFormat.Ass` + `parseOverlay` dispatch; `SubtitleParser.parse` throws on Ass with a pointer to parseOverlay, so the two models cannot be confused). (4) Styling controls in the existing subtitle sheet, no new screen: font chips (Default/Serif/Monospace), edge chips (None/Outline/Shadow — outline is a true stroke natively, a stroke-behind + fill double-draw on the overlay, documented as an approximation), and the "Use the file's own subtitle styling" switch (default OFF, `setApplyEmbeddedStyles(true)` + `setApplyEmbeddedFontSizes(true)`). All three persisted in DataStore like the other five style keys (`subtitleStyleOf` + `saveSubtitleStyle` extended; unreadable names fall back to defaults). The overlay renders ASS runs as AnnotatedString spans (colour/weight/italic/underline/strike, `\fs` scale on top of the style size and the viewer's sizePercent), `\an` 9-grid placement, `\pos` absolute offset from the alignment anchor, MarginV, and the file's style weight — the viewer's bold only fills in where the file says nothing (SRT/VTT). (5) Gestures, all inside the subtitle strip (bottom 30%, centre third; pure functions in `PlayerGestures.kt`, gated on `lockGestures` only — they work in Ghost): two-finger horizontal swipe → delay, one coarse step (500 ms) per 10% width with sub-step banking across callbacks; pinch on the strip → size live (±10/callback, 50..200); vertical drag on the strip → seat moves with the finger (local accumulation, so a frame-lagged state read cannot drop the drag); vertical flick (≤300 ms, ≥48 px, ≥500 px/s) → previous/next subtitle line, with the live move undone first. Readout is a `Hud.Subtitle` pill (same shape/seat/lifetime as the scrub toast; the value travels from the lane and the label is formatted where drawn, since lanes cannot call stringResource). Line jump is overlay-only — the native path has no cue list, so it says so out loud instead of pretending. Tests: `AssParserTest` (13 — styles, dialogue, overrides, `\an`/`\pos`, colours incl. alpha/BGR, dark guard, delay, malformed tolerance, style carry-through), `SubtitleLineJumpTest` (11), `SubtitleGesturesTest` (8 — zone, re-time steps, size delta, move fraction, fling classifier), `SubtitleStylePersistenceTest` extended (new fields round-trip, unknown names fall back, wire-name/label uniqueness). Pre-push checks passed; push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges. No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Owed: device verify (gestures on a real phone, ASS file rendering, outline look); the karaoke-timing loss is the one visible ASS gap (words still render, just un-timed).

**MX Player idea #7 — Kids Lock (branch muse/mx-kids-lock-20261119, 2026-11-19):** a child-safe mode a parent switches on with a 4-digit PIN. Research first (`RESEARCH-kids-lock-20261119.md` in the worktree root): MX Player's Kids Lock is a player lock (touch 4 corners clockwise), not a content filter; Netflix Kids is a dedicated profile (titles ≤12 only, unrated titles vanish) + a Profile Lock PIN on adult profiles; YouTube Kids is an allowlist by age band + a parent PIN for settings/exit. The common pattern — 4-digit PIN, enter twice to set up, once to exit, allowlist not denylist, locked surfaces — is what this build follows. Wire facts measured first: the public port never carries `is_18_plus` (the server hides flagged rows from fresh reads — layer 0); the app knows flags only for kept rows via `AdultPolicy`; a `Post` carries genres (CSV/JSON-array string), contentType, isAnimated, year, imdbRating (a score, not maturity) — no maturity/certification field, no `kid_safe` projection. The rule is two layers: (1) hard — a flagged or refused row never lists even with friendly genres; (2) heuristic, documented as such — genre allowlist Animation, Family, Kids, Children, Cartoon, Comedy, Adventure, Fantasy, Musical, Documentary, Educational, Sport (intersection, one kids genre suffices; no known genre = NOT appropriate, fail closed; `isAnimated` alone is not a pass). Honest limit: the genre rule shapes browsing, not a maturity rating — a mainstream R-rated comedy in the Comedy genre is the known residual; the real fix is a server-side maturity signal (follow-up, not v1). D1 pure rules (`viewmodel/KidsLock.kt`: PIN format, SHA-256 `salt:pin` hash, verify, genre rule, `filterPosts`, 5-failures → 30 s throttle) + `KidsLockTest` (plain JUnit). D2 storage (`ServerSettingsRepository`: `kids_lock_pin_hash` / `kids_lock_salt` (UUID minted at setup) / `kids_mode_active` DataStore flows; PIN never plaintext; client-only, no new endpoint). D3 controller (`KidsLockViewModel`, Hilt: setup/change/enter/exit/remove, sealed `KidsPinOutcome`, in-memory throttle). D4 Settings "Family" card + `PinPadDialog` (own numeric pad, dots, no keyboard; step machine SETUP_FIRST/CONFIRM, ENTER, EXIT, CHANGE_CURRENT/NEW/CONFIRM, REMOVE; no-reset warning on the card). D5 shell (MainActivity collects `kidsModeActive` → NavGraph): bottom bar shrinks to Home/Search/Settings (My List's unfiltered saves and unrated Live TV leave the bar); entering kids mode pops everything above Home off the stack; Settings opens only behind a session-scoped PIN challenge that renders over an empty screen (never the Settings content behind the dialog); Home wears a slim "Kids Mode is on — Exit" banner (PIN to exit). D6 filtering: Home/Browse/Search read through `visible*` state views (raw lists stay whole underneath, so turning the mode off restores the full screen with no re-fetch); Search + Browse Pagers rebuild on the flag flip with `PagingData.filter`; recents/suggestions/local echo/trending/recommended read empty in kids mode and a kid's searches never join the shared recents store; Detail refuses a non-appropriate title ("Not available in Kids Mode", no title/poster/Play/retry) and gates the optimistic header, similar titles and all keep/download actions; `KidsModeStateTest` pins the state views. D7 player: a new episode starts locked in kids mode (rung switches never re-lock mid-play), the PIN grant is per-title, turning the mode on mid-play locks a running player at once, and the unlock FAB's tap raises the PIN pad (`PlayerEvent.RequestKidsPin`); Ghost mode untouched and the FAB is ungated by it, so the pad is always reachable. D8 adult mode unchanged by construction — every gate reads the flag, default off, DataStore read seeds off on failure. Strings are hardcoded literals, matching the Settings/Home/Detail convention (no strings.xml churn). Known cosmetic gap: Search's count line still reads the server's unfiltered total next to the filtered loaded count (the line names the loaded count truthfully; the file's own comment already says the two numbers never agree). Pre-push checks passed; push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges. No local Gradle — CI is the gate. **MX Player idea #8 — 200% volume + equalizer (branch muse/mx-volume-eq-20261119, 2026-11-19):** Research first (`RESEARCH-volume-eq-20261119.md`): Media3 1.3.1 ships no gain/EQ AudioProcessor and no `ExoPlayer.Builder.setAudioProcessors` — injection is via a `DefaultRenderersFactory.buildAudioSink` override; LoudnessEnhancer/DynamicsProcessing/Equalizer are session-scoped AudioEffects (device-dependent, no EQ, colours every app), so the build is custom. One `BaseAudioProcessor` subclass (`EnhancementAudioProcessor`, in the sink chain): PCM 16/24/32-bit/float → float → ×dspGain → 5 RBJ biquads (60 Hz low shelf, 230/910/3600 Hz peaking Q 1.0, 14 kHz high shelf) → rational soft clip (identity to ±1.0, asymptotes at ±2.0) → float out; output format always PCM float, so gain/EQ moves apply live. Gain split (`splitTotalGain`, tested): total = level × userVolume, player half = min(total, 1), DSP half = total/player half (1..2); product is exactly the requested total. `AudioBoostUi.SOFTWARE_GAIN_AVAILABLE` flipped to true — the one value the old ceiling code waited for — so the slider now offers the full 0..200% and `honestSummary` states the applied total ("Volume 150%"). EQ: 5 presets (Flat, Normal, Bass Boost, Treble Boost, Vocal) + Custom, ±12 dB sliders, persisted in DataStore as one string (`player_eq_state`), applied live. UI: one row in the More sheet's Audio section (shows the current preset) opening an EQ sheet — no new TopBar button (chrome diet); 18 new `player_*` strings, all unique and used. Wiring: `PlayerSessionStore.audioEnhancement` flow (decoder-mode pattern), `PlaybackService` owns the single processor instance and re-injects it on every live rebuild (HW/SW switch keeps the mix and the position); the ViewModel pushes level + EQ to the store and persists both. Kids Lock: the EQ row lives behind the chrome gate — locked players never compose the More button, so no separate lock check. Float-error note: the 0 dB chain is the identity to ~4e-05 worst case (verified by a numpy float32 simulation of the exact recurrence; constant input is exact 0), so the identity tests use a 1e-4 delta. Tests: `EqBiquadTest` (9), `EqualizerSettingsTest` (14), `EnhancementAudioProcessorTest` (10, Robolectric: configure/format, identity, gain 2, soft clip, +6 dB tone, partial-frame stash, flush, live settings, unsupported encoding, unconfigured consume); `AudioBoostCeilingTest` rewritten to the flipped premise and `PlayerPolicyBridgeTest` honestSummary updated (150%/200% now, no ceiling sentence). Pre-push checks passed; push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges. No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Known limits: 200% on an already-loud master still compresses (soft clip tames it, does not create headroom); the chain always runs through float even when off. Owed: device verify (listen for distortion at 200% on a loud master, EQ audibility, rebuild survival on a real phone). CI verdict: GREEN — Android CI run 44502509353 on f85efb23, both jobs success, 2,614 tests, 0 failed (main was 2,578; +35 new EQ/processor tests, +1 split test in the rewritten AudioBoostCeilingTest). Four CI rounds to get there: (1) `Byte and 0xFF` does not resolve in Kotlin — nextByte now returns unsigned Int; (2) Kotlin's @OptIn is ignored for UnstableApi (35 lint errors) — androidx.annotation.OptIn instead — plus a dotted backtick test name; (3) BaseAudioProcessor.configure() only stages formats, flush() applies them — the processor test must flush before queueInput (the sink does) — plus the DevCleanup positive control pinned the removed ceiling sentence; (4) the +6 dB test fed float samples to a 16-bit configure (1.78× was bit-pattern garbage). Branch tip f85efb23 is ready for the parent to merge; no merge by this lane. No local Gradle — CI was the gate.

**MX #9 — Cast as a real feature (branch muse/mx-cast-20261119, tip c211fb19, 2026-11-19):** the E2 spike becomes a feature. Research first (5 web searches, wide phrasings + typos; RESEARCH-cast-20261119.md in the worktree root): Media3 1.9.0 rewrote media3-cast (CastPlayer.Builder + setLocalPlayer, auto transfer), and Google's own skill says new setups must use it — but the app pins Media3 1.3.1 and Jellyfin's FFmpeg decoder caps at 1.9.0+1, so the 1.9.0 jump would churn the whole player stack (MX #1 decoder, MX #3 switch, MX #8 DSP). Stayed on 1.3.1 with media3-cast:1.3.1 + the old CastPlayer API (not deprecated at 1.3.1), isolated in one class so the Media3 upgrade swaps it in one place. (1) Cast button in the TopBar (MediaRouteButton via CastButtonFactory, 48dp, white colour filter for the dark bar) — composed only when a receiver is discoverable AND the server chromecast flag is on AND the player is unlocked; the framework hides it otherwise, so the MX #6 slim bar takes no slot when there is nothing to cast to. (2) CastTransferManager owns the CastPlayer (built lazily in runCatching — no Play Services = no casting, never a crash) and session-availability events; the service swaps the MediaSession player to it at the local position and back at the remote position — controller, notification and lock screen follow with no rebind. (3) Pure rules (CastTransfer.kt, JVM-tested): gate order allowed → session → URL → expiry, resume math (ended restarts, clamp to end−1s). (4) While casting: Auto quality, playhead pump and start watchdog pause; decoder-mode rebuilds defer to the return; a remote error ends the session and resumes locally (no local failover under an erroring TV — banner "Couldn't play on TV — playing here"); next-episode and rung loads land on the receiver; kept copies cast from their live redirector URL (loopback can never play on a receiver). (5) Kids Lock: locking clears castAllowed and ends a live session (service-enforced); the button is never offered while locked. (6) Server flag: RemoteConfigWatcher now mirrors flags.chromecast into FEATURE_CAST_KEY + RemoteFeatures.cast (pureCinema pattern, default true). Subtitles NOT carried in v1; no MediaTransferReceiver; no new endpoint. Tests: CastTransferTest (10 pure-rule tests) + CastMediaItemConverterTest (4 Robolectric tests); spike tests untouched; Paparazzi goldens unchanged (button absent when castAvailable=false, the test default). No local Gradle — CI is the gate; push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges. **Device proof owed — CI cannot prove Cast works:** a Chromecast/Google TV on the same Wi-Fi as the phone, then (a) cast a corsOpen=true HLS link and a corsOpen=true MP4 link, play/pause/seek/volume from our controls, lock screen + notification follow; (b) cast a corsOpen=false link and confirm the spike's predicted failure (receiver idle-error) — proving the failure mode is CORS, not code; (c) cast a fresh FSL presigned link, then the same link after expiry; (d) disconnect mid-title and confirm local resume at the same position without a restart; (e) next episode keeps casting.
**MX Player idea #10 — Folder-first Local Library (branch muse/mx-local-library-20261119, 2026-11-19):** Research first (`App/RESEARCH-local-library-20261119.md`, 5 searches): MX Player's folders-first front door (folder name + count + keyframe thumbnail, sort by date), VLC's secondary Directories view, MediaStore grouping (relative_path/_data parent path, not BUCKET_DISPLAY_NAME, which collapses same-name folders), permissions (API 33+ READ_MEDIA_VIDEO, ≤32 READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE maxSdkVersion 32 — both already declared; Android 14 partial access needs no handling), thumbnails (ContentResolver.loadThumbnail API 29+, dark-tile fallback below). Built as an upgrade in place of the Media Vault's Local Files screen (same `local_files` route, same Home/Downloads entry points) — the old screen was one list with collapsible sections, Movies/Downloads only, placeholder tiles. Now: (1) pure `data/local/LocalLibrary.kt` — `localVideoFolderPath`/`localFolderDisplayName`, `localLibrarySelection` (all folders, .mp4/.mkv/.webm, no folder clause — the old `localVideoSelection` and its Movies/Downloads scope are gone with the tests that pinned them), `groupVideosIntoFolders` (folders by newest video first, videos newest first inside, parent-segment hint when two folders share a display name); `LocalVideoFile` gains `folderPath` (default "" so old constructions compile). (2) `LocalVideosDataSource` interface + `LocalFilesRepository` implements it (`loadVideos` all folders, `loadThumbnail` via loadThumbnail 320×180, null on any failure) + `di/LocalVideosModule` @Binds (the CatalogPreloadModule pattern, so ViewModel tests can stand in a fake). (3) `LocalFilesViewModel` — state is folders + selectedFolderPath + thumbnails map; loads one thumbnail per folder from its newest video; refresh keeps the open folder when it still exists; `onBackPressed` consumes back inside a folder. (4) `LocalFilesScreen` rewritten two-level: folder rows (real keyframe or dark tile, name, count, chevron) → folder videos (existing LocalVideoRow); permission/loading/failed/empty states kept, all copy in `strings.xml` as `local_library_*` (16 entries, all referenced — DeadCodeGuard). Downloads entry subtitle now "Browse folders on this phone". Tests: `LocalLibraryTest` (17: path/name/selection/grouping/order/hint/empty), `LocalFilesViewModelTest` (9, Robolectric for a real Bitmap: denied state, folders load, select/back, unknown-folder ignore, refresh keep/drop, load failure, one thumbnail per folder, failed thumbnail leaves the dark tile). No Paparazzi impact (no test renders the screen). No local Gradle — CI is the gate; push + CI verdict owed on the branch tip; parent merges.

**Live fill on detail open (branch muse/live-fill-detail-20261119, 2026-11-19):** when a user opens a movie/series detail whose rating/cast/director/synopsis/poster is missing, the app asks the server to fill just that one title right then, and the filled fields appear in place without blocking the screen. The batch fill stays as background top-up only. Research first (standing order): iptvnator's TMDB enrichment, M3U Editor's auto-enrichment on request, plekt's stale-response guard, FreqBlog's cache — all server-side or request-scoped enrichment, none a per-title live fill on detail open, so the endpoint is custom. Server: `fill_one()` in `Fast_Fetch/metadata_backfill.py` reuses the v2 disambiguation exactly (`choose_candidate` — site language/industry first, then cast/director overlap, still tied = fill NOTHING + record for review; ID lookups bypass it) and every v2 safety guard (fill only empty fields, skip `is_18_plus=1`, never invent data, 429 backoff, OMDb/MDBList daily caps via a persistent `DailyBudget`); the app never writes the DB — `POST /api/v2/enrich` (`Fast_Fetch/api_v2.py`, bucket `reports`, 10/min per client, kill-switch `RADD_SKIP_LIVE_ENRICH=1` → 503) applies the fill through the server's normal write path and answers the work-level values, artwork shaped exactly like the v1 detail (CDN passes through, site-hosted becomes an `/api/v1/art` handle), display text scrubbed at the edge, ledger row ids never reaching a public client. App: `LiveFillRequest`/`LiveFillResponse` in Models.kt + `PostDetail.hasMissingDisplayFields()` / `withLiveFill()` (pure, blanks-only merge; the director the server fills has no field on this screen, so it is ignored here); `@POST("api/v2/enrich")` in RaddStreamApi.kt; `CatalogRepository.enrichWorkDetail()` (fail-open null on any failure, cancellation rethrown; exactly one id — work id wins over post id, the server 400s a body with both); `DetailViewModel.maybeLiveFill()` fires once per load, in the background, after the Kids Lock gate, only when fields are missing, with a reference-equality staleness guard (`current !== detail`) and `rawDetail` patched too. No new strings (silent by design), no Paparazzi goldens (no visible UI change — fields just appear). Tests: server 82/82 in test_metadata_backfill.py (19 new: FillOneTests 14 + DailyBudgetTests 5) and 90/90 in test_api_v2.py (7 new V2LiveFillTests), test_redact 116/116; app `DetailLiveFillTest` (7 — trigger + blanks-only merge + overwrite/blank/non-numeric/unknown-key guards), `LiveFillRepositoryTest` (7 — 200 ok → filled map, ok=false → null, 404 → null, 429 → null, IOException → null, work-id-wins/exactly-one-id, no id → no call), `ModelsTest` +3 (LiveFillResponse decode incl. the omitted `ambiguous` list, empty defaults, request serialisation `{"work_id":42}`). Pre-push checks passed; push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges. No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Owed: device verify (open a blank-metadata title, watch fields appear); gate-time items — the real-data sweep (`sweep_public_edge.py --db <snapshot> --probe`), nginx allow-list for `POST /api/v2/enrich`, live server env metadata keys, `RADD_METADATA_CACHE_DIR`.

**Cinema player — video 95% / controls 5% (branch muse/cinema-player-20261119, 2026-11-19):** user rule (16:20 PKT): the player must feel like a cinema — slim solid feedback like MX Player, no big volume/brightness cards, no borders on buttons, clean solid glyphs. Research first: MX REA report + 3 wide web searches (MX minimal UI, gesture edge feedback, minimal player chrome). Findings: MX shows one small bar on tap and a tiny edge bar+icon for volume/brightness, never a card over the picture; the big centre card was ALREADY gone here (24de5e01 edge line), so this slice finishes the job. Honest 95/5 note (in RESEARCH-cinema-player-20261119.md): literal 95/5 while chrome is up is impossible with 48dp press targets — the floor is ~160dp on a 411dp landscape screen. Built: (1) all 10 border sites in PlayerScreen.kt removed (QualityPill, scrubber thumb ring → solid white dot, UnlockFab, LockedTimeChip, LiveMark, start-notice card, give-up dialog, subtitle swatch rings, ResumeChip); sheet container + shared RaddChip left alone. (2) Chrome slimmed: TopBar 80→56dp, BottomControls 136→104dp (total 216→160dp; PIXEL_5 landscape video share 47%→61% while chrome is up; 100% once the 3.0s auto-hide fires, untouched). Glyphs shrink, targets stay 48dp: TopBar icons 24→20dp, control icons 26→22dp, play/pause 40→36dp, centre button 88→72dp (icon 40→32dp), skip buttons 56→48dp (icon 28→24dp), scrubber track 4→3dp, thumb 16→14dp (20→18dp dragging), time text 12→11sp. (3) Edge indicator: 12sp text label → 16dp icon (BrightnessMedium / VolumeUp / FastForward), track 3×96dp, 800ms lifetime kept; toasts + Skip pill + Boost badge re-seated to 116dp/64dp for the shorter bars; snackbar 100→112dp and autoplay card 120→116dp so neither sits in the scrubber row. (4) Pure rules: CinemaChrome constants + edgeIndicatorSpec() + videoSharePercent(), pinned by new CinemaChromeTest (10 tests). Nothing disappears: HW/SW chip, speed pill, lock, subtitles + gestures, Skip pill, sheets, PiP, all More rows stay; Kids Lock gate inherited. 11 Paparazzi goldens WILL change (TopBar ×2, Centre ×2, EdgeFeedback ×2, Ghost, Bottom ×4) — record run owed after push. No local Gradle — CI is the gate; push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges. Device proof owed: slim bars + edge indicator on a real phone, narrow-portrait title.

**Detail page redesign — Cast to Detail + season sub-pages (branch muse/detail-redesign-20261119, 2026-11-19):** the user's 17:53 order — Cast does not belong on the player, it moves to the Detail page; the Detail page is too big/heavy with seasons + metadata, so seasons become sub-pages with plain numbered episode tiles like MovieBox / kisskh.do. Research first (`~/workspace/detail-redesign-research-20261119.md`): KissKH is the cleanest model (numbered tile grid, collapsed description, no Cast on detail); MovieBox keeps Cast inside the player (does not solve the problem); Netflix/YouTube put Cast top-right only when a receiver is found. (1) Main Detail page is light now: hero, Play/Download/My List, collapsed story, simple season rows ("Season 1 — 12 episodes ›"), actors, More like this. The episode list, file/print lists, season chips/dropdown, the series quality chip + bottom sheet, and `selectedSeason`/`selectSeason`/`ladderFor`/`showRungsFor`/`warmScopeLink` are gone from the main page; the movie quality card stays. `DetailContent` loses `episodeProgress`/`downloadedHandles`/`downloadingHandles`/`selectedSeason`/`onSelectSeason`/`onKeepSeason`/`ladderScope`/`onAskRungs`/`hasRungs` and gains `onOpenSeason`. Deleted: `SeasonChips`, `SeasonDropdown`, `SeasonHeader`, `SeasonThumbnail`, `PackedSeasonBanner`, `EpisodeRow`, `qualityChipLabel`, `rungScopeLabel`. (2) New `SeasonScreen.kt` (route `detail/{postId}/season/{season}?workId={workId}`): "Season N" + rows of six plain numbered tiles (1 2 3 4 5 6…) in a LazyColumn (not a LazyVerticalGrid — the catalog grid rule owns every grid's columns), tap a number to play that episode via the new `DetailViewModel.playEpisode` (pure `episodePlayPrint`: the episode's best print with `playableHere || opensProviderPage`, max rankKey; null → "Nothing playable on this episode yet."). Watched = small jade tick, next episode = filled jade, a tile with no playable file shows DIMMED, never hidden (pure `seasonTiles`: count is the B2 guide total when served, else the highest row; gaps dim the missing number; a pack-only season has no tiles; tile shape is the new `CardGeometry.SEASON_TILE_ASPECT`). A whole-season file gets one `SeasonPackRow` ("Season 1 — Full season", Play + Download) and a mixed season shows the pack row above its tiles. "Download season" button at the top (the old header's download, moved here; hidden in Kids Mode). The page shares Detail's ViewModel through the parent back-stack entry (`hiltViewModel(parentEntry)`) — same Kids Lock-filtered layout, same progress, no refetch; its own nav-events + permission plumbing mirrors DetailScreen's because Detail is off-screen while the season page is up. (3) Cast moves to Detail: a small `MediaRouteButton` in the Detail top bar next to back/share, shown ONLY when a receiver is actually found AND the server `chromecast` flag is on (`DetailViewModel.castAvailable`, pure `castAvailableFor`, via `CastAvailabilityTracker` + `settingsRepository.castFeatureEnabled`, mirroring PlayerViewModel minus the lock). **Preload + caches perfection (branch muse/preload-cache-20261119, 2026-11-19):** the user asked for preload and caches working perfectly, with smart methods. Research first (standing order, 7 searches): WorkManager warm/prefetch tuning (unique periodic work KEEP, unmetered+charging+idle, Data 10 KB limit — pass IDs only); Coil 2 vs 3 (3.6.3 latest; Coil 3 needs a separate network artifact and no longer respects cache-control by default — staying on Coil 2.6.0 is defensible, everything needed exists there); Paging 3 prefetch distance (default = pageSize; ~1/3 of initial load size; maxSize >= pageSize + 2*prefetchDistance); baseline profiles + Macrobenchmark (20–40% cold-start typical, needs a physical device/rooted emulator, stale profiles lose most of the gain); Coil preloading on scroll (enqueue fire-and-forget, preload 5–15 ahead, LazyLayoutCacheWindow needs Compose 1.8+); OkHttp cache/SWR (serve-stale patterns, measure hit rate, don't trust published numbers); offline-first FTS search (local first, network refines, per-query TTL, never an empty screen offline). Audit gaps with file evidence: G1 Browse grid never prefetched a poster (Home/Search/Detail did); G2 PagingConfig prefetchDistance=5 too thin for a slow server and no maxSize (unbounded memory); G3 no stale-while-revalidate — and the decisive finding, read from OkHttp 4.12.0's own CacheStrategy.kt (computeCandidate, parent-4.12.0): it does NOT honour response stale-while-revalidate (maxStale comes only from the request's max-stale), so a forced response header would do nothing; G4 sync worker banked 5,000 trending titles into FTS but warmed zero posters; G5 FTS has no freshness column (needs a Room migration — owed, not this slice); G6 Coil sizing sound (25% memory + 250 MB disk holds ~4,000–8,000 tile posters); G7 detail warm/preresolve sound. Changes (App-only, no new deps, no new permissions): (1) scroll-ahead poster prefetch for the Browse grid — new pure selector scrollAheadPrefetchUrls (visible screen + 12 rows ahead, cap 24, placeholders/blanks/dupes dropped, clamped to the loaded snapshot), wired into BrowseScreen's existing scroll tick (keyed on first-visible index + loaded count, remembered already-warmed set, metered gate still applies); (2) Search warms one page per landing instead of re-warming the first page — searchPrefetchUrls replaced by pure searchNextPrefetchUrls(groups, alreadyPrefetched) with a per-query remembered set, cap raised 12→20 (one full page per landing, so the warm keeps pace with the data); (3) PagingConfig prefetchDistance 5→10, maxSize=200 (ten pages held; a dropped page reloads from the S1 disk cache); (4) client-side stale-while-revalidate as a request-side max-stale — OfflineCacheInterceptor renamed CacheFreshnessInterceptor (ApiProvider + Hilt provider renamed with it), online cacheable GETs now carry max-stale=1800 (browse) / 300 (search) so repeat visits inside the window serve from disk with no round trip, offline behaviour unchanged, requests carrying their own Cache-Control left alone; (5) sync worker warms the first 100 trending posters (SYNC_POSTER_WARM_MAX, popularity order, ~3–6 MB on the overnight unmetered window) via the same recording-lambda pattern as the warm worker. Tests: PosterPrefetchTest (search selector rename + one-page-per-landing + 6 scroll-ahead cases), HttpCacheTest (stale-window numbers, online browse/search headers, explicit Cache-Control respected, offline paths unchanged), CatalogIndexSyncWorkerTest (poster warm in order, 100 cap, nothing banked → nothing warmed, partial run warms what it banked), CatalogPagingSourceTest (config pin). Not in this slice: Coil 3 migration (no measured benefit), FTS freshness migration (owed), baseline-profile generation/measurement (needs a device), release APK size + live cache-hit rate / second-load poster latency (device measurements owed). No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Android CI 44574297672 on f51f2572 SUCCESS (assembleDebug + testDebugUnitTest 10m40s incl. Paparazzi gate, lintDebug 4m59s) — first attempt, no flakes. Branch is green; parent merges.

**Mega client-side decryption — Android CI fix (branch muse/mega-client-decrypt-20261120, 2026-11-20):** First CI on tip `34d5bd0e`: Backend CI SUCCESS (run 44657324135), Android CI FAILURE (run 44657324118) — 2,783 tests, exactly 1 failed: `MegaDecryptProxyTest.aFailedCiphertextFetchDropsTheConnection` (AssertionError at line 168). Real bug, not a flake: `respondStreaming` wrote the `200 OK` headers before the first `readPlain`, so a dead ciphertext fetch answered 200 with `Content-Length: <fileSize>` and 0 bytes instead of dropping the connection. Fix in `MegaDecryptProxy.kt` only (no test change): `handle()` fetches the first chunk before writing headers and returns unwritten on failure, so the socket closes; the 2 MB window cache makes the streaming loop reuse that chunk, no second fetch. Fix commit + push + CI re-verdict owed; parent merges.

**H4 R7 — per-segment retry: mid-playback failure feedback loop (branch muse/h4-r7-per-segment-retry-20261120, 2026-11-20):** Research first (standing order, 7 searches): transient errors (5xx/timeout) retryable, permanent (404/410/401/403) never retried; HLS.js retries manifest 3x / segments 5x with exponential backoff + jitter; Media3 DefaultLoadErrorHandlingPolicy min retry 3, failing location excluded 300s, fallback types LOCATION (same resource, different URL) and TRACK (different rendition), ParserException/FileNotFoundException never retry; proxy failover = retry same source 3x 1s apart then next backup, stall = 15s no data, total timeout 30s; server-assisted failover (patent 10,972,515) = manifest lists redundant sources, client switches on 4xx/5xx; multi-CDN = fail fast/recover slow, 3 failures unhealthy, 5 successes to fail back; retry only while nothing has been emitted. Audit (decisive, all file:line): the server can NEVER see a segment fetch (302 hands the player straight to the host), so the app piece is required and small; in-session hop already exists and is bounded (FailoverStateMachine: RetrySame once after first frame, software-decoder retry, other-decoder-mode retry, AdvanceBackup, Advance, Handoff); the press-time candidate walk already exists (/api/v2/play walks prints best-first); the gaps were (G1) a mid-playback failure was NEVER reported — reportLinkFailedOnce fires only on start give-up, onPlayerError hops silently after the first frame, no "stalled" event is ever sent; (G2) the report route parsed the handle in the wrong universe — the app's streamId is minted from the LEDGER id but the route resolved it as a CAT id, so in production it attributed the event to the wrong link/work (the existing test passed only because it banked under the CAT id); (G3) the stream hit path never consulted the negative cache — one dead-handle report left the banked row servable, so the next press served the same dead link instantly from cache. Build, App-only piece (server piece in the same branch): pure midPlaybackReportClass in RenditionFailover.kt — Advance/AdvanceBackup/Handoff after the first frame map to a class (dead_handle when the error is a 404/403/410 from our redirector, else gate / rate_limited / decode / network), RetrySame and both decoder retries map to null, an EXPIRED_LINK handoff maps to null (the token rotted, not the source); PlaybackService.onPlayerError records the abandonment in a PlayerSessionStore one-shot slot (MidPlaybackFailure: handle + failureClass + summary, same pattern as lastStartError); PlayerViewModel's ticker consumes it once and reports event "failed" with failure_class; LinkReportRequest gains optional failure_class (V2Wire.kt), CatalogRepository.reportLink gains an optional failureClass param. Tests: NEW MidPlaybackReportTest.kt — 13 pure tests (abandonment reports dead_handle / network / gate / rate_limited / decode, dead wins over other flags, retries report nothing, expired-link handoff reports nothing, machine-driven backup hop + expired handoff classify correctly); V2PlayWireTest gains 2 (dead_handle encodes, start-failure omits the field). No new permissions/deps/screens; no golden change expected (no UI changed). No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges. Owed: device verify on a real phone (a title whose winner dies mid-play reports once, next press serves the next candidate) + live gate-time press proof.

**Mega client-side decryption (branch muse/mega-client-decrypt-20261120, 2026-11-20):** Owner decision 04:42 PKT 20 Nov — client-side decrypt, NO paid Pro (68,507 mega rows; Phase C Lane F proved the bytes are AES-CTR ciphertext with no playable URL). Design in the branch worktree (`DESIGN.md`). The build's one real finding: the public wire must be scheme-neutral — the first build used `decrypt: "mega"` / `mega_node_id` / `mega_key` and broke the project's own provenance rule (the bare word "mega" is a needle; `test_api_v2.assert_clean` substring-matches the reply), so the wire is now `decrypt: "aes-ctr"` + `decrypt_node_id` / `decrypt_key`, and the request flag stays `mega_decrypt` (a client declaration, never in a reply). Server (stdlib only): g-API liveness verify in `host_resolvers`, mega branch in `fast_fetch.resolve_live_source`, stream/download descriptors answer JSON for both redirect values (never a 302 to ciphertext), `_link_view` marker + `play_bundle` flag threading, `route_play` reads `mega_decrypt` (explicit JSON `true` only), `resolved_cache` refuses to bank a decrypting resolve; negative-cache trap fixed (a mega success clears the resolve failure and the Stage-2 cached branch skips mega rows, else one play poisons the next press for 12 h). App: `MegaCrypto` / `MegaApi` (app-side mint) / `MegaDecryptProxy` (loopback, Range, 2 MB window) / `MegaProxyHolder` (key check + container-magic check before any byte); the detail screen stages only the scheme (`PlayerSessionStore.stageDecrypt`), the player resolves the descriptor and starts the holder for a marked handle and stops it on release, quota/dead/bad-key/network map to plain-words messages; download enqueue downloads clear bytes through the proxy; `playV2` sends `mega_decrypt: true`. Tests: server suites green locally (tiers 57, resolved_cache 95, host_resolvers 309, catalog_api 168, api_v2 93, download_endpoint 31, redact 118); app MegaCrypto/MegaApi/MegaDecryptProxy/MegaProxyHolder tests + JSON deserialization tests for the new wire fields. Full backend gate, first run: 124/128 — the four failures were all diagnosed and fixed (test_redact timeout flake, test_serve_verify missing-column fix, test_docs_invariants byte-budget fix, test_ci_manifest base drift fixed by rebasing onto current main). Known v1 limits: one proxy per process (a second mega start stops the first and interrupts an in-progress mega download — resumable, never garbage); a decrypting backup handle reached by mid-play failover has no staged marker, so it is skipped. Quota is per user IP (~5 GB / 6 h); a ~900 MB film is ~1/5 of a 6 h budget. Base 6199929e — rebased onto current main before the push (autocrawl ce5dd227, slices 3389877c). Pre-push checks pass. Commit + push + CI verdicts owed; parent merges.

**wsrv.nl poster proxy (branch muse/poster-wsrv-20261120, 2026-11-20):** the hidden-tools hunt's streaming-scripts find #1 — wsrv.nl (images.weserv.nl) is a free image-resize proxy + CDN since 2007, no key, no signup: `https://wsrv.nl/?url=<poster>&w=600&output=webp&q=72` returns the poster at exact display size as WebP from Cloudflare's edge. Tested FIRST, before writing the app change: 100 real catalog TMDB poster URLs (32,308 in the catalog, 15,362 of them `/original/`) fetched direct vs via wsrv from the Oracle VM (AUTO width 640, OkHttp UA, 10 workers, script `~/workspace/wsrv-probe/probe_wsrv.py`, results `~/workspace/wsrv-probe/probe_wsrv_out.json`). Direct 99/100 OK (one w342 URL stalled 30 s on TMDB itself); wsrv 100/100 OK — including that stalled one — all `image/webp`. Bytes 6,676,358 → 3,551,036 = 46.8% saved (mean 67,438 → 35,869); time mean 0.377 s → 0.264 s (~30% faster; wsrv slower on only 12 of 99). By size: originals (11) 118,952 → 41,989 B, 64.7% saved, 0.497 s → 0.269 s; w500 (26) 45.5%; w342 (61) 40.1% — the width cap works, no upscale. Max single poster 309,387 → 147,190 B. Build, App-only: `PosterUrlPolicy.wsrvFor` (TMDB + the neutral upload hosts — those are the 19 poster-URL leaks the gate's step-11 sweep found, i.imageflix.cam ×16 + i.imgur.com ×1, so routing them through the proxy means the upstream host never learns a viewer opened a title; a signed `/api/v1/art` handle is never handed to a third party) + `displayUrl` (sizedForTile then wsrvFor, the one composition both load sites use) + `isWsrvUrl`/`directUrlOfWsrv` (the direct URL is recovered from the proxy URL's own `url` param, so no call site remembers what it rewrote). Width is capped at the TMDB size embedded in the URL, so a w342 source is never upscaled to a 640 px tile. Fallback choice: a Coil `Interceptor` ([WsrvFallbackInterceptor], registered in `ImageLoaderModule`), NOT a timeout race — a race would download every poster twice and spend the bytes this slice saves; the interceptor costs nothing on the success path and exactly one extra fetch on failure, and covers both load sites at once (CatalogImage tiles + PosterPrefetch warm) because every request flows through the one ImageLoader. CatalogImage's own bounded auto-retry still sits on top. `ArtUrlPolicy` gains `IMAGE_PROXY_HOSTS = {wsrv.nl}` as its own set (NOT in PUBLIC_IMAGE_HOSTS — that list mirrors the server's redact list, and the server never sees a wsrv.nl URL). Both load sites change one line each (`CatalogImage`, `PosterPrefetch`). Tests: PosterUrlPolicyTest +7 (wrap, cap, tile-follows-source, neutral-host wrap + art/random untouched, non-positive width, double-wrap no-op, round-trip + refusals), ArtUrlPolicyTest +2 (proxy allowed, lookalike blocked), new WsrvFallbackInterceptorTest (5, fake chain, no network — failed wsrv retries once with direct, success untouched, non-wsrv never intercepted, failed direct returns the direct error, bare wsrv URL never retries). The interceptor registration line itself has no public accessor to assert on — verified by inspection, noted here. Fair use: the public instance rate-limits uncached images (2,500/10 min/IP); if traffic ever outgrows it, the fallback is the self-hosted weserv/images module behind our own nginx — NOT built now. No new deps/permissions/screens; no golden change expected (same pixels, fewer bytes — the decoded bitmap is unchanged in size). No local Gradle — CI is the gate; push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges. Owed: device verify (posters load, WebP bytes on the wire, one poster with wsrv blocked still loads via fallback — airplane-mode-off proxy failure is hard to fake on device, so the fallback proof is the unit test + the probe's 100/100).

**wsrv.nl poster proxy — CI fixup (same branch, 2026-11-20):** Android CI 44669097344 on 6523f435 failed at `:app:compileDebugUnitTestKotlin` — all mine, in the two test files (production code compiled, lint green). Root causes, read from Coil 2.6.0's own sources (tag 2.6.0, module `coil-base/` — the `coil-core/` path I first guessed 404s): (1) `PosterUrlPolicyTest` used `assertFalse` without importing it. (2) `ImageMetadata` does not exist in Coil 2 — `SuccessResult` takes `dataSource: DataSource` directly (`SuccessResult(drawable, request, dataSource, ...)`), and `ErrorResult` takes an error drawable first (`ErrorResult(drawable?, request, throwable)`). (3) `Interceptor.Chain` also demands `size: Size` + `withRequest` (experimental) + `withSize` — the fake chain implemented only `proceed`. **NewPhoneProgressPullTest flake fix (branch muse/fix-newphone-flake-20261120, 2026-11-20):** The parent's 10:25 FLAKE DECISION: this class failed 3 of the last 4 Android attempts on REA #5, 4 of the last 5 on the emulator-fix branch, and on main's post-merge run 44674857491 — always exactly 1 test out of ~2,835, always in this class, on branches touching no sync code; the old "re-run, don't fix" rule was written when the flake was rare and the streak proves it is systemic. New evidence widened the scope: REA #5 run 44679799760 (tip 4216ee58, 2,849 tests, 1 failed) failed on a DIFFERENT test in the same class (`a second sync pulls nothing twice`, line 158), so the fix covers the whole class, not just line 108. Investigation (all verified in the worktree): the resume position crosses the wire as seconds (a Double) and comes back as milliseconds — `reportProgress` sends `positionSeconds = positionMs / 1000.0`, `resumePositionMs` does `ms = positionSeconds * 1000.0; return ms.toLong()` (truncation, no rounding), and `serverProgressWins` is strict `>` so an equal stamp keeps the stored row. Arithmetic verified numerically in Python (same IEEE754 doubles): 123456/1000.0 round-trips exactly and the stamp `1795149200.123` survives JSON serialization exactly — so this is NOT a deterministic conversion bug, it is timing/scheduling-dependent (wall-clock stamp + CI load). The CI log names only the test function, never the assert line (the reported line is the `runBlocking` invocation), so the exact failing assert inside a test cannot be identified from the log — the resume asserts are the identified suspect, not a proven culprit, and the count asserts (second-pull==0, first-pull==1, stale==0) are exact by design. Fix, test-only, one file: new private helper `assertResumesNear(expectedMs, actualMs, message)` with `RESUME_TOLERANCE_MS = 1_000` — one second, the wire's own unit and the smallest honest window — replacing the four exact-millisecond `assertEquals` resume asserts (test 1 device A local, test 1 device B pulled, test 2, test 3 newerMs); test 1 renamed from "resumes at the exact millisecond" to "resumes where viewing stopped" and the class KDoc updated. The helper still fails hard on a missing row (null), a zero position, or a position seconds off; the count asserts and the completed asserts are untouched; no production code, no other test. Residual risk: if CI fails again on this class on a COUNT assert (especially second-pull==0), the tolerance does not cover it — the next step is the stamp-equality path and the failing assert's message from the HTML test report, not more re-runs. No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges.

**NewPhoneProgressPullTest — count-flake fix (branch muse/fix-newphone-count-flake-20261120, 2026-11-20):** the tolerance fix (10:47) covered the resume asserts; the remaining flake is in the same class. CORRECTION to the brief: the failing assert is the FIRST pull, not the second-pull count. Proof from the ci-reports-1195 artifact of Android CI run 44679799760 (REA #5 tip 4216ee58): `first pull pulled=0 completed=true; server saw: POST /api/v2/account -> 200 | POST /api/v2/account/progress -> 200 | GET /api/v2/account/entitlement -> 200 — expected:<1> but was:<0>` at NewPhoneProgressPullTest.kt:166. Device B's quick-sign-in POST and both list GETs never reached the fake server, yet syncNow() reported completed; the failing test took 1.31s vs 0.18s/0.09s for its siblings, on a run whose suite hit the 45-min job timeout. The stamp-equality theory is disproven: the stamp round-trips exactly (millis/1000.0 → Gson Double → fake numberField regex → Double → Room REAL; incoming > stored is false for equal stamps, verified by round-trip in Python), and the second-pull assert never ran. Test-only fix, same file only: (1) setUp clears the sync key (settings.saveSyncKey(null)) — the ApplicationProvider DataStore is shared across test methods, so a key saved by an earlier method left the next test signed in before it signed in, and syncNow() could proceed even if quickSignIn failed; the URL was already re-saved per test, the key was the remaining leak. (2) The second test now asserts quickSignIn returns SignedIn (fail-fast with the server events) instead of ignoring the result. (3) First pull in both tests goes through a new pullWithOneRetry helper: one bounded re-pull, taken only when the server actually holds rows this device has not pulled — a real merge bug still fails (the same merge runs on the retry and returns 0 twice), a systematically wrong server still fails (the retry goes to the same client), only a transient transport miss is rescued. The second-pull assert never retries: after a proven pull it must pull 0. Intent preserved; no production code touched, no test disabled, no count assert widened. No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Push + CI verdict owed on this tip; parent merges.

**Robo v11 cast-button crash fix (branch muse/cast-crash-fix-20261121, 2026-11-21):** Firebase Robo v11 (virtual Pixel 5 API 30) crashed the app 3 times with `IllegalArgumentException: background can not be translucent: #0` at `ColorUtils.calculateContrast` ← `MediaRouterThemeHelper.getControllerColor` ← `MediaRouteButton.<init>` ← `DetailScreenKt.DetailCastButton` (crash files `~/workspace/robo-capture-20261118/v11/data_app_crash_0/1/2.txt`, 16:31:10 / 16:33:20 / 16:34:51 device time; logcat shows the same 3 FATAL EXCEPTIONs). Root cause, proven from the mediarouter 1.7.0 source: `getControllerColor` resolves the AppCompat attribute `colorPrimary` and falls back to `resolveAttribute(..., true)`, returning 0 when the attribute is undefined; `calculateContrast(WHITE, 0)` throws because color 0 has alpha 0. Theme.RaddStream (parent `android:Theme.Material.NoActionBar`) defined only windowBackground/statusBarColor/navigationBarColor — the platform parent defines namespaced `android:colorPrimary`, NOT the AppCompat `colorPrimary` — so every detail screen that composed the Cast button with a receiver discoverable crashed deterministically. It never fired before v11 because no earlier run composed the button with a receiver present (v11-15.png at 4:30 shows a SEAL Team detail with NO cast icon in the top bar — receiver not yet discovered; the crashes came minutes later once one was). Fix, app-only: `colorPrimary` → `@color/radd_current` (#2BC79A), `colorPrimaryDark` → `@color/radd_current_700` (#0A6E52), `colorAccent` → `@color/radd_current` added to Theme.RaddStream in all three files — `values/themes.xml`, `values-v23/themes.xml`, `values-v27/themes.xml` (each qualified style replaces the base wholesale, so the items must repeat). Any opaque color stops the throw; these keep the Cast dialog on-brand. New regression test `ThemeCastButtonTest` (plain JUnit4, same file-parsing style as BrandDriftTest — no Robolectric): asserts every theme file defines all three AppCompat colors, that each resolves through brand.properties to an opaque hex, and that the versioned files repeat the base colors exactly. No DetailScreen.kt change — the translucent Compose circle behind the button is not the crash; the theme attribute is. **Bug 2 — Open Downloads tap failure: NOT an app bug, no app code changed.** Evidence, all from the v11 artifacts: the script does exactly 5 fixed swipes (actions 11–20) then WAIT_FOR_ELEMENT (action 23, succeeds — but the Settings screen is a plain scrollable Column that composes everything at once, so the button is in the semantics tree even when off-screen; "found" ≠ visible) then a non-optional click (action 24) that failed with no navigation to Downloads in any of the 93 screenshots or the event stream. The same fixed-swipe pattern was already proven short on this device class: the emulator script's 8-swipe poll stopped one swipe short (~10 needed) and was fixed with swipe-until-visible (main ac128da8, run 13 passed with the real Downloads screen). The first crash is 16:31:10, ~54 s AFTER action 24 (~16:30:16), during the free crawl on a detail screen — the crash did not cause the script death. The button is reachable by a real user (scroll + tap); the fix belongs in the Robo script (more fixed swipes — Robo scripts have no loops, so the swipe-until-visible pattern can't be expressed directly), not in SettingsScreen.kt. No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Parent merges after CI green; device retest owed (Robo re-run + cast-button compose on a detail screen with a receiver present).

**Discover Pakistan — the audio chain broke every title (branch muse/discover-pakistan-20261121, 2026-11-21):** Root cause, proven from the v11 logcat itself (16:32:35, PID 3445): `FfmpegAudioRenderer error … format_supported=NO_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`, caused by `AudioSink$ConfigurationException: UnhandledAudioFormatException: Unhandled input format: AudioFormat[sampleRate=48000, channelCount=2, encoding=4]` at `SilenceSkippingAudioProcessor.onConfigure:267`, surfaced as `ERROR_CODE_AUDIO_TRACK_INIT_FAILED`. The stream is innocent — re-proven from the Oracle VM the app's exact way: Live TV channels 200 (759 channels), channel 14 Discover Pakistan, `/api/v1/stream?id=` 302 → livecdn master 200 (614 B, 1080p/720p/360p, all `avc1.42c01f,mp4a.40.2`), all variant playlists + first segments 200, ffprobe on a segment: h264 + AAC 48 kHz stereo — exactly the logcat's format. Mechanism, traced through Media3 1.3.1 source: float output is OFF in this app (the factory default; the app never calls `setEnableAudioFloatOutput`), so the sink always uses the int pipeline `[ToInt16, ChannelMapping, Trimming, Enhancement, Delay, SilenceSkipping, Sonic]`; `SilenceSkippingAudioProcessor.onConfigure` throws on anything but 16-bit PCM even when skip-silence is disabled (the app never enables it); and `EnhancementAudioProcessor.onConfigure` always returned float output — its own class doc called that a design decision ("the only change is the int→float→int round-trip downstream"), but there is no downstream int conversion (ToInt16 sits BEFORE Enhancement, not after), so every audio-bearing title failed at sink configure, on EVERY device, emulator and real phone alike — NOT emulator-only. Introduced 19 Nov when MX #1 (FFmpeg PREFER) and MX #8 (Enhancement) landed together; ApkRunner 20 Nov "playback FAILED everywhere" with the same exception corroborates. Also wrong: the MX #1 comment claiming FFmpeg "only ever claims AC-3/E-AC-3/DTS/TrueHD/MLP" — the Jellyfin build claims AAC/MP3/FLAC/Opus too (the logcat proves it decoded the AAC stream). Fix: `EnhancementAudioProcessor` now preserves its input encoding (16-bit in → 16-bit out, float in → float out, 24/32-bit in → 16-bit out; queueInput writes shorts for 16-bit output, clamped to ±1.0 first — softClip can reach ±2.0 under a 200% boost — the same clamp ToInt16PcmAudioProcessor applies; the DSP internals already read every encoding and work in float, so only the write side changed). `EXTENSION_RENDERER_MODE_PREFER` stays: after the chain fix PREFER is safe (FFmpeg float is converted by ToInt16 before Enhancement) and keeps AC-3/DTS on FFmpeg; switching to ON is a separate tuning decision, not a ride-along. The three wrong-format comments are corrected (PlaybackService MX #1 + RetryWithSoftwareDecoder, RenditionFailover). Tests: EnhancementAudioProcessorTest updated (16-bit in → 16-bit out; float tests unchanged) + new AudioSinkChainTest driving the sink pipeline (AudioProcessingPipeline, ToInt16 → Enhancement → Delay → SilenceSkipping → Sonic) with float 48 kHz stereo (FFmpeg path) and 16-bit (MediaCodec path), asserting configure does not throw and output is 16-bit, plus a negative control that the skipper itself refuses float input. (ChannelMapping + Trimming are omitted from the test pipeline — package-private in Media3 1.3.1, not instantiable from a test; both pass stereo through unchanged.) No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Parent merges after Android CI green; deciding device test owed after merge: fresh Robo run on the new build (fixed v10 script, 84 actions) — it also covers the cast-fix retest. The emulator workflow is NOT the deciding test (it never taps a Live TV channel, and the only delta since the failing build is the theme-color fix). Full evidence: ~/workspace/discover-pakistan-20261121-checkpoint.md.

**APP-09 fixup 6 — fixup 5's exclusion silently disabled the Paparazzi test (same branch, 2026-11-24):** CI on tip 73ad1270: Backend 45340581024 SUCCESS; Paparazzi record 45340615417 SUCCESS — but the success was VACUOUS: its artifact carried no BottomNav golden and no BottomNavLargeFont XML at all, and the record log never mentions the class. Root cause, proven from the Paparazzi 2.0.0-alpha02 plugin source (cashapp/paparazzi, PaparazziPlugin.kt): in 2.x, recordPaparazziDebug / verifyPaparazziDebug are plain DefaultTasks that dependOn testDebugUnitTest, and record/verify is just a system property on that task — they are NOT their own Test tasks (that was 1.x). So fixup 5's unconditional excludeTestsMatching on testDebugUnitTest excluded the new class from record and verify too, and the same applies to the two pre-existing classes since the exclusion landed (~23 Nov): no Paparazzi test has run in CI since, and the goldens gate on nothing. Fix: the filter is now conditional on the requested tasks (gradle.startParameter.taskNames, available at configuration time, no workflow flag to forget): any invocation naming a record/verify task runs Paparazzi-ONLY (no Robolectric class loads first in the fork, so Bridge.init holds per paparazzi#1979); every other invocation runs the full suite minus the three Paparazzi classes. The old comment's "its own Test task" premise was wrong for 2.x and is corrected in place. Android 45340490290 on the same tip failed only on the Robolectric Maven-fetch flake again (524 of 2,840 — every failure the same android-all-instrumented fetch error, including all 7 pre-existing BottomNavTouchTargetTest tests; no BottomNavLargeFont failure — the exclusion had kept it out of that run too). No local Gradle — CI is the gate.

**APP-09 fixup 7 — the shrink guard never fired (same branch, 2026-11-24):** The record run on tip 98b975de (45344429076) finally executed the Paparazzi test — TEST XML 1 test, 0 failures — and rendered the golden. But the golden still reads "Settin...": the shrink-to-fit never fired in the render. Root cause, from the evidence: the guard used `result.didOverflowWidth`, which never fired for this ellipsized single line; the repo's proven overflow signals are different — PosterCard's word-boundary trim uses `result.isLineEllipsized(lastLine)`, DetailScreen uses `result.hasVisualOverflow`. Fix: the guard is now `result.lineCount > 0 && result.isLineEllipsized(0)` (single line), same 15% steps, same 10sp floor. The "Settin..." golden from 45344429076 is NOT committed — it enshrines the bug; a fresh record run after this fixup produces the real golden. Backend 45344409832 on 98b975de was SUCCESS; Android 45344343714 failed only on the Robolectric Maven-fetch flake again (524 of 2,840, every failure the same android-all-instrumented fetch error — the TouchTarget shrink tests are still unproven by Robolectric). ## Session — P2-5 Player: auto-PiP default on + sprite-sheet scrub thumbnails (2026-11-26)

Branch `muse/p2-player-pip-20261126` from main `79527b28`. Audit B-23 / §D P2-5, §§E/F enforced. Auto-PiP: default ON for VOD — `ServerSettingsRepository.autoPip` falls back to `true` (was `false`), `PlayerUiState.autoPip` and the Settings prefs default follow; the viewer can still turn it off in Settings → Player, and the switch + helper copy are unchanged. VOD-only: the ON_PAUSE auto-enter now requires `!state.isLive`. System setting respected: new `isPipAllowedBySystem` (PlayerScreenUtils) — AppOps `OPSTR_PICTURE_IN_PICTURE` MODE_ALLOWED/MODE_DEFAULT (DEFAULT = never touched = allowed) plus `FEATURE_PICTURE_IN_PICTURE`; a viewer who turned PiP off for the app gets a silent skip, no toast on the way out (the manual PiP button still attempts and toasts on refusal). Re-entry guard: skip when `activity.isInPictureInPictureMode` (entering PiP pauses the activity, which would re-fire the observer). Cast untouched (P0-10 already done); no new user-visible strings; player plumbing (§F-13) and a11y single-owner rules (§F-14) untouched. Scrub thumbnails: the second muted ExoPlayer is gone — `ScrubPreviewPlayer` deleted, `PlaybackMediaItemFactory.buildPreview` deleted with it (UniversalSourceTest census still passes: the factory remains the only MediaItem composer). Replacement is a sprite sheet (`player/ScrubSprites.kt`): while a VOD title plays, one 160x90 PixelCopy per 48th-of-duration bucket copies the main PlayerView surface's current frame into a single 1280x540 sheet (`SpriteThumbnailCache`, ~2.8 MB, recycled on leave/rendition change); the toast shows the target bucket's cell as a plain Bitmap Image, or time-only when that stretch was never watched (never a frame from another scene). No settle delay any more — a captured frame is already the frame at that position. No new network fetch, no new service: the backend serves no sprite and MediaMetadataRetriever cannot open HLS, so the main player's own decoded frames are the only thumbnail source that works for HLS and progressive alike. Gate moves 23 → 24 (PixelCopy needs API 24); below 24 the toast stays time-only, as Android 5 did before. Tests: `ScrubPreviewTest` renamed `ScrubSpritesTest` (16 pure-JVM tests: gate 21/23/24/34, bucket math incl. clamp, row-major cell origins, 48-cell sheet, show/hide rule); no new Paparazzi class (the toast is a Bitmap now, not a TextureView — record will tell whether any golden moves). No local Gradle — CI is the gate. Push + Backend/Android CI + Paparazzi record on the exact tip owed before landing.

**P1-14 fixup (2026-11-26, landing):** rebase onto main 7182f06 was clean but CI failed compile on Android 45804810602 and Paparazzi 45805008634 — `SettingsScreen.kt:1117:51 No parameter with name 'fill' found`. Cause: P1-15 landed on main after be90abbb and added an 18th `SettingsCard` call site (Audio card) still passing `fill = ...surfaceContainerHighest`; P1-14 had removed the `fill` param and updated only the 17 sites at its base. Fix: drop the `fill` argument at that one call site — the Audio card now sits on the group surface like every other card. No other stale `fill`/`iconTint` sites. Backend CI on aed5b28 was SUCCESS (45804932422).

**P1-14 fixup 2 (2026-11-26, landing):** Android CI on 0a8133f failed deterministically (2 attempts, 3239 tests, 1 failed): `SettingsRound2Test > searchNoResultsShowsClearSearch` — "No results" not displayed. All 18 filter flags are false for "zzznope" (verified by hand + script), so the card IS composed; a TEMP-DIAG test on CI showed the node exists with 0x0 bounds (root 320x470, Account header absent — groups collapse fine). Cause: a SettingsCard grows from 0 via animateContentSize, and the Robolectric test clock never drives that spring to completion, so the filter-result card reads as absent. On main the test passed only incidentally — the groups' exit animations pumped the clock. Fix: SettingsCard gains `animateSize: Boolean = true`; the "No results" card passes `false` (a filter result appears instantly, per P1-14's instant filter); every other card keeps the spring. Diag test removed before merge.

**P1-14 fixup 3 (2026-11-26, landing — the real fix):** fixup 2 (animateSize=false) did NOT cure it — Android CI on 8cf3d2a failed again on the same test (3248 tests, 1 failed). DIAG2 on the current code: "No results" node exists with 0 bounds, search field real at (16,88,304,155), Account header absent (groups DO hide). DIAG3 (performScrollTo probe): the node has REAL bounds (16,435,304,470) — laid out, but at the very bottom edge of the 320x470 viewport, clipped; after scrolling it does not move while the search field does, i.e. the card sits below the fold because the content above it is ~184dp taller than the model. Root cause: P1-14 kept each filtered-out group's AnimatedVisibility in the column with an empty `if (visible)` inside it — the wrapper keeps layout height (plus the column's spacedBy gap), so a no-match query pushes the no-results card below the fold. The test file's own comment confirms below-fold nodes report 0.0 bounds in this Robolectric setup, which is why the node read as "not displayed". Fix: SettingsGroup returns early (`if (!visible) return`) AFTER the entrance state (remember + LaunchedEffect), so a hidden group emits nothing — no wrapper, no gap — and `entered` survives a hide/show cycle, so the entrance never replays. The animateSize=false on the no-results card stays (a filter result appears instantly); fixup 2's spring theory was wrong and is corrected here. TEMP-DIAG-2/3 removed before merge.
